Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$
([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}$, $\mu$, $\chi_k$ and the
spaces $H^s(\mathbb T^3_{2\pi};\mathbb R^m)$ be as in
[[def-gr-periodic-torus-and-sobolev-spaces]] ($m\ge1$).

**(a) Mode sets.** For $N\ge0$ put
$\Lambda_N:=\{k\in\mathbb Z^3:|k|\le N\}$ with $|k|$ the Euclidean norm, and
$$X_N:=\Bigl\{\sum_{k\in\Lambda_N}a_k\chi_k:\ a_k\in\mathbb C^m,\ a_{-k}=\overline{a_k}\Bigr\}\subseteq C^\infty(\mathbb T^3_{2\pi};\mathbb R^m),$$
the **Galerkin space of modes up to $N$**; it is a finite-dimensional real
vector space of dimension $d_N:=m\,|\Lambda_N|$, and $X_N\subseteq X_{N'}$ for
$N\le N'$. (The reality condition $a_{-k}=\overline{a_k}$ is exactly the
condition that the trigonometric polynomial be real-valued.)

**(b) Projection.** For $u\in L^2(\mathbb T^3_{2\pi};\mathbb R^m)$ define
$$P_Nu:=\sum_{k\in\Lambda_N}\widehat u(k)\chi_k,\qquad (P_Nu)(x)=\sum_{k\in\Lambda_N}\widehat u(k)\chi_k(x),$$
with $\widehat u(k)$ the Fourier coefficients of clause (c) of
[[def-gr-periodic-torus-and-sobolev-spaces]]; the second expression is a finite
sum, so $P_Nu\in X_N$; and $P_N:X_N\to X_N$ is the identity.
$P_N$ is called the **Galerkin (Fourier) projection**.

The definition fixes the projection only. Its self-adjointness,
derivative-commutation and operator-norm properties are proved in
[[lem-gr-galerkin-projection-properties]].

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$
([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $m\ge1$, $N\ge0$, and let $P_N$ be the Galerkin
projection and $X_N$ the Galerkin space of [[def-gr-galerkin-fourier-projection]]
on $\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}$. Then:

**(a)** $P_N$ is linear on $L^2(\mathbb T^3_{2\pi};\mathbb R^m)$, self-adjoint
($\langle P_Nu,v\rangle_2=\langle u,P_Nv\rangle_2$ for all $u,v\in L^2$) and
idempotent ($P_N^2=P_N$), with range $X_N$ and kernel the classes with vanishing
coefficients on $\Lambda_N$;

**(b)** for every multi-index $\alpha$ with $|\alpha|\le s$ and every
$u\in H^s$, $P_ND^\alpha u=D^\alpha P_Nu$;

**(c)** for every $0\le r\le s$ and every $u\in H^r$,
$\|P_Nu\|_{H^r}\le\|u\|_{H^r}$;

**(d)** for every $0\le r\le s$ and every $u\in H^r$, $P_Nu\to u$ in $H^r$ as
$N\to\infty$;

**(e)** for every $s\ge1$, every $u\in H^s$ and every $N\ge0$,
$$\|u-P_Nu\|_{H^{s-1}}\le C_s\,(1+N^2)^{-1/2}\,\|u\|_{H^s}$$
with $C_s$ depending only on $s$.

Let $m\ge1$ and let $B\in\operatorname{Sym}_m(\mathbb R)$ be positive definite,
that is $B^{\mathsf T}=B$ and $z^{\mathsf T}Bz>0$ for every nonzero
$z\in\mathbb R^m$ with the standard coordinate inner product.

**(a)** There are real numbers $0<a\le b$ with $a\,|z|^2\le z^{\mathsf T}Bz\le b\,|z|^2$
for every $z\in\mathbb R^m$; equivalently $aI\le B\le bI$ in the Loewner
order. They can be taken to be the least and largest eigenvalues of $B$.

**(b)** $B$ is invertible and $\tfrac1bI\le B^{-1}\le\tfrac1aI$, so in
particular $\|B^{-1}z\|\le a^{-1}\|z\|$.

**(c)** Let $\Lambda$ be a compact topological space and let
$B:\Lambda\to\operatorname{Sym}_m(\mathbb R)$ be continuous with $B(\lambda)$
positive definite for every $\lambda\in\Lambda$. Then there are constants
$0<a\le b$ with $aI\le B(\lambda)\le bI$ for every $\lambda\in\Lambda$.

**(d)** Let $D\subseteq\mathbb R^p$ be open and let $B:D\to\operatorname{Sym}_m(\mathbb R)$
be smooth with $B(x)\ge aI$ for a constant $a>0$ and all $x\in D$. Then
$x\mapsto B(x)^{-1}$ is smooth on $D$ and $B(x)^{-1}\le a^{-1}I$ there.

Let $D\subseteq\mathbb R\times\mathbb R^n$ be open, let $F:D\to\mathbb R^n$ be continuous and locally Lipschitz in the state variable, and let $(t_0,x_0)\in D$. Then a unique local solution of the IVP exists on some interval around the initial time. More quantitatively, if $h,r>0$ make

$$[t_0-h,t_0+h]\times\overline B(x_0,r)\subseteq D,$$

if $\|F\|_2\le M$ and $F$ has state-Lipschitz constant $L$ on this cylinder, and if $hM\le r$ and $Lh<1$, then there is exactly one solution on $[t_0-h,t_0+h]$ through $(t_0,x_0)$ whose graph lies in the cylinder. Any two solutions through the same initial data agree on every common subinterval containing $t_0$.

In particular, a unique local solution exists on an interval around the initial time.

Let $F(t,x,\lambda)$ be jointly $C^\infty$ in $(t,x,\lambda)$ on an open time-state-parameter
domain. Near any base data $(t_0,x_0,\lambda_0)$ there are a compact time
interval $I$ and a neighbourhood $W$ of $(x_0,\lambda_0)$ such that, for every
$(y,\lambda)\in W$, the solution of

$$x'(t)=F(t,x(t),\lambda),\qquad x(t_0)=y,$$

is defined on $I$, and the resulting solution map is smooth in the pair
$(y,\lambda)$.

Let $k\in\mathbb N$, let $m,q\ge1$, let $U\subseteq\mathbb R^m$ be open, and let $f:U\to\mathbb R^q$. A map $f:U\to\mathbb R^q$ is of class $C^k$ when each component is of class $C^k$. Each scalar component uses the word-derivative convention of [[def-ck-and-multi-index-notation-in-several-variables]], whose source dimension is positive. The map is **smooth**, or $C^\infty$, when it is $C^k$ for every $k\in\mathbb N$.

Let $n\ge1$ and let $U,V\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ be open. A bijection $f:U\to V$ is a **$C^k$ diffeomorphism** when both $f$ and $f^{-1}$ are $C^k$. For $k\ge1$, a **local $C^k$ diffeomorphism at $a\in U$** is a restriction $f|_P:P\to Q$ between open neighbourhoods of $a$ and $f(a)$ that is a $C^k$ diffeomorphism. At $k=1$ this agrees with [[def-c-one-map-and-local-inverse]]: continuous first partial derivatives give the required total derivative by [[thm-continuous-partial-derivatives-imply-total-differentiability]], while continuity of the total derivative gives continuity of its matrix entries and hence of the first partial derivatives.

Assume Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $s\ge5$, let $O\subseteq\mathbb R^m$ be open, let $I$ be an open time interval, let $I_0\subseteq I$ be a compact interval, and let $F:I\times\mathbb T^3\times O\to\mathbb R^{m'}$ and $A:I\times\mathbb T^3\times O\to M_{m'}(\mathbb R)$ be smooth. Fix compact $K\subseteq O$ and $R\ge0$. Constants below depend on these data and are uniform in $t\in I_0$. For $u,v\in H^s$ with values in $K$ and norms at most $R$:

**(a)** $\|F(t,\cdot,u)\|_{H^j}\le C(1+\|u\|_{H^s})$ for $0\le j\le s$.

**(b)** $\|F(t,\cdot,u)-F(t,\cdot,v)\|_{H^{s-1}}\le C\|u-v\|_{H^{s-1}}$. The same bound holds at order zero.

**(c)** For $1\le j=|\alpha|\le s-1$, $\|[D^\alpha,A(t,\cdot,u)]w\|_2\le C\|w\|_{H^{j-1}}$. For $|\alpha|=s$, $\|[D^\alpha,A(t,\cdot,u)]w\|_2\le C\|w\|_{H^{s-1}}$. Commutators are interpreted distributionally by their Leibniz expansion, even if the two individual order-$j$ terms are not separately in $L^2$.

**(d)** For $0\le j\le s-1$, $\|A(t,\cdot,u)w\|_{H^j}\le C\|w\|_{H^j}$.

**(e)** Let $n\ge6$, $\rho\ge0$ and $z\in H^n$ with values in $K$ and $\|z\|_{H^{n-1}}\le\rho$. Then $\|F(t,\cdot,z)\|_{H^n}\le C_\rho(1+\|z\|_{H^n})$. Moreover for $w\in H^{n-1}$ and $|\alpha|\le n$,
$$\|[D^\alpha,A(t,\cdot,z)]w\|_2\le C_\rho\bigl(\|w\|_{H^{n-1}}+(1+\|z\|_{H^n})\|w\|_{H^{n-2}}\bigr).$$
The same estimates apply to any smooth coefficient obtained from $F,A$ by differentiation or by a smooth matrix inverse where that inverse exists on a neighborhood of $I_0\times\mathbb T^3\times K$.

Let $k\in\mathbb N$, let $m,q\ge1$, let $U\subseteq\mathbb R^m$ be open, and let $f:U\to\mathbb R^q$. A map $f:U\to\mathbb R^q$ is of class $C^k$ when each component is of class $C^k$. Each scalar component uses the word-derivative convention of [[def-ck-and-multi-index-notation-in-several-variables]], whose source dimension is positive. The map is **smooth**, or $C^\infty$, when it is $C^k$ for every $k\in\mathbb N$.

Let $n\ge1$ and let $U,V\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ be open. A bijection $f:U\to V$ is a **$C^k$ diffeomorphism** when both $f$ and $f^{-1}$ are $C^k$. For $k\ge1$, a **local $C^k$ diffeomorphism at $a\in U$** is a restriction $f|_P:P\to Q$ between open neighbourhoods of $a$ and $f(a)$ that is a $C^k$ diffeomorphism. At $k=1$ this agrees with [[def-c-one-map-and-local-inverse]]: continuous first partial derivatives give the required total derivative by [[thm-continuous-partial-derivatives-imply-total-differentiability]], while continuity of the total derivative gives continuity of its matrix entries and hence of the first partial derivatives.

Let $n \in \mathbb{N}$ with $n \ge 1$, let $\mathbb{R}^n$ be the set of functions
$n \to \mathbb{R}$ and let $d_2$ be the Euclidean metric on it
([[lem-metrics-on-rn]]). Then:

1. **Closed boxes are compact.** For reals $a_k \le b_k$ $(k < n)$ the box
   $Q = \{\, x \in \mathbb{R}^n : a_k \le x_k \le b_k \text{ for every } k < n \,\}$
   is a compact subset of $(\mathbb{R}^n, d_2)$ ([[def-metric-compactness]]).
2. **Heine-Borel.** A subset $K \subseteq \mathbb{R}^n$ is a compact subset of
   $(\mathbb{R}^n, d_2)$ if and only if $K$ is closed in $\mathbb{R}^n$
   ([[def-metric-topology]]) and bounded
   ([[def-metric-bounded-diameter]]).
3. **The real line.** A subset $K \subseteq \mathbb{R}$ is a compact subset of
   $(\mathbb{R}, d_{\mathbb{R}})$, the usual metric $d_{\mathbb{R}}(x,y) = |x-y|$
   ([[lem-real-line-is-a-metric-space]]), if and only if $K$ is closed in
   $\mathbb{R}$ and bounded.

**No choice principle is used.** The bisection below halves one coordinate at a
time and takes the **left** half whenever the left half still fails to be finitely
covered, the right half otherwise: a rule with two outcomes, decided by a
property of the box, not a selection. That is the whole reason the theorem is
available in ZF, while the general "complete and totally bounded implies compact"
([[thm-complete-and-totally-bounded-implies-compact]]) is not.

The hypothesis $n \ge 1$ is inherited from [[lem-metrics-on-rn]], which defines
$\mathbb{R}^n$ and its metrics only there; the last remark below records what
happens at $n = 0$.

Let $(X,d)$ be a nonempty compact metric space ([[def-metric-compactness]],
[[def-metric-space]]) and let $f : X \to \mathbb{R}$ be continuous
([[def-metric-continuity]]), $\mathbb{R}$ carrying its usual metric
$d_{\mathbb{R}}(s,t) = |s-t|$ ([[lem-real-line-is-a-metric-space]]). Then the
image $f[X]$ is bounded above and below ([[def-bounded-set]]), and it has a
maximum and a minimum ([[def-max-min]]): there are points
$x_{\max}, x_{\min} \in X$ with

$$f(x_{\min}) \;\le\; f(x) \;\le\; f(x_{\max}) \qquad \text{for every } x \in X,$$

and then $f(x_{\max}) = \sup f[X]$ and $f(x_{\min}) = \inf f[X]$
([[def-complete-ordered-field]], [[def-infimum]]).

Nonemptiness of $X$ is a hypothesis and not an oversight: for $X = \emptyset$ the
image is empty and has neither a supremum nor a maximum. No choice principle is
used.

Assume Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]) for the Lebesgue-measure interfaces. Let $X$ be a real or complex Banach space, let $a<b$, and let $f:[a,b]\to X$ be continuous. Differentiation uses the underlying real structure. Then $G(t):=\int_a^t f(s)\,ds$ is differentiable on $(a,b)$ and has the corresponding one-sided derivatives at $a,b$, with $G'(t)=f(t)$, and this derivative extends continuously to $[a,b]$. Consequently, if $\varphi:[a,b]\to X$ is continuous, differentiable on $(a,b)$ with $\varphi'$ continuous on $(a,b)$ and extendable to a continuous $X$-valued function on $[a,b]$, then $\int_a^b\varphi'(s)\,ds=\varphi(b)-\varphi(a)$. The Bochner integral here is the one of [[def-bochner-integrable-function]]; the identities also hold for continuous curves on $[0,\infty)$ restricted to compact subintervals.

derivations.claim: (The finite-dimensional form of the Galerkin system.) Fix a basis of $X_N$ and let $\pi:\mathbb R^{d_N}\to X_N$ be the coordinate isomorphism. Define $V:=\{z\in\mathbb R^{d_N}:\pi(z)(x)\in O\ \forall x\}$, an open set containing the coordinates of $P_Nu_0$, and for $z\in V$ and $v\in X_N$ define $M(t,z)v:=P_N[A^0(t,\cdot,\pi(z))\,v]$. For $v\ne0$, self-adjointness [L1] gives $\langle v,M(t,z)v\rangle_{L^2}=\int v^{\mathsf T}A^0(t,\cdot,\pi(z))v\,d\mu\ge a_z\|v\|_2^2$ with $a_z>0$ by [L2] applied to a compact set containing the values of $\pi(z)$; on compact subsets of $V$ the bound is uniform, so $M(t,z)$ is invertible with smooth inverse there by [[lem-gr-positive-definite-symmetric-matrix-bounds]] clause (d). Define $G(t,z):=\pi^{-1}\!\left(M(t,z)^{-1}\bigl(-P_N[\sum_iA^i(t,\cdot,\pi(z))\partial_i\pi(z)+B(t,\cdot,\pi(z))]\bigr)\right)$, which is smooth in $(t,z)$ on $I\times V$ by [L4] and the smoothness of the inverse; then $u_N(t)=\pi(z(t))$ solves the Galerkin system iff $z'(t)=G(t,z(t))$, and $z(0)$ is the coordinate of $P_Nu_0$.

(Local existence and smooth dependence (a), (c).) Since $G$ is continuous and locally Lipschitz on the open set $I\times V$ and the initial point lies in it, Picard--Lindelöf [L3] gives a unique local solution through the initial point, defined on an open interval $J_N\ni0$; smoothness of $G$ and the smooth-dependence theorem [L3] give the smooth finite-dimensional flow, hence (c), and (a) follows by transporting through $\pi$.

(Continuation within the coefficient time domain.) Suppose $T_*\in I$ is finite and the stated value and norm bounds hold. The coordinate set $Q$ of fields in $X_N$ whose values lie in compact $C\subseteq O$ and whose $H^s$ norms are at most $R_1$ is closed and bounded in a finite-dimensional space, hence compact, and it lies inside $V$. Choose $\delta>0$ with $[T_*-\delta,T_*+\delta]\subseteq I$. The smooth field $G$ is bounded by some $L$ on this compact time interval times $Q$. Thus for $T_*-\delta<t<t'<T_*$ the equation and the ordinary fundamental theorem of calculus give $|z(t')-z(t)|\le L|t'-t|$. The coordinate curve has a limit $z_*\in Q$ as $t\uparrow T_*$, by completeness of Euclidean space and closedness of $Q$. Extend it to $z(T_*)=z_*$. Continuity of $G$ gives $G(t,z(t))\to G(T_*,z_*)$, so its integral identity extends to $T_*$ and the extended curve is $C^1$ there from the left. Picard--Lindelöf [L3] at the interior point $(T_*,z_*)$ supplies a local solution on both sides of $T_*$. The original curve and this local solution agree on their overlap by uniqueness, hence glue to a solution beyond $T_*$. This contradicts maximality and proves (b). The backward criterion follows by reversing time.

boundaries.evidence: The Given clause includes an admissible projected datum, so its coordinate domain V in step 1.1 is nonempty; Lambda_N includes k=0.
An admissible zero datum need not be an equilibrium because B(t,x,0) may be nonzero; step 1.1 keeps that forcing when forming G.
For m=1 and N=0, X_N consists of a scalar constant mode and step 1.1 gives an ordinary scalar ODE with the same positive projected mass coefficient.
Step 1.1 proves the projected mass matrix positive before inversion; leaving the open state set is explicitly excluded by the compact trajectory in step 3.1.
Step 3.1 assumes T_* lies inside I and constructs the limiting coordinate z_* in compact Q before restarting; no continuation at a coefficient-domain endpoint is claimed.
The basis fixed in step 1.1 is one finite-dimensional basis; the Countable Choice premise comes from the analytic/Fourier suppliers, not an arbitrary family of ODE choices.

with $\widehat u(k)$ the Fourier coefficients of clause (c) of

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$
([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $s\ge5$, let $O\subseteq\mathbb R^m$ be open,
let $A^\mu,B$ be a periodic symmetric hyperbolic coefficient family on $O$ over
an open interval $I\ni0$ ([[def-gr-periodic-symmetric-hyperbolic-system]]), let
$u_0\in H^s(\mathbb T^3_{2\pi};\mathbb R^m)$ take values in a compact
$K\subseteq O$ with $\|u_0\|_{H^s}\le R$, and let $P_N$, $X_N$ be the Galerkin
projection and space ([[def-gr-galerkin-fourier-projection]]). Fix $N\ge0$ for which $P_Nu_0$ takes values in $O$. Then:

**(a)** there is an open interval $J_N\ni0$ and a $C^1$ map $u_N:J_N\to X_N$
such that for all $t\in J_N$
$$P_N\Bigl[A^0(t,\cdot,u_N(t))\,\partial_tu_N(t)+\sum_{i=1}^3A^i(t,\cdot,u_N(t))\,\partial_iu_N(t)+B(t,\cdot,u_N(t))\Bigr]=0\quad\text{in }L^2,$$
with $u_N(0)=P_Nu_0$;

**(b)** [continuation criterion] if $[0,T_*)$ is the forward-maximal interval of
existence of $u_N$ and there are a compact $C\subseteq O$ and a constant
$R_1\ge0$ with $u_N(t)$ taking values in $C$ and $\|u_N(t)\|_{H^s}\le R_1$ for
all $t\in[0,T_*)$, and $T_*\in I$, then $u_N$ does not have $T_*$ as a finite forward endpoint:
the solution extends beyond $T_*$;

**(c)** the solution is unique and its local flow depends smoothly on the
finite-dimensional coordinates of the initial data.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$
([[def-countable-choice]]). Fix an integer $m\ge1$, an open set
$O\subseteq\mathbb R^m$ with the subspace topology and a nondegenerate open
interval $I\subseteq\mathbb R$ containing $0$. All functions on
$\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}$ are those of [[def-gr-periodic-torus-and-sobolev-spaces]],
and smoothness on $I\times\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}\times O$ means smoothness of the
representative in the sense of clause (e) of that item.

**(a) Coefficients.** A **periodic symmetric hyperbolic coefficient family** on
$O$ consists of smooth maps
$$A^\mu:I\times\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}\times O\to\operatorname{Sym}_m(\mathbb R)\quad(\mu=0,1,2,3),\qquad B:I\times\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}\times O\to\mathbb R^m,$$
such that $A^0(t,x,u)$ is positive definite for every
$(t,x,u)\in I\times\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}\times O$; here
$\operatorname{Sym}_m(\mathbb R)$ is the real vector space of symmetric
$m\times m$ matrices, identified with symmetric endomorphisms of $\mathbb R^m$
through the standard coordinate inner product, and positive definiteness means
$z^TA^0(t,x,u)z>0$ for every nonzero $z\in\mathbb R^m$
([[def-ck-and-multi-index-notation-in-several-variables]]).

**(b) The system.** The associated **symmetric hyperbolic system** is
$$A^0(t,x,u)\,\partial_tu+\sum_{i=1}^3A^i(t,x,u)\,\partial_iu+B(t,x,u)=0 .\qquad(\star)$$

**(c) Values and norms.** A map $u:J\to H^s(\mathbb T^3_{2\pi};\mathbb R^m)$
on an interval $J$ **takes values in a set $E\subseteq\mathbb R^m$** when
$u(t)(x)\in E$ for every $t\in J$ and every $x\in\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}$, with
$u(t)$ read through its continuous representative when $s>3/2$. For compact
$K\subseteq O$ and $R\ge0$ put
$$\mathcal S(K,R):=\bigl\{u_0\in H^s(\mathbb T^3_{2\pi};\mathbb R^m):u_0\text{ takes values in }K,\ \|u_0\|_{H^s}\le R\bigr\}.$$

**(d) Classical solutions.** Let $s\ge2$. A **classical solution of $(\star)$ on
$J\times\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}$** is a $C^1$ map
$u:J\times\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}\to\mathbb R^m$ with $u(t,x)\in O$ for all
$(t,x)$ and $(\star)$ satisfied at every point, such that
$u\in L^\infty(J;H^s)$ and $\partial_tu\in L^\infty(J;H^{s-1})$. (For $s\ge2$
the embedding clause gives a continuous representative, so the pointwise
conditions are meaningful.)

**(e) Sobolev solutions.** Let $s\ge5$ and let $J$ be an open interval. A map
$u:J\to H^s(\mathbb T^3_{2\pi};\mathbb R^m)$ is a **Sobolev solution of
$(\star)$ on $J$** when

1. $u\in L^\infty(J;H^s)\cap C^0(J;H^{s-1})$ and the distributional time
   derivative $\partial_tu$ lies in $L^\infty(J;H^{s-1})$;
2. $u$ takes values in $O$;
3. for almost every $t\in J$ the identity $(\star)$ holds in
   $L^2(\mathbb T^3_{2\pi};\mathbb R^m)$, the coefficients being composed with
   the continuous representative of $u(t)$; all products are defined because
   $A^0(t,\cdot,u(t))$ and $A^i(t,\cdot,u(t))$ lie in $H^s$ with norm bounded
   by a function of $\|u(t)\|_{H^s}$, $\partial_tu(t)$ and $\partial_iu(t)$ lie
   in $H^{s-1}$, and $B(t,\cdot,u(t))$ lies in $H^s$.

**(f) Initial data.** **Initial data for $(\star)$ at time $0$** are a class
$u_0\in H^s(\mathbb T^3_{2\pi};\mathbb R^m)$ with $s\ge5$ whose values lie in a
compact subset of $O$; a solution **has initial value $u_0$** when
$u(t)\to u_0$ in $H^{s-1}$ as $t\to0$ within $J$.

The definition introduces the system and its solution classes only; existence,
uniqueness, continuous dependence and smooth persistence are asserted and
proved in [[thm-gr-periodic-symmetric-hyperbolic-existence]],
[[thm-gr-periodic-symmetric-hyperbolic-uniqueness-stability]] and
[[thm-gr-periodic-symmetric-hyperbolic-smooth-persistence]].

Let $m\ge1$ and let $B\in\operatorname{Sym}_m(\mathbb R)$ be positive definite,
that is $B^{\mathsf T}=B$ and $z^{\mathsf T}Bz>0$ for every nonzero
$z\in\mathbb R^m$ with the standard coordinate inner product.

**(a)** There are real numbers $0<a\le b$ with $a\,|z|^2\le z^{\mathsf T}Bz\le b\,|z|^2$
for every $z\in\mathbb R^m$; equivalently $aI\le B\le bI$ in the Loewner
order. They can be taken to be the least and largest eigenvalues of $B$.

**(b)** $B$ is invertible and $\tfrac1bI\le B^{-1}\le\tfrac1aI$, so in
particular $\|B^{-1}z\|\le a^{-1}\|z\|$.

**(c)** Let $\Lambda$ be a compact topological space and let
$B:\Lambda\to\operatorname{Sym}_m(\mathbb R)$ be continuous with $B(\lambda)$
positive definite for every $\lambda\in\Lambda$. Then there are constants
$0<a\le b$ with $aI\le B(\lambda)\le bI$ for every $\lambda\in\Lambda$.

**(d)** Let $D\subseteq\mathbb R^p$ be open and let $B:D\to\operatorname{Sym}_m(\mathbb R)$
be smooth with $B(x)\ge aI$ for a constant $a>0$ and all $x\in D$. Then
$x\mapsto B(x)^{-1}$ is smooth on $D$ and $B(x)^{-1}\le a^{-1}I$ there.

Assume Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $s\ge5$, let $O\subseteq\mathbb R^m$ be open, let $I$ be an open time interval, let $I_0\subseteq I$ be a compact interval, and let $F:I\times\mathbb T^3\times O\to\mathbb R^{m'}$ and $A:I\times\mathbb T^3\times O\to M_{m'}(\mathbb R)$ be smooth. Fix compact $K\subseteq O$ and $R\ge0$. Constants below depend on these data and are uniform in $t\in I_0$. For $u,v\in H^s$ with values in $K$ and norms at most $R$:

**(a)** $\|F(t,\cdot,u)\|_{H^j}\le C(1+\|u\|_{H^s})$ for $0\le j\le s$.

**(b)** $\|F(t,\cdot,u)-F(t,\cdot,v)\|_{H^{s-1}}\le C\|u-v\|_{H^{s-1}}$. The same bound holds at order zero.

**(c)** For $1\le j=|\alpha|\le s-1$, $\|[D^\alpha,A(t,\cdot,u)]w\|_2\le C\|w\|_{H^{j-1}}$. For $|\alpha|=s$, $\|[D^\alpha,A(t,\cdot,u)]w\|_2\le C\|w\|_{H^{s-1}}$. Commutators are interpreted distributionally by their Leibniz expansion, even if the two individual order-$j$ terms are not separately in $L^2$.

**(d)** For $0\le j\le s-1$, $\|A(t,\cdot,u)w\|_{H^j}\le C\|w\|_{H^j}$.

**(e)** Let $n\ge6$, $\rho\ge0$ and $z\in H^n$ with values in $K$ and $\|z\|_{H^{n-1}}\le\rho$. Then $\|F(t,\cdot,z)\|_{H^n}\le C_\rho(1+\|z\|_{H^n})$. Moreover for $w\in H^{n-1}$ and $|\alpha|\le n$,
$$\|[D^\alpha,A(t,\cdot,z)]w\|_2\le C_\rho\bigl(\|w\|_{H^{n-1}}+(1+\|z\|_{H^n})\|w\|_{H^{n-2}}\bigr).$$
The same estimates apply to any smooth coefficient obtained from $F,A$ by differentiation or by a smooth matrix inverse where that inverse exists on a neighborhood of $I_0\times\mathbb T^3\times K$.

Let $m\ge1$, let $U\subseteq\mathbb R^m$ be open, and let $f:U\to\mathbb R$. A **multi-index** is $\alpha=(\alpha_0,\ldots,\alpha_{m-1})\in\mathbb N^m$. Put

$$|\alpha|:=\sum_{i<m}\alpha_i,\qquad \alpha!:=\prod_{i<m}\alpha_i!,\qquad h^\alpha:=\prod_{i<m}h_i^{\alpha_i}\quad(h\in\mathbb R^m).$$

Here $|\alpha|$ and $\alpha!$ use the natural-number sum and product of [[def-nat-finite-sum-and-product]], and $n!$ is the factorial of [[def-factorial-and-falling-factorial]]. By contrast, $h^\alpha$ is the finite product in $\mathbb R$ of [[def-finite-sum]], with the natural exponents interpreted by [[def-integer-power]]. For the zero multi-index $0$, set $D^0f:=f$. For nonzero $\alpha$, write

$$D^\alpha f:=\partial_0^{\alpha_0}\cdots\partial_{m-1}^{\alpha_{m-1}}f$$

for this displayed, canonical order whenever it exists. Coordinate partial derivatives have the meaning fixed in [[def-directional-and-partial-derivatives]].

For $k\in\mathbb N$, $f$ is of class $C^k$ on $U$ when, for every word $(i_1,\ldots,i_r)$ of coordinate indices with $0\le r\le k$, the iterated derivative $\partial_{i_r}\cdots\partial_{i_1}f$ exists and is continuous on $U$; the word of length $0$ denotes $f$. Thus this definition does **not** presuppose that differently ordered derivatives are equal. Equality of their values is a later theorem under these regularity hypotheses.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$
([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $m\ge1$, $N\ge0$, and let $P_N$ be the Galerkin
projection and $X_N$ the Galerkin space of [[def-gr-galerkin-fourier-projection]]
on $\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}$. Then:

**(a)** $P_N$ is linear on $L^2(\mathbb T^3_{2\pi};\mathbb R^m)$, self-adjoint
($\langle P_Nu,v\rangle_2=\langle u,P_Nv\rangle_2$ for all $u,v\in L^2$) and
idempotent ($P_N^2=P_N$), with range $X_N$ and kernel the classes with vanishing
coefficients on $\Lambda_N$;

**(b)** for every multi-index $\alpha$ with $|\alpha|\le s$ and every
$u\in H^s$, $P_ND^\alpha u=D^\alpha P_Nu$;

**(c)** for every $0\le r\le s$ and every $u\in H^r$,
$\|P_Nu\|_{H^r}\le\|u\|_{H^r}$;

**(d)** for every $0\le r\le s$ and every $u\in H^r$, $P_Nu\to u$ in $H^r$ as
$N\to\infty$;

**(e)** for every $s\ge1$, every $u\in H^s$ and every $N\ge0$,
$$\|u-P_Nu\|_{H^{s-1}}\le C_s\,(1+N^2)^{-1/2}\,\|u\|_{H^s}$$
with $C_s$ depending only on $s$.

derivations.claim: (Order zero.) Pair the Galerkin equation [L2] with $\partial_tu_N$: since $\partial_tu_N\in X_N$, self-adjointness [L1] gives $\int(\partial_tu_N)^{\mathsf T}P_N[A^0\partial_tu_N]=\int(\partial_tu_N)^{\mathsf T}A^0\partial_tu_N\ge a\|\partial_tu_N\|_2^2$ by [L3]; the right-hand side is $-\int(\partial_tu_N)^{\mathsf T}P_N[A^i\partial_iu_N+B]\le\|\partial_tu_N\|_2\|A^i\partial_iu_N+B\|_2$, and $\|A^i\partial_iu_N+B\|_{L^2}\le C_R(1+\|u_N\|_{H^s})$ by [L4] (the composition $A^i(t,\cdot,u_N)$ lies in $H^s\subseteq C^0$, so its sup norm is at most $C_R$, and $\|\partial_iu_N\|_2\le\|u_N\|_{H^s}$; the term $B$ is similar). Hence $a\|\partial_tu_N\|_2\le C_R(1+\|u_N\|_{H^s})$.

(Induction on the order: the estimate at order $j$.) Fix $j$ with $1\le j\le s-1$ and suppose the bound holds for all orders below $j$; fix $|\alpha|=j$. Applying $P_ND^\alpha$ to the Galerkin equation [L2] (legitimate by commutation [L1]) and pairing with $D^\alpha\partial_tu_N\in X_N$ gives, after moving the leading term and using self-adjointness [L1], $a\|D^\alpha\partial_tu_N\|_2\le\bigl\|[D^\alpha,A^0(t,\cdot,u_N)]\partial_tu_N\bigr\|_2+\bigl\|D^\alpha(A^i(t,\cdot,u_N)\partial_iu_N+B(t,\cdot,u_N))\bigr\|_2$: indeed $D^\alpha(A^0\partial_tu_N)=A^0D^\alpha\partial_tu_N+[D^\alpha,A^0]\partial_tu_N$ by [L5], and the pairing of $P_ND^\alpha(A^0\partial_tu_N)$ with $D^\alpha\partial_tu_N$ removes $P_N$. The first term is at most $C_R\|\partial_tu_N\|_{H^{j-1}}$ by [L4], hence at most $C_R'(1+\|u_N\|_{H^s})$ by the induction hypothesis; the second is at most $C_R(1+\|u_N\|_{H^s})$ by [L4] applied to the compositions $A^i(t,\cdot,u_N)$ and the product bound, since $\|\partial_iu_N\|_{H^{j}}\le\|u_N\|_{H^s}$. Summing over the finitely many $|\alpha|\le j$ gives the estimate at order $j$.
(Conclusion.) The induction of step 2.1, starting from step 1.1, gives the stated bound for every $0\le j\le s-1$ after enlarging the constant to be independent of $j$.

boundaries.evidence: The Statement is conditional on a Galerkin solution on J; if J is empty the bound is vacuous, and otherwise K must contain its values.
Step 1.1 retains B(u_N) in the projected equation, so a zero field is not assumed stationary; the RHS estimate includes 1 for inhomogeneous forcing.
The range j=0 in Statement is the base L2 coercivity estimate of step 1.1; N=0 still has the constant Fourier mode rather than an empty Galerkin space.
The time-matrix positivity bound used in step 1.1 protects its inverse estimate; no estimate is claimed when this coercivity vanishes.
The Statement fixes a compact I0 strictly inside the coefficient time domain, so coefficient derivatives are bounded at its endpoints as well as its interior.
Statement and steps 1.1–2.1: All differentiations in the proof concern the given finite-dimensional Galerkin solution; Countable Choice is retained for its Fourier and Sobolev prerequisites.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$
([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}$, $\mu$, $\chi_k$,
$\widehat u(k)$, the weak derivatives $D^\alpha$ and the spaces
$H^s(\mathbb T^3_{2\pi};\mathbb R^N)$ be as in
[[def-gr-periodic-torus-and-sobolev-spaces]], and put
$$N_s(u)^2:=\sum_{k\in\mathbb Z^3}(1+|k|^2)^s\,|\widehat u(k)|^2,\qquad |k|^2:=k_1^2+k_2^2+k_3^2 .$$

**(a)** Let $u\in H^s$ and let $\alpha\in\mathbb N_0^3$ with $|\alpha|\le s$. Then
$D^\alpha u\in H^{s-|\alpha|}$ and
$$\widehat{D^\alpha u}(k)=(ik)^\alpha\,\widehat u(k)\qquad(k\in\mathbb Z^3),\qquad (ik)^\alpha:=\prod_{j=1}^3(ik_j)^{\alpha_j}.$$

**(b)** Let $u\in L^2(\mathbb T^3_{2\pi};\mathbb R^N)$ satisfy $N_s(u)<\infty$.
Then $u\in H^s(\mathbb T^3_{2\pi};\mathbb R^N)$, and there are constants
$0<c_s\le C_s<\infty$, depending only on $s$, such that
$$c_s\,N_s(u)^2\le\|u\|_{H^s}^2\le C_s\,N_s(u)^2 .$$
The right-hand inequality holds for every $u\in H^s$, so the two norms are
equivalent on $H^s$.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$
([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $m\ge1$, $N\ge0$, and let $P_N$ be the Galerkin
projection and $X_N$ the Galerkin space of [[def-gr-galerkin-fourier-projection]]
on $\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}$. Then:

**(a)** $P_N$ is linear on $L^2(\mathbb T^3_{2\pi};\mathbb R^m)$, self-adjoint
($\langle P_Nu,v\rangle_2=\langle u,P_Nv\rangle_2$ for all $u,v\in L^2$) and
idempotent ($P_N^2=P_N$), with range $X_N$ and kernel the classes with vanishing
coefficients on $\Lambda_N$;

**(b)** for every multi-index $\alpha$ with $|\alpha|\le s$ and every
$u\in H^s$, $P_ND^\alpha u=D^\alpha P_Nu$;

**(c)** for every $0\le r\le s$ and every $u\in H^r$,
$\|P_Nu\|_{H^r}\le\|u\|_{H^r}$;

**(d)** for every $0\le r\le s$ and every $u\in H^r$, $P_Nu\to u$ in $H^r$ as
$N\to\infty$;

**(e)** for every $s\ge1$, every $u\in H^s$ and every $N\ge0$,
$$\|u-P_Nu\|_{H^{s-1}}\le C_s\,(1+N^2)^{-1/2}\,\|u\|_{H^s}$$
with $C_s$ depending only on $s$.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$
([[def-countable-choice]]) for the quotient, product-measure and integration
clauses below, as in [[def-the-one-dimensional-torus-and-normalized-haar-integral]].

**(a) The 2 pi-periodic torus.** Let $\mathbb T_{2\pi}:=\mathbb R/2\pi\mathbb Z$
carry the quotient topology, and let
$$\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}:=\mathbb T_{2\pi}\times\mathbb T_{2\pi}\times\mathbb T_{2\pi}$$
with the product topology; write $q:\mathbb R^3\to\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}$ for the
quotient map and $[x]:=(x^1+2\pi\mathbb Z,x^2+2\pi\mathbb Z,x^3+2\pi\mathbb Z)$.
The map $[0,2\pi)^3\to\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}$, $x\mapsto[x]$, is a bijection. The
normalized product measure $\mu$ is $\mu_{\mathbb T}\otimes\mu_{\mathbb T}\otimes\mu_{\mathbb T}$,
where $\mu_{\mathbb T}$ is the normalized measure of
[[def-the-one-dimensional-torus-and-normalized-haar-integral]] transported by
$t\mapsto2\pi t$; it is a probability measure on the Borel sets of
$\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}$ and $\int f\,d\mu=(2\pi)^{-3}\int_{[0,2\pi)^3}f\circ q\,d\lambda_3$
for bounded measurable $f$ ([[thm-tonelli-theorem-for-sigma-finite-product-spaces]]).

**(b) Test functions and continuous classes.** For $N\ge1$ let
$C^\infty(\mathbb T^3_{2\pi};\mathbb R^N)$ be the set of compositions
$u\circ q$ of smooth maps $u:\mathbb R^3\to\mathbb R^N$ that are $2\pi$-periodic
in each variable; these are the **smooth test functions** (real-valued when
$N=1$). For $m\ge0$ let $C^m(\mathbb T^3_{2\pi};\mathbb R^N)$ be the set of
$u\circ q$ with $u\in C^m(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb R^N)$ $2\pi$-periodic in each
variable ([[def-c-r-and-smooth-maps-between-smooth-manifolds]]), with
$$\|u\|_{C^m}:=\max_{|\alpha|\le m}\ \sup_{x\in\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}}\bigl|(D^\alpha u)(x)\bigr| ,$$
where $D^\alpha$ is the multi-index derivative of
[[def-ck-and-multi-index-notation-in-several-variables]] applied to any
periodic representative; the displayed expression is independent of the
representative.

**(c) The Hilbert space $L^2$.** For $N\ge1$ let
$L^2(\mathbb T^3_{2\pi};\mathbb R^N)$ be the quotient of the set of measurable
$u$ with $\int|u|^2\,d\mu<\infty$ by the $\mu$-a.e. zero functions
([[def-l-p-space-as-a-quotient-by-null-functions]],
[[thm-the-l-p-norm-descends-to-the-quotient-and-makes-l-p-a-normed-space]]),
with inner product $\langle u,v\rangle_2=\int u\cdot v\,d\mu$ and norm
$\|u\|_2=\langle u,u\rangle_2^{1/2}$; it is a real Hilbert space
([[lem-l-two-with-the-integral-pairing-is-a-hilbert-space]]). For
$u\in L^2(\mathbb T^3_{2\pi};\mathbb R^N)$ and $k\in\mathbb Z^3$ the
**$k$-th Fourier coefficient** is the vector
$$\widehat u(k):=\int_{\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}}u(x)\,e^{-ik\cdot x}\,d\mu(x)\in\mathbb C^N ,$$
where $e^{-ik\cdot x}:=\chi_{-k}$ with $\chi_k([x]):=\exp(i\,k\cdot x)$; here
$u$ is read through any representative. Write $\chi_k:\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}\to\mathbb C$,
$k\in\mathbb Z^3$, for these **characters**; under the identification
$x=2\pi y$ they are the characters $\exp(2\pi i\,k\cdot y)$ of
[[thm-fourier-basis-and-parseval-on-the-n-torus]], so $(\chi_k)_{k\in\mathbb Z^3}$
is an orthonormal basis of the complex space $L^2(\mathbb T^3_{2\pi};\mathbb C)$.

**(d) Weak derivatives and the periodic Sobolev spaces.** For
$u,v\in L^1(\mathbb T^3_{2\pi};\mathbb R)$ and $\alpha\in\mathbb N_0^3$ say that
$v$ is the **weak derivative** $D^\alpha u$ if
$$\int_{\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}}u\,D^\alpha\varphi\,d\mu=(-1)^{|\alpha|}\int_{\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}}v\,\varphi\,d\mu$$
for every $\varphi\in C^\infty(\mathbb T^3_{2\pi};\mathbb R)$, where $D^\alpha\varphi$
is the multi-index derivative of the periodic representative
([[def-weak-derivative-of-a-locally-integrable-function]] records the
Euclidean analogue). For an integer $s\ge0$ let
$$H^s(\mathbb T^3_{2\pi};\mathbb R^N):=\Bigl\{u\in L^2(\mathbb T^3_{2\pi};\mathbb R^N):\ \text{for every }|\alpha|\le s\text{ there is }v_\alpha\in L^2(\mathbb T^3_{2\pi};\mathbb R^N)\text{ with }v_\alpha=D^\alpha u\Bigr\},$$
the vector-valued weak derivative being componentwise, and put
$$\|u\|_{H^s}:=\Bigl(\sum_{|\alpha|\le s}\|D^\alpha u\|_2^2\Bigr)^{1/2}.$$
The classes $L^2\subseteq L^1$ on the probability space, so the integrals in the
test identity are finite: $|\int u\,D^\alpha\varphi\,d\mu|\le\|u\|_2\|D^\alpha\varphi\|_2$
by Cauchy--Schwarz. The definition asserts neither that the weak derivative
exists nor that the two norms compared in the next item are equivalent; those
are proved in [[lem-gr-periodic-fourier-differentiation-and-norm-equivalence]].

**(e) Conventions.** $O\subseteq\mathbb R^m$ open, $I\subseteq\mathbb R$ an
interval and maps $F:I\times\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}\times O\to\mathbb R^{m'}$ are
called smooth when their representatives $F(t,q(x),u)=G(t,x,u)$ have
$G\in C^\infty$. Throughout this page the torus is always this
$2\pi$-periodic one; a statement "for every $x$" means for every point of
$\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}$, and "a.e." means $\mu$-a.e.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$
([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $m\ge1$, $N\ge0$, and let $P_N$ be the Galerkin
projection and $X_N$ the Galerkin space of [[def-gr-galerkin-fourier-projection]]
on $\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}$. Then:

**(a)** $P_N$ is linear on $L^2(\mathbb T^3_{2\pi};\mathbb R^m)$, self-adjoint
($\langle P_Nu,v\rangle_2=\langle u,P_Nv\rangle_2$ for all $u,v\in L^2$) and
idempotent ($P_N^2=P_N$), with range $X_N$ and kernel the classes with vanishing
coefficients on $\Lambda_N$;

**(b)** for every multi-index $\alpha$ with $|\alpha|\le s$ and every
$u\in H^s$, $P_ND^\alpha u=D^\alpha P_Nu$;

**(c)** for every $0\le r\le s$ and every $u\in H^r$,
$\|P_Nu\|_{H^r}\le\|u\|_{H^r}$;

**(d)** for every $0\le r\le s$ and every $u\in H^r$, $P_Nu\to u$ in $H^r$ as
$N\to\infty$;

**(e)** for every $s\ge1$, every $u\in H^s$ and every $N\ge0$,
$$\|u-P_Nu\|_{H^{s-1}}\le C_s\,(1+N^2)^{-1/2}\,\|u\|_{H^s}$$
with $C_s$ depending only on $s$.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$
([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}$, $\mu$, $\chi_k$ and the
spaces $H^s(\mathbb T^3_{2\pi};\mathbb R^m)$ be as in
[[def-gr-periodic-torus-and-sobolev-spaces]] ($m\ge1$).

**(a) Mode sets.** For $N\ge0$ put
$\Lambda_N:=\{k\in\mathbb Z^3:|k|\le N\}$ with $|k|$ the Euclidean norm, and
$$X_N:=\Bigl\{\sum_{k\in\Lambda_N}a_k\chi_k:\ a_k\in\mathbb C^m,\ a_{-k}=\overline{a_k}\Bigr\}\subseteq C^\infty(\mathbb T^3_{2\pi};\mathbb R^m),$$
the **Galerkin space of modes up to $N$**; it is a finite-dimensional real
vector space of dimension $d_N:=m\,|\Lambda_N|$, and $X_N\subseteq X_{N'}$ for
$N\le N'$. (The reality condition $a_{-k}=\overline{a_k}$ is exactly the
condition that the trigonometric polynomial be real-valued.)

**(b) Projection.** For $u\in L^2(\mathbb T^3_{2\pi};\mathbb R^m)$ define
$$P_Nu:=\sum_{k\in\Lambda_N}\widehat u(k)\chi_k,\qquad (P_Nu)(x)=\sum_{k\in\Lambda_N}\widehat u(k)\chi_k(x),$$
with $\widehat u(k)$ the Fourier coefficients of clause (c) of
[[def-gr-periodic-torus-and-sobolev-spaces]]; the second expression is a finite
sum, so $P_Nu\in X_N$; and $P_N:X_N\to X_N$ is the identity.
$P_N$ is called the **Galerkin (Fourier) projection**.

The definition fixes the projection only. Its self-adjointness,
derivative-commutation and operator-norm properties are proved in
[[lem-gr-galerkin-projection-properties]].

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$
([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $s\ge5$, fix a compact interval $I_0$ inside the coefficient time domain, and assume $J\subseteq I_0$. Let $A^\mu,B$ be a periodic symmetric
hyperbolic coefficient family on the open set $O\subseteq\mathbb R^m$
([[def-gr-periodic-symmetric-hyperbolic-system]]), let $K\subseteq O$ be compact
and $R\ge0$, and let $u_N:J\to X_N$ be a Galerkin solution of
[[lem-gr-galerkin-ode-local-solution]] for some $N\ge0$. Suppose that
$u_N(t)$ takes values in $K$ and satisfies $\|u_N(t)\|_{H^s}\le R$ for every
$t\in J$. Then there is $C=C(A^\mu,B,K,R,s,I_0)$ such that for every
$0\le j\le s-1$ and every $t\in J$
$$\|\partial_tu_N(t)\|_{H^j}\le C\,\bigl(1+\|u_N(t)\|_{H^s}\bigr).$$

Assume Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]) for the Lebesgue-measure interfaces. Let $X$ be a real or complex Banach space, let $a<b$, and let $f:[a,b]\to X$ be continuous. Differentiation uses the underlying real structure. Then $G(t):=\int_a^t f(s)\,ds$ is differentiable on $(a,b)$ and has the corresponding one-sided derivatives at $a,b$, with $G'(t)=f(t)$, and this derivative extends continuously to $[a,b]$. Consequently, if $\varphi:[a,b]\to X$ is continuous, differentiable on $(a,b)$ with $\varphi'$ continuous on $(a,b)$ and extendable to a continuous $X$-valued function on $[a,b]$, then $\int_a^b\varphi'(s)\,ds=\varphi(b)-\varphi(a)$. The Bochner integral here is the one of [[def-bochner-integrable-function]]; the identities also hold for continuous curves on $[0,\infty)$ restricted to compact subintervals.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$
([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $s\ge0$ be an integer and $N\ge1$, write
$H^s=H^s(\mathbb T^3_{2\pi};\mathbb R^N)$ for the periodic Sobolev space with
its norm $\|\cdot\|_{H^s}$ and Fourier coefficients
$\widehat u(k)\in\mathbb C^N$ of [[def-gr-periodic-torus-and-sobolev-spaces]],
and put

**(b)** more precisely, for every Cauchy sequence $(u_n)$ in $H^s$ there is

**(i)** there is $\kappa\ge0$ with $\|x\|_0\le\kappa\|x\|_1$ for every
$x\in X_1$; and

converging in $X_0$ ([[def-metric-convergence]]).

derivations.claim: (Compact embedding (a) by deterministic index selection.) Let $(v_j)$ be bounded by $R$ in $H^r$. Put $S_0=\mathbb N$. For each $n\ge1$ let $M_n$ be the least integer $M\ge0$ for which $RC_r(1+M^2)^{-1/2}<2^{-n}/4$, with any $M_n=0$ if $R=0$. On every infinite index subset $S\subseteq\mathbb N$, the sequence $(P_{M_n}v_j)_{j\in S}$ has range with compact closure in the finite-dimensional space $X_{M_n}$ by [L2], so its range admits a finite cover by open $H^{r-1}$-balls of radius $2^{-n}/4$ centred at its own terms. Indeed compactness gives a finite cover by radius-$2^{-n}/8$ balls, and choosing one range term from each ball that meets the range enlarges these to the required balls (only finite choices). At least one required ball contains projected terms for infinitely many $j\in S$. Starting with $S=S_{n-1}$, let $\ell_n$ be the least index in $S_{n-1}$ whose centred ball has this property and define $S_n:=\{j\in S_{n-1}:\|P_{M_n}(v_j-v_{\ell_n})\|_{H^{r-1}}<2^{-n}/4\}$. This is an infinite nested subset, and for $j,l\in S_n$ the triangle inequality and the two tail bounds [L1] give $\|v_j-v_l\|_{H^{r-1}}<2^{-n}$. Let $k_n$ be the least index in $S_n$ greater than $k_{n-1}$, with $k_0=0$. Every such index exists. For $j,l\ge n$, $k_j,k_l\in S_n$, hence $(v_{k_n})$ is Cauchy in $H^{r-1}$ and converges by [L5]. All recursive selections use least natural-number indices; no dependent choice is needed. This proves (a).

(Equicontinuity (b).) For $t,t'\in(-T,T)$ the curve $s\mapsto u_N(s)$ is $C^1$ into the normed space $H^{s-1}$, so by [L4] $\|u_N(t)-u_N(t')\|_{H^{s-1}}\le\bigl|\int_{t'}^t\|\partial_tu_N(s)\|_{H^{s-1}}ds\bigr|\le C_R(1+R)|t-t'|$ by [L3]. This proves (b) with $C_0=C_R(1+R)$, a constant depending only on $A^\mu,B,K,R,s,[-T,T]$.

(Locally uniform subsequence (c).) Enumerate $\mathcal N$ in increasing order and apply [L7] to that sequence with $X_0:=H^{s-1}(\mathbb T^3_{2\pi};\mathbb R^m)$ and $X_1:=H^s(\mathbb T^3_{2\pi};\mathbb R^m)$: $X_0$ is complete by [L5], the inclusion bound $\|x\|_{X_0}\le\|x\|_{X_1}$ holds by [L1], property (ii) of [L7] is clause (a) with $r=s$ (legitimate since $s\ge5\ge1$), and the family $u_N$ satisfies the two bounds of [L7] by the hypothesis and step 1.2. The extraction lemma therefore yields a strictly increasing sequence $N_j\in\mathcal N$, $N_j\to\infty$ and a continuous $u:(-T,T)\to H^{s-1}$ with $u_{N_j}\to u$ uniformly on every compact subinterval of $(-T,T)$. This is (c).

Let $m\ge1$ and let $B\in\operatorname{Sym}_m(\mathbb R)$ be positive definite,
that is $B^{\mathsf T}=B$ and $z^{\mathsf T}Bz>0$ for every nonzero

**(a)** There are real numbers $0<a\le b$ with $a\,|z|^2\le z^{\mathsf T}Bz\le b\,|z|^2$
for every $z\in\mathbb R^m$; equivalently $aI\le B\le bI$ in the Loewner
order. They can be taken to be the least and largest eigenvalues of $B$.

**(b)** $B$ is invertible and $\tfrac1bI\le B^{-1}\le\tfrac1aI$, so in

**(c)** Let $\Lambda$ be a compact topological space and let

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$
([[def-countable-choice]]) for the quotient, product-measure and integration
clauses below, as in [[def-the-one-dimensional-torus-and-normalized-haar-integral]].

**(a) The 2 pi-periodic torus.** Let $\mathbb T_{2\pi}:=\mathbb R/2\pi\mathbb Z$
carry the quotient topology, and let
$$\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}:=\mathbb T_{2\pi}\times\mathbb T_{2\pi}\times\mathbb T_{2\pi}$$
with the product topology; write $q:\mathbb R^3\to\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}$ for the
quotient map and $[x]:=(x^1+2\pi\mathbb Z,x^2+2\pi\mathbb Z,x^3+2\pi\mathbb Z)$.
The map $[0,2\pi)^3\to\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}$, $x\mapsto[x]$, is a bijection. The
normalized product measure $\mu$ is $\mu_{\mathbb T}\otimes\mu_{\mathbb T}\otimes\mu_{\mathbb T}$,
where $\mu_{\mathbb T}$ is the normalized measure of
[[def-the-one-dimensional-torus-and-normalized-haar-integral]] transported by
$t\mapsto2\pi t$; it is a probability measure on the Borel sets of
$\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}$ and $\int f\,d\mu=(2\pi)^{-3}\int_{[0,2\pi)^3}f\circ q\,d\lambda_3$
for bounded measurable $f$ ([[thm-tonelli-theorem-for-sigma-finite-product-spaces]]).

**(b) Test functions and continuous classes.** For $N\ge1$ let
$C^\infty(\mathbb T^3_{2\pi};\mathbb R^N)$ be the set of compositions
$u\circ q$ of smooth maps $u:\mathbb R^3\to\mathbb R^N$ that are $2\pi$-periodic
in each variable; these are the **smooth test functions** (real-valued when
$N=1$). For $m\ge0$ let $C^m(\mathbb T^3_{2\pi};\mathbb R^N)$ be the set of
$u\circ q$ with $u\in C^m(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb R^N)$ $2\pi$-periodic in each
variable ([[def-c-r-and-smooth-maps-between-smooth-manifolds]]), with
$$\|u\|_{C^m}:=\max_{|\alpha|\le m}\ \sup_{x\in\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}}\bigl|(D^\alpha u)(x)\bigr| ,$$
where $D^\alpha$ is the multi-index derivative of
[[def-ck-and-multi-index-notation-in-several-variables]] applied to any
periodic representative; the displayed expression is independent of the
representative.

**(c) The Hilbert space $L^2$.** For $N\ge1$ let
$L^2(\mathbb T^3_{2\pi};\mathbb R^N)$ be the quotient of the set of measurable
$u$ with $\int|u|^2\,d\mu<\infty$ by the $\mu$-a.e. zero functions
([[def-l-p-space-as-a-quotient-by-null-functions]],
[[thm-the-l-p-norm-descends-to-the-quotient-and-makes-l-p-a-normed-space]]),
with inner product $\langle u,v\rangle_2=\int u\cdot v\,d\mu$ and norm
$\|u\|_2=\langle u,u\rangle_2^{1/2}$; it is a real Hilbert space
([[lem-l-two-with-the-integral-pairing-is-a-hilbert-space]]). For
$u\in L^2(\mathbb T^3_{2\pi};\mathbb R^N)$ and $k\in\mathbb Z^3$ the
**$k$-th Fourier coefficient** is the vector
$$\widehat u(k):=\int_{\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}}u(x)\,e^{-ik\cdot x}\,d\mu(x)\in\mathbb C^N ,$$
where $e^{-ik\cdot x}:=\chi_{-k}$ with $\chi_k([x]):=\exp(i\,k\cdot x)$; here
$u$ is read through any representative. Write $\chi_k:\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}\to\mathbb C$,
$k\in\mathbb Z^3$, for these **characters**; under the identification
$x=2\pi y$ they are the characters $\exp(2\pi i\,k\cdot y)$ of
[[thm-fourier-basis-and-parseval-on-the-n-torus]], so $(\chi_k)_{k\in\mathbb Z^3}$
is an orthonormal basis of the complex space $L^2(\mathbb T^3_{2\pi};\mathbb C)$.

**(d) Weak derivatives and the periodic Sobolev spaces.** For
$u,v\in L^1(\mathbb T^3_{2\pi};\mathbb R)$ and $\alpha\in\mathbb N_0^3$ say that
$v$ is the **weak derivative** $D^\alpha u$ if
$$\int_{\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}}u\,D^\alpha\varphi\,d\mu=(-1)^{|\alpha|}\int_{\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}}v\,\varphi\,d\mu$$
for every $\varphi\in C^\infty(\mathbb T^3_{2\pi};\mathbb R)$, where $D^\alpha\varphi$
is the multi-index derivative of the periodic representative
([[def-weak-derivative-of-a-locally-integrable-function]] records the
Euclidean analogue). For an integer $s\ge0$ let
$$H^s(\mathbb T^3_{2\pi};\mathbb R^N):=\Bigl\{u\in L^2(\mathbb T^3_{2\pi};\mathbb R^N):\ \text{for every }|\alpha|\le s\text{ there is }v_\alpha\in L^2(\mathbb T^3_{2\pi};\mathbb R^N)\text{ with }v_\alpha=D^\alpha u\Bigr\},$$
the vector-valued weak derivative being componentwise, and put
$$\|u\|_{H^s}:=\Bigl(\sum_{|\alpha|\le s}\|D^\alpha u\|_2^2\Bigr)^{1/2}.$$
The classes $L^2\subseteq L^1$ on the probability space, so the integrals in the
test identity are finite: $|\int u\,D^\alpha\varphi\,d\mu|\le\|u\|_2\|D^\alpha\varphi\|_2$
by Cauchy--Schwarz. The definition asserts neither that the weak derivative
exists nor that the two norms compared in the next item are equivalent; those
are proved in [[lem-gr-periodic-fourier-differentiation-and-norm-equivalence]].

**(e) Conventions.** $O\subseteq\mathbb R^m$ open, $I\subseteq\mathbb R$ an
interval and maps $F:I\times\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}\times O\to\mathbb R^{m'}$ are
called smooth when their representatives $F(t,q(x),u)=G(t,x,u)$ have
$G\in C^\infty$. Throughout this page the torus is always this
$2\pi$-periodic one; a statement "for every $x$" means for every point of
$\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}$, and "a.e." means $\mu$-a.e.

derivations.claim: (Equivalence (a).) For each $|\alpha|\le s$ the integrand $(D^\alpha u_N)^{\mathsf T}A^0D^\alpha u_N$ lies between $a|D^\alpha u_N|^2$ and $b|D^\alpha u_N|^2$ pointwise by [L1]; integrating and summing over $\alpha$ gives $a\|u_N\|_{H^s}^2\le e\le b\|u_N\|_{H^s}^2$.

(Substituting the Galerkin equation into $e'$.) For each $|\alpha|\le s$ use $D^\alpha u_N\in X_N$ and self-adjoint commutativity [L2]: $\int(D^\alpha u_N)^{\mathsf T}A^0D^\alpha\partial_tu_N=\int(D^\alpha u_N)^{\mathsf T}D^\alpha(A^0\partial_tu_N)-\int(D^\alpha u_N)^{\mathsf T}[D^\alpha,A^0]\partial_tu_N$ and $\int(D^\alpha u_N)^{\mathsf T}P_ND^\alpha(A^0\partial_tu_N)=-\int(D^\alpha u_N)^{\mathsf T}D^\alpha(A^i\partial_iu_N+B)$ by the Galerkin equation and self-adjointness. Substituting into [L4] and splitting $D^\alpha(A^i\partial_iu_N)=A^iD^\alpha\partial_iu_N+[D^\alpha,A^i]\partial_iu_N$, the symmetric term integrates by parts on the torus: $\int(D^\alpha u_N)^{\mathsf T}A^iD^\alpha\partial_iu_N=-\tfrac12\int(D^\alpha u_N)^{\mathsf T}(\partial_iA^i)(D^\alpha u_N)$. Hence $e'(t)=\sum_{|\alpha|\le s}\bigl[-2\int(D^\alpha u_N)^{\mathsf T}[D^\alpha,A^0]\partial_tu_N-2\int(D^\alpha u_N)^{\mathsf T}[D^\alpha,A^i]\partial_iu_N+\int(D^\alpha u_N)^{\mathsf T}(\partial_iA^i)D^\alpha u_N-2\int(D^\alpha u_N)^{\mathsf T}D^\alpha B+\int(D^\alpha u_N)^{\mathsf T}(\dot A^0)D^\alpha u_N\bigr]$.

(Bounding the terms by $1+e$.) Each of the five sums is bounded using Cauchy--Schwarz and [L3]: $\bigl|\int(D^\alpha u_N)^{\mathsf T}[D^\alpha,A^0]\partial_tu_N\bigr|\le\|D^\alpha u_N\|_2\,C_R\|\partial_tu_N\|_{H^{s-1}}\le C_R(1+\|u_N\|_{H^s})\|D^\alpha u_N\|_2$; similarly for the spatial commutators with $\|\partial_iu_N\|_{H^{s-1}}\le\|u_N\|_{H^s}$; the $\partial_iA^i$ and $\dot A^0$ terms are bounded by a constant times $\|D^\alpha u_N\|_2^2$; and $\bigl|\int(D^\alpha u_N)^{\mathsf T}D^\alpha B\bigr|\le C_R(1+\|u_N\|_{H^s})\|D^\alpha u_N\|_2$. Summing over $|\alpha|\le s$, using Young's inequality [L5] and $\|u_N\|^2_{H^s}\le a^{-1}e$ from step 1.1, gives $|e'|\le C(1+e)$ with $C=C(A^\mu,B,K,R,s,I_0)$.

(Gronwall consequence.) By step 1.1 and step 2.1, $e(t)\le(1+e(t_0))e^{C|t-t_0|}$ on every interval where the bounds hold, by Gronwall's integral inequality ([[thm-gronwall-integral-inequality]]); this uses only $|e'|\le C(1+e)$ and the differentiability of $e$ from [L4].

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$
([[def-countable-choice]]). Let integers $s\ge m\ge0$ satisfy $s-m>3/2$, and
let $u\in H^s(\mathbb T^3_{2\pi};\mathbb R^N)$ with the objects and notation of
[[def-gr-periodic-torus-and-sobolev-spaces]]. Then:

**(a)** There is a unique representative $u^*\in C^m(\mathbb T^3_{2\pi};\mathbb R^N)$
of the class $u$, and for every $|\alpha|\le m$ the series
$\sum_{k\in\mathbb Z^3}(ik)^\alpha\widehat u(k)\chi_k$ converges absolutely and
uniformly on $\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}$ to $D^\alpha u^*$; moreover there is
$C=C(s,m,N)$ with
$$\|u^*\|_{C^m}\le C\,\|u\|_{H^s}.$$

**(b)** Writing $d(x,y):=\min\{\,|x-y+2\pi l|:l\in\mathbb Z^3\,\}$ for the
induced metric on $\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}$ and fixing
$0<\theta\le\min\{1,s-m-\tfrac32\}$, there is $C'=C'(s,m,N,\theta)$ with
$$\bigl|D^\alpha u^*(x)-D^\alpha u^*(y)\bigr|\le C'\,\|u\|_{H^s}\,d(x,y)^\theta\qquad(x,y\in\mathbb T^3_{2\pi},\ |\alpha|\le m).$$

**(c)** The assignment $u\mapsto u^*$ is linear; and if $(u_j)$ is a sequence in
$H^s$ with $u_j\to u$ in $H^s$, then $u_j^*\to u^*$ uniformly together with all
derivatives of order at most $m$.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$
([[def-countable-choice]]) for the quotient, product-measure and integration
clauses below, as in [[def-the-one-dimensional-torus-and-normalized-haar-integral]].

**(a) The 2 pi-periodic torus.** Let $\mathbb T_{2\pi}:=\mathbb R/2\pi\mathbb Z$
carry the quotient topology, and let
$$\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}:=\mathbb T_{2\pi}\times\mathbb T_{2\pi}\times\mathbb T_{2\pi}$$
with the product topology; write $q:\mathbb R^3\to\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}$ for the
quotient map and $[x]:=(x^1+2\pi\mathbb Z,x^2+2\pi\mathbb Z,x^3+2\pi\mathbb Z)$.
The map $[0,2\pi)^3\to\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}$, $x\mapsto[x]$, is a bijection. The
normalized product measure $\mu$ is $\mu_{\mathbb T}\otimes\mu_{\mathbb T}\otimes\mu_{\mathbb T}$,
where $\mu_{\mathbb T}$ is the normalized measure of
[[def-the-one-dimensional-torus-and-normalized-haar-integral]] transported by
$t\mapsto2\pi t$; it is a probability measure on the Borel sets of
$\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}$ and $\int f\,d\mu=(2\pi)^{-3}\int_{[0,2\pi)^3}f\circ q\,d\lambda_3$
for bounded measurable $f$ ([[thm-tonelli-theorem-for-sigma-finite-product-spaces]]).

**(b) Test functions and continuous classes.** For $N\ge1$ let
$C^\infty(\mathbb T^3_{2\pi};\mathbb R^N)$ be the set of compositions
$u\circ q$ of smooth maps $u:\mathbb R^3\to\mathbb R^N$ that are $2\pi$-periodic
in each variable; these are the **smooth test functions** (real-valued when
$N=1$). For $m\ge0$ let $C^m(\mathbb T^3_{2\pi};\mathbb R^N)$ be the set of
$u\circ q$ with $u\in C^m(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb R^N)$ $2\pi$-periodic in each
variable ([[def-c-r-and-smooth-maps-between-smooth-manifolds]]), with
$$\|u\|_{C^m}:=\max_{|\alpha|\le m}\ \sup_{x\in\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}}\bigl|(D^\alpha u)(x)\bigr| ,$$
where $D^\alpha$ is the multi-index derivative of
[[def-ck-and-multi-index-notation-in-several-variables]] applied to any
periodic representative; the displayed expression is independent of the
representative.

**(c) The Hilbert space $L^2$.** For $N\ge1$ let
$L^2(\mathbb T^3_{2\pi};\mathbb R^N)$ be the quotient of the set of measurable
$u$ with $\int|u|^2\,d\mu<\infty$ by the $\mu$-a.e. zero functions
([[def-l-p-space-as-a-quotient-by-null-functions]],
[[thm-the-l-p-norm-descends-to-the-quotient-and-makes-l-p-a-normed-space]]),
with inner product $\langle u,v\rangle_2=\int u\cdot v\,d\mu$ and norm
$\|u\|_2=\langle u,u\rangle_2^{1/2}$; it is a real Hilbert space
([[lem-l-two-with-the-integral-pairing-is-a-hilbert-space]]). For
$u\in L^2(\mathbb T^3_{2\pi};\mathbb R^N)$ and $k\in\mathbb Z^3$ the
**$k$-th Fourier coefficient** is the vector
$$\widehat u(k):=\int_{\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}}u(x)\,e^{-ik\cdot x}\,d\mu(x)\in\mathbb C^N ,$$
where $e^{-ik\cdot x}:=\chi_{-k}$ with $\chi_k([x]):=\exp(i\,k\cdot x)$; here
$u$ is read through any representative. Write $\chi_k:\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}\to\mathbb C$,
$k\in\mathbb Z^3$, for these **characters**; under the identification
$x=2\pi y$ they are the characters $\exp(2\pi i\,k\cdot y)$ of
[[thm-fourier-basis-and-parseval-on-the-n-torus]], so $(\chi_k)_{k\in\mathbb Z^3}$
is an orthonormal basis of the complex space $L^2(\mathbb T^3_{2\pi};\mathbb C)$.

**(d) Weak derivatives and the periodic Sobolev spaces.** For
$u,v\in L^1(\mathbb T^3_{2\pi};\mathbb R)$ and $\alpha\in\mathbb N_0^3$ say that
$v$ is the **weak derivative** $D^\alpha u$ if
$$\int_{\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}}u\,D^\alpha\varphi\,d\mu=(-1)^{|\alpha|}\int_{\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}}v\,\varphi\,d\mu$$
for every $\varphi\in C^\infty(\mathbb T^3_{2\pi};\mathbb R)$, where $D^\alpha\varphi$
is the multi-index derivative of the periodic representative
([[def-weak-derivative-of-a-locally-integrable-function]] records the
Euclidean analogue). For an integer $s\ge0$ let
$$H^s(\mathbb T^3_{2\pi};\mathbb R^N):=\Bigl\{u\in L^2(\mathbb T^3_{2\pi};\mathbb R^N):\ \text{for every }|\alpha|\le s\text{ there is }v_\alpha\in L^2(\mathbb T^3_{2\pi};\mathbb R^N)\text{ with }v_\alpha=D^\alpha u\Bigr\},$$
the vector-valued weak derivative being componentwise, and put
$$\|u\|_{H^s}:=\Bigl(\sum_{|\alpha|\le s}\|D^\alpha u\|_2^2\Bigr)^{1/2}.$$
The classes $L^2\subseteq L^1$ on the probability space, so the integrals in the
test identity are finite: $|\int u\,D^\alpha\varphi\,d\mu|\le\|u\|_2\|D^\alpha\varphi\|_2$
by Cauchy--Schwarz. The definition asserts neither that the weak derivative
exists nor that the two norms compared in the next item are equivalent; those
are proved in [[lem-gr-periodic-fourier-differentiation-and-norm-equivalence]].

**(e) Conventions.** $O\subseteq\mathbb R^m$ open, $I\subseteq\mathbb R$ an
interval and maps $F:I\times\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}\times O\to\mathbb R^{m'}$ are
called smooth when their representatives $F(t,q(x),u)=G(t,x,u)$ have
$G\in C^\infty$. Throughout this page the torus is always this
$2\pi$-periodic one; a statement "for every $x$" means for every point of
$\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}$, and "a.e." means $\mu$-a.e.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$
([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $s\ge5$, let $O\subseteq\mathbb R^m$ be open,
let $A^\mu,B$ be a periodic symmetric hyperbolic coefficient family on $O$ over
an open interval $I\ni0$ ([[def-gr-periodic-symmetric-hyperbolic-system]]), let
$u_0\in H^s(\mathbb T^3_{2\pi};\mathbb R^m)$ take values in a compact
$K\subseteq O$ with $\|u_0\|_{H^s}\le R$, and let $P_N$, $X_N$ be the Galerkin
projection and space ([[def-gr-galerkin-fourier-projection]]). Fix $N\ge0$ for which $P_Nu_0$ takes values in $O$. Then:

**(a)** there is an open interval $J_N\ni0$ and a $C^1$ map $u_N:J_N\to X_N$
such that for all $t\in J_N$
$$P_N\Bigl[A^0(t,\cdot,u_N(t))\,\partial_tu_N(t)+\sum_{i=1}^3A^i(t,\cdot,u_N(t))\,\partial_iu_N(t)+B(t,\cdot,u_N(t))\Bigr]=0\quad\text{in }L^2,$$
with $u_N(0)=P_Nu_0$;

**(b)** [continuation criterion] if $[0,T_*)$ is the forward-maximal interval of
existence of $u_N$ and there are a compact $C\subseteq O$ and a constant
$R_1\ge0$ with $u_N(t)$ taking values in $C$ and $\|u_N(t)\|_{H^s}\le R_1$ for
all $t\in[0,T_*)$, and $T_*\in I$, then $u_N$ does not have $T_*$ as a finite forward endpoint:
the solution extends beyond $T_*$;

**(c)** the solution is unique and its local flow depends smoothly on the
finite-dimensional coordinates of the initial data.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$
([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $m\ge1$, $N\ge0$, and let $P_N$ be the Galerkin
projection and $X_N$ the Galerkin space of [[def-gr-galerkin-fourier-projection]]
on $\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}$. Then:

**(a)** $P_N$ is linear on $L^2(\mathbb T^3_{2\pi};\mathbb R^m)$, self-adjoint
($\langle P_Nu,v\rangle_2=\langle u,P_Nv\rangle_2$ for all $u,v\in L^2$) and
idempotent ($P_N^2=P_N$), with range $X_N$ and kernel the classes with vanishing
coefficients on $\Lambda_N$;

**(b)** for every multi-index $\alpha$ with $|\alpha|\le s$ and every
$u\in H^s$, $P_ND^\alpha u=D^\alpha P_Nu$;

**(c)** for every $0\le r\le s$ and every $u\in H^r$,
$\|P_Nu\|_{H^r}\le\|u\|_{H^r}$;

**(d)** for every $0\le r\le s$ and every $u\in H^r$, $P_Nu\to u$ in $H^r$ as
$N\to\infty$;

**(e)** for every $s\ge1$, every $u\in H^s$ and every $N\ge0$,
$$\|u-P_Nu\|_{H^{s-1}}\le C_s\,(1+N^2)^{-1/2}\,\|u\|_{H^s}$$
with $C_s$ depending only on $s$.

Let $m\ge1$ and let $B\in\operatorname{Sym}_m(\mathbb R)$ be positive definite,
that is $B^{\mathsf T}=B$ and $z^{\mathsf T}Bz>0$ for every nonzero
$z\in\mathbb R^m$ with the standard coordinate inner product.

**(a)** There are real numbers $0<a\le b$ with $a\,|z|^2\le z^{\mathsf T}Bz\le b\,|z|^2$
for every $z\in\mathbb R^m$; equivalently $aI\le B\le bI$ in the Loewner
order. They can be taken to be the least and largest eigenvalues of $B$.

**(b)** $B$ is invertible and $\tfrac1bI\le B^{-1}\le\tfrac1aI$, so in
particular $\|B^{-1}z\|\le a^{-1}\|z\|$.

**(c)** Let $\Lambda$ be a compact topological space and let
$B:\Lambda\to\operatorname{Sym}_m(\mathbb R)$ be continuous with $B(\lambda)$
positive definite for every $\lambda\in\Lambda$. Then there are constants
$0<a\le b$ with $aI\le B(\lambda)\le bI$ for every $\lambda\in\Lambda$.

**(d)** Let $D\subseteq\mathbb R^p$ be open and let $B:D\to\operatorname{Sym}_m(\mathbb R)$
be smooth with $B(x)\ge aI$ for a constant $a>0$ and all $x\in D$. Then
$x\mapsto B(x)^{-1}$ is smooth on $D$ and $B(x)^{-1}\le a^{-1}I$ there.

Assume Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $s\ge5$, let $O\subseteq\mathbb R^m$ be open, let $I$ be an open time interval, let $I_0\subseteq I$ be a compact interval, and let $F:I\times\mathbb T^3\times O\to\mathbb R^{m'}$ and $A:I\times\mathbb T^3\times O\to M_{m'}(\mathbb R)$ be smooth. Fix compact $K\subseteq O$ and $R\ge0$. Constants below depend on these data and are uniform in $t\in I_0$. For $u,v\in H^s$ with values in $K$ and norms at most $R$:

**(a)** $\|F(t,\cdot,u)\|_{H^j}\le C(1+\|u\|_{H^s})$ for $0\le j\le s$.

**(b)** $\|F(t,\cdot,u)-F(t,\cdot,v)\|_{H^{s-1}}\le C\|u-v\|_{H^{s-1}}$. The same bound holds at order zero.

**(c)** For $1\le j=|\alpha|\le s-1$, $\|[D^\alpha,A(t,\cdot,u)]w\|_2\le C\|w\|_{H^{j-1}}$. For $|\alpha|=s$, $\|[D^\alpha,A(t,\cdot,u)]w\|_2\le C\|w\|_{H^{s-1}}$. Commutators are interpreted distributionally by their Leibniz expansion, even if the two individual order-$j$ terms are not separately in $L^2$.

**(d)** For $0\le j\le s-1$, $\|A(t,\cdot,u)w\|_{H^j}\le C\|w\|_{H^j}$.

**(e)** Let $n\ge6$, $\rho\ge0$ and $z\in H^n$ with values in $K$ and $\|z\|_{H^{n-1}}\le\rho$. Then $\|F(t,\cdot,z)\|_{H^n}\le C_\rho(1+\|z\|_{H^n})$. Moreover for $w\in H^{n-1}$ and $|\alpha|\le n$,
$$\|[D^\alpha,A(t,\cdot,z)]w\|_2\le C_\rho\bigl(\|w\|_{H^{n-1}}+(1+\|z\|_{H^n})\|w\|_{H^{n-2}}\bigr).$$
The same estimates apply to any smooth coefficient obtained from $F,A$ by differentiation or by a smooth matrix inverse where that inverse exists on a neighborhood of $I_0\times\mathbb T^3\times K$.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$
([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $s\ge5$, fix a compact interval $I_0$ inside the coefficient time domain, and assume $J\subseteq I_0$. Let $A^\mu,B$ be a periodic symmetric
hyperbolic coefficient family on the open set $O\subseteq\mathbb R^m$
([[def-gr-periodic-symmetric-hyperbolic-system]]), let $K\subseteq O$ be compact
and $R\ge0$, and let $u_N:J\to X_N$ be a Galerkin solution of
[[lem-gr-galerkin-ode-local-solution]] for some $N\ge0$. Suppose that
$u_N(t)$ takes values in $K$ and satisfies $\|u_N(t)\|_{H^s}\le R$ for every
$t\in J$. Then there is $C=C(A^\mu,B,K,R,s,I_0)$ such that for every
$0\le j\le s-1$ and every $t\in J$
$$\|\partial_tu_N(t)\|_{H^j}\le C\,\bigl(1+\|u_N(t)\|_{H^s}\bigr).$$

Assume Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $s\ge5$, let $I_0$ be a compact interval inside the coefficient time domain, and let $K\subseteq O$ be compact. Let $u_N:J\to X_N$ be a Galerkin solution, with $J\subseteq I_0$, values in $K$ and $\|u_N\|_{H^s}\le R$. Then, uniformly in $N$,
$$\|\partial_t^2u_N(t)\|_{H^{s-2}}\le C(A^\mu,B,K,R,s,I_0),$$
and consequently
$$\|\partial_tu_N(t)-\partial_tu_N(t')\|_{H^{s-2}}\le C(A^\mu,B,K,R,s,I_0)|t-t'|.$$
No convexity of $K$ is required.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$
([[def-countable-choice]]).

**(a)** For every integer $r\ge1$, every $R\ge0$ and every sequence $(v_j)$
in $H^r(\mathbb T^3_{2\pi};\mathbb R^m)$ with $\|v_j\|_{H^r}\le R$ there is a
subsequence converging in $H^{r-1}(\mathbb T^3_{2\pi};\mathbb R^m)$.

**(b)** Let $s\ge5$, $R\ge0$, $T>0$ with the compact slab $[-T,T]$ contained in the coefficient time domain $I$, let $K\subseteq O$ be compact, and let
$u_N:(-T,T)\to X_N$ ($N\in\mathcal N$), where $\mathcal N\subseteq\mathbb N_0$ is any infinite set of Fourier cutoffs be a family of Galerkin solutions with
$u_N(t)$ taking values in $K$ and $\|u_N(t)\|_{H^s}\le R$ for all $t$. Then the
family is equicontinuous in the $H^{s-1}$ metric: there is
$C_0=C_0(A^\mu,B,K,R,s,[-T,T])$ with
$$\|u_N(t)-u_N(t')\|_{H^{s-1}}\le C_0\,|t-t'|\qquad(t,t'\in(-T,T),\ N\in\mathcal N).$$

**(c)** Under the hypotheses of (b) there are a strictly increasing sequence
$N_j\in\mathcal N$, $N_j\to\infty$ and $u\in C^0((-T,T);H^{s-1}(\mathbb T^3_{2\pi};\mathbb R^m))$
with $u_{N_j}\to u$ uniformly on every compact subinterval of $(-T,T)$ in the
$H^{s-1}$ norm.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$
([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $s\ge0$ be an integer and $N\ge1$, write
$H^s=H^s(\mathbb T^3_{2\pi};\mathbb R^N)$ for the periodic Sobolev space with
its norm $\|\cdot\|_{H^s}$ and Fourier coefficients
$\widehat u(k)\in\mathbb C^N$ of [[def-gr-periodic-torus-and-sobolev-spaces]],
and put
$$N_s(u)^2:=\sum_{k\in\mathbb Z^3}(1+|k|^2)^s\,|\widehat u(k)|^2\le+\infty .$$
Then:

**(a)** every Cauchy sequence in $(H^s,\|\cdot\|_{H^s})$ converges in
$(H^s,\|\cdot\|_{H^s})$; that is, $H^s$ is a real Banach space;

**(b)** more precisely, for every Cauchy sequence $(u_n)$ in $H^s$ there is
$u\in H^s$ with $N_s(u_n-u)\to0$, and then
$\|u_n-u\|_{H^s}\le C_s^{1/2}N_s(u_n-u)\to0$, where $C_s$ is the constant of
clause (b) of
[[lem-gr-periodic-fourier-differentiation-and-norm-equivalence]]; this $u$ is
the unique limit of $(u_n)$.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$
([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $X_0$ be a complete normed space over
$\mathbb R$ or $\mathbb C$ ([[def-banach-space]],
[[def-complete-metric-space]]) and let $X_1\subseteq X_0$ be a linear subspace
carrying a norm $\|\cdot\|_1$ such that ([[def-normed-subspace]]):

**(i)** there is $\kappa\ge0$ with $\|x\|_0\le\kappa\|x\|_1$ for every
$x\in X_1$; and

**(ii)** every sequence in $X_1$ bounded in $\|\cdot\|_1$ has a subsequence
converging in $X_0$ ([[def-metric-convergence]]).

Let $T>0$, $R\ge0$, $C\ge0$, and for $j\in\mathbb N$ let
$f_j:(-T,T)\to X_1$ satisfy
$$\|f_j(t)\|_1\le R,\qquad \|f_j(t)-f_j(t')\|_0\le C\,|t-t'|\qquad(t,t'\in(-T,T),\ j\in\mathbb N).$$

Then there are a strictly increasing sequence $j_1<j_2<\cdots$ in $\mathbb N$
and a continuous map $f:(-T,T)\to X_0$ ([[def-continuous-map-top]]) such that
$f_{j_n}\to f$ uniformly on every compact subinterval of $(-T,T)$; moreover
$\|f(t)-f(t')\|_0\le C\,|t-t'|$ for all $t,t'\in(-T,T)$.

Assume Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]) for the Lebesgue-measure interfaces. Let $X$ be a real or complex Banach space, let $a<b$, and let $f:[a,b]\to X$ be continuous. Differentiation uses the underlying real structure. Then $G(t):=\int_a^t f(s)\,ds$ is differentiable on $(a,b)$ and has the corresponding one-sided derivatives at $a,b$, with $G'(t)=f(t)$, and this derivative extends continuously to $[a,b]$. Consequently, if $\varphi:[a,b]\to X$ is continuous, differentiable on $(a,b)$ with $\varphi'$ continuous on $(a,b)$ and extendable to a continuous $X$-valued function on $[a,b]$, then $\int_a^b\varphi'(s)\,ds=\varphi(b)-\varphi(a)$. The Bochner integral here is the one of [[def-bochner-integrable-function]]; the identities also hold for continuous curves on $[0,\infty)$ restricted to compact subintervals.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$
([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}$, $\mu$, $\chi_k$,
$\widehat u(k)$, the weak derivatives $D^\alpha$ and the spaces
$H^s(\mathbb T^3_{2\pi};\mathbb R^N)$ be as in
[[def-gr-periodic-torus-and-sobolev-spaces]], and put
$$N_s(u)^2:=\sum_{k\in\mathbb Z^3}(1+|k|^2)^s\,|\widehat u(k)|^2,\qquad |k|^2:=k_1^2+k_2^2+k_3^2 .$$

**(a)** Let $u\in H^s$ and let $\alpha\in\mathbb N_0^3$ with $|\alpha|\le s$. Then
$D^\alpha u\in H^{s-|\alpha|}$ and
$$\widehat{D^\alpha u}(k)=(ik)^\alpha\,\widehat u(k)\qquad(k\in\mathbb Z^3),\qquad (ik)^\alpha:=\prod_{j=1}^3(ik_j)^{\alpha_j}.$$

**(b)** Let $u\in L^2(\mathbb T^3_{2\pi};\mathbb R^N)$ satisfy $N_s(u)<\infty$.
Then $u\in H^s(\mathbb T^3_{2\pi};\mathbb R^N)$, and there are constants
$0<c_s\le C_s<\infty$, depending only on $s$, such that
$$c_s\,N_s(u)^2\le\|u\|_{H^s}^2\le C_s\,N_s(u)^2 .$$
The right-hand inequality holds for every $u\in H^s$, so the two norms are
equivalent on $H^s$.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$
([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $m\ge1$, $N\ge0$, and let $P_N$ be the Galerkin
projection and $X_N$ the Galerkin space of [[def-gr-galerkin-fourier-projection]]
on $\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}$. Then:

**(a)** $P_N$ is linear on $L^2(\mathbb T^3_{2\pi};\mathbb R^m)$, self-adjoint
($\langle P_Nu,v\rangle_2=\langle u,P_Nv\rangle_2$ for all $u,v\in L^2$) and
idempotent ($P_N^2=P_N$), with range $X_N$ and kernel the classes with vanishing
coefficients on $\Lambda_N$;

**(b)** for every multi-index $\alpha$ with $|\alpha|\le s$ and every
$u\in H^s$, $P_ND^\alpha u=D^\alpha P_Nu$;

**(c)** for every $0\le r\le s$ and every $u\in H^r$,
$\|P_Nu\|_{H^r}\le\|u\|_{H^r}$;

**(d)** for every $0\le r\le s$ and every $u\in H^r$, $P_Nu\to u$ in $H^r$ as
$N\to\infty$;

**(e)** for every $s\ge1$, every $u\in H^s$ and every $N\ge0$,
$$\|u-P_Nu\|_{H^{s-1}}\le C_s\,(1+N^2)^{-1/2}\,\|u\|_{H^s}$$
with $C_s$ depending only on $s$.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$
([[def-countable-choice]]) for the quotient, product-measure and integration
clauses below, as in [[def-the-one-dimensional-torus-and-normalized-haar-integral]].

**(a) The 2 pi-periodic torus.** Let $\mathbb T_{2\pi}:=\mathbb R/2\pi\mathbb Z$
carry the quotient topology, and let
$$\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}:=\mathbb T_{2\pi}\times\mathbb T_{2\pi}\times\mathbb T_{2\pi}$$
with the product topology; write $q:\mathbb R^3\to\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}$ for the
quotient map and $[x]:=(x^1+2\pi\mathbb Z,x^2+2\pi\mathbb Z,x^3+2\pi\mathbb Z)$.
The map $[0,2\pi)^3\to\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}$, $x\mapsto[x]$, is a bijection. The
normalized product measure $\mu$ is $\mu_{\mathbb T}\otimes\mu_{\mathbb T}\otimes\mu_{\mathbb T}$,
where $\mu_{\mathbb T}$ is the normalized measure of
[[def-the-one-dimensional-torus-and-normalized-haar-integral]] transported by
$t\mapsto2\pi t$; it is a probability measure on the Borel sets of
$\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}$ and $\int f\,d\mu=(2\pi)^{-3}\int_{[0,2\pi)^3}f\circ q\,d\lambda_3$
for bounded measurable $f$ ([[thm-tonelli-theorem-for-sigma-finite-product-spaces]]).

**(b) Test functions and continuous classes.** For $N\ge1$ let
$C^\infty(\mathbb T^3_{2\pi};\mathbb R^N)$ be the set of compositions
$u\circ q$ of smooth maps $u:\mathbb R^3\to\mathbb R^N$ that are $2\pi$-periodic
in each variable; these are the **smooth test functions** (real-valued when
$N=1$). For $m\ge0$ let $C^m(\mathbb T^3_{2\pi};\mathbb R^N)$ be the set of
$u\circ q$ with $u\in C^m(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb R^N)$ $2\pi$-periodic in each
variable ([[def-c-r-and-smooth-maps-between-smooth-manifolds]]), with
$$\|u\|_{C^m}:=\max_{|\alpha|\le m}\ \sup_{x\in\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}}\bigl|(D^\alpha u)(x)\bigr| ,$$
where $D^\alpha$ is the multi-index derivative of
[[def-ck-and-multi-index-notation-in-several-variables]] applied to any
periodic representative; the displayed expression is independent of the
representative.

**(c) The Hilbert space $L^2$.** For $N\ge1$ let
$L^2(\mathbb T^3_{2\pi};\mathbb R^N)$ be the quotient of the set of measurable
$u$ with $\int|u|^2\,d\mu<\infty$ by the $\mu$-a.e. zero functions
([[def-l-p-space-as-a-quotient-by-null-functions]],
[[thm-the-l-p-norm-descends-to-the-quotient-and-makes-l-p-a-normed-space]]),
with inner product $\langle u,v\rangle_2=\int u\cdot v\,d\mu$ and norm
$\|u\|_2=\langle u,u\rangle_2^{1/2}$; it is a real Hilbert space
([[lem-l-two-with-the-integral-pairing-is-a-hilbert-space]]). For
$u\in L^2(\mathbb T^3_{2\pi};\mathbb R^N)$ and $k\in\mathbb Z^3$ the
**$k$-th Fourier coefficient** is the vector
$$\widehat u(k):=\int_{\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}}u(x)\,e^{-ik\cdot x}\,d\mu(x)\in\mathbb C^N ,$$
where $e^{-ik\cdot x}:=\chi_{-k}$ with $\chi_k([x]):=\exp(i\,k\cdot x)$; here
$u$ is read through any representative. Write $\chi_k:\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}\to\mathbb C$,
$k\in\mathbb Z^3$, for these **characters**; under the identification
$x=2\pi y$ they are the characters $\exp(2\pi i\,k\cdot y)$ of
[[thm-fourier-basis-and-parseval-on-the-n-torus]], so $(\chi_k)_{k\in\mathbb Z^3}$
is an orthonormal basis of the complex space $L^2(\mathbb T^3_{2\pi};\mathbb C)$.

**(d) Weak derivatives and the periodic Sobolev spaces.** For
$u,v\in L^1(\mathbb T^3_{2\pi};\mathbb R)$ and $\alpha\in\mathbb N_0^3$ say that
$v$ is the **weak derivative** $D^\alpha u$ if
$$\int_{\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}}u\,D^\alpha\varphi\,d\mu=(-1)^{|\alpha|}\int_{\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}}v\,\varphi\,d\mu$$
for every $\varphi\in C^\infty(\mathbb T^3_{2\pi};\mathbb R)$, where $D^\alpha\varphi$
is the multi-index derivative of the periodic representative
([[def-weak-derivative-of-a-locally-integrable-function]] records the
Euclidean analogue). For an integer $s\ge0$ let
$$H^s(\mathbb T^3_{2\pi};\mathbb R^N):=\Bigl\{u\in L^2(\mathbb T^3_{2\pi};\mathbb R^N):\ \text{for every }|\alpha|\le s\text{ there is }v_\alpha\in L^2(\mathbb T^3_{2\pi};\mathbb R^N)\text{ with }v_\alpha=D^\alpha u\Bigr\},$$
the vector-valued weak derivative being componentwise, and put
$$\|u\|_{H^s}:=\Bigl(\sum_{|\alpha|\le s}\|D^\alpha u\|_2^2\Bigr)^{1/2}.$$
The classes $L^2\subseteq L^1$ on the probability space, so the integrals in the
test identity are finite: $|\int u\,D^\alpha\varphi\,d\mu|\le\|u\|_2\|D^\alpha\varphi\|_2$
by Cauchy--Schwarz. The definition asserts neither that the weak derivative
exists nor that the two norms compared in the next item are equivalent; those
are proved in [[lem-gr-periodic-fourier-differentiation-and-norm-equivalence]].

**(e) Conventions.** $O\subseteq\mathbb R^m$ open, $I\subseteq\mathbb R$ an
interval and maps $F:I\times\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}\times O\to\mathbb R^{m'}$ are
called smooth when their representatives $F(t,q(x),u)=G(t,x,u)$ have
$G\in C^\infty$. Throughout this page the torus is always this
$2\pi$-periodic one; a statement "for every $x$" means for every point of
$\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}$, and "a.e." means $\mu$-a.e.

derivations.claim: (The limit is in $H^s$ with the uniform bound (a).) Fix $t$. For every finite $F\subseteq\mathbb Z^3$, [L7] gives $\sum_{k\in F}(1+|k|^2)^s|\widehat u(t)(k)|^2=\lim_j\sum_{k\in F}(1+|k|^2)^s|\widehat{u_{N_j}(t)}(k)|^2\le 4^sR_1^2$; taking the supremum over finite $F$ gives $N_s(u(t))^2\le 4^sR_1^2$, so $u(t)\in H^s$ and $\|u(t)\|_{H^s}\le C_sR_1$ by the norm equivalence, the bound being uniform in $t$. Values in $K_1$ and continuity into $H^{s-1}$ follow from [L1]. To establish strong measurability into $H^s$, for each $M$ the finite Fourier sum $t\mapsto P_Mu(t)$ is continuous into $H^s$, since its finitely many coefficients are continuous by the $H^{s-1}$ continuity. Moreover $P_Mu(t)\to u(t)$ in $H^s$ for every $t$, by the now finite weighted Fourier sum. Explicitly choose compact intervals $J_M$ increasing to $(-T,T)$. On each $J_M$, uniform continuity of $P_Mu$ permits a finite partition into Borel intervals and a finite-valued simple function $h_M$ whose values are sampled from $P_Mu$ and whose $H^s$ error is at most $1/M$; put $h_M=0$ off $J_M$. For every fixed $t$, eventually $t\in J_M$ and $\|h_M(t)-u(t)\|_{H^s}\le1/M+\|P_Mu(t)-u(t)\|_{H^s}\to0$. Thus $u$ is a pointwise limit of measurable simple functions into $H^s$, hence strongly measurable, and its uniform norm bound gives the claimed $L^\infty H^s$ membership. This is (a).

(A convergent subsequence of the time derivatives.) Put $g_j:=\partial_tu_{N_j}$. By [L4] the family is bounded in $H^{s-1}$ and Lipschitz in $H^{s-2}$; by [L5] there is a strictly increasing $j_n$ with $g_{j_n}\to g$ uniformly on every compact subinterval of $(-T,T)$ in $H^{s-2}$, for some $g\in C^0((-T,T);H^{s-2})$. Discarding the complementary terms, rename the subsequence by $N_j$: still $u_{N_j}\to u$ on compact subintervals in $H^{s-1}$ and now $g_j\to g$ on compact subintervals in $H^{s-2}$.

(The time derivative (b).) (i) Let $\psi\in C_c^\infty((-T,T))$ and $v\in H^{s-2}$; put $J':=\operatorname{supp}\psi$. By [L6], $\int_{J'}\psi'(t)\langle u_{N_j}(t),v\rangle dt=-\int_{J'}\psi(t)\langle g_j(t),v\rangle dt$ for every $j$; by step 1.2 the limits $\int_{J'}\psi'\langle u,v\rangle dt$ and $\int_{J'}\psi\langle g,v\rangle dt$ are attained uniformly on $J'$, so $\int\psi'\langle u,v\rangle dt=-\int\psi\langle g,v\rangle dt$. Hence the $H^{s-2}$-valued distributional derivative $\partial_tu$ equals the class of $g$. (ii) Fix $t$; by step 1.2, $\widehat{g_j(t)}(k)\to\widehat g(t)(k)$ for every $k$ [L7], so for every finite $K\subseteq\mathbb Z^3$ the finite sums $\sum_{k\in K}(1+|k|^2)^{s-1}|\widehat{g_j(t)}(k)|^2$ are at most $c_{s-1}^{-1}\|g_j(t)\|_{H^{s-1}}^2\le c_{s-1}^{-1}C_{R_1}^2$ by [L4]; passing to the limit and taking the supremum over finite $K$ gives $N_{s-1}(g(t))^2\le c_{s-1}^{-1}C_{R_1}^2$, so $g(t)\in H^{s-1}$ with $\|g(t)\|_{H^{s-1}}\le C_{s-1}^{1/2}c_{s-1}^{-1/2}C_{R_1}$ by [L7]. For each $M$, $t\mapsto P_Mg(t)$ is continuous into $H^{s-1}$ because $g\in C^0H^{s-2}$ and the projection has finite rank, and $P_Mg(t)\to g(t)$ in $H^{s-1}$ for each $t$. Applying the compact-interval simple-function construction of step 1.1 at order $s-1$ proves strong measurability of $g$ into $H^{s-1}$. Thus $\partial_tu$ is represented by the function $g\in L^\infty((-T,T);H^{s-1})$, uniformly bounded as asserted. This is (b).

(The limit solves the equation distributionally (c), first part.) Let $\psi\in C^\infty((-T,T)\times\mathbb T^3_{2\pi};\mathbb R^m)$ have compact support in $t$. Testing the Galerkin equation [L2] with $\psi$ and using self-adjointness of $P_{N_j}$ gives $\int\!\!\int\psi^{\mathsf T}[A^0(u_{N_j})\partial_tu_{N_j}+A^i(u_{N_j})\partial_iu_{N_j}+B(u_{N_j})]=\int\!\!\int(\psi-P_{N_j}\psi)^{\mathsf T}[\cdots]$, and the right-hand side tends to $0$ because $\psi-P_{N_j}\psi\to0$ in $L^2$ [L2] while the bracket is bounded in $L^\infty L^2$ by [L3] and [L4]. On the left, all factors converge on the compact $t$-support of $\psi$: $A^0(u_{N_j})\to A^0(u)$, $A^i(u_{N_j})\to A^i(u)$ and $B(u_{N_j})\to B(u)$ uniformly by [L1]; $\partial_iu_{N_j}\to\partial_iu$ uniformly by [L1]; and $\partial_tu_{N_j}=g_j\to g=\partial_tu$ uniformly in $H^{s-2}\subseteq L^2$ by step 1.2 and step 2.1; hence the limit is $\int\!\!\int\psi^{\mathsf T}[A^0(u)\partial_tu+A^i(u)\partial_iu+B(u)]=0$ for every test $\psi$, which is the distributional form of $(\star)$.

(Classical regularity and initial value.) From the distributional equation of step 3.1, $\partial_tu=-(A^0(t,\cdot,u))^{-1}[A^i(t,\cdot,u)\partial_iu+B(t,\cdot,u)]$ as $H^{s-2}$-valued distributions; the right-hand side agrees with the continuous function $g=\partial_tu\in C^0((-T,T);H^{s-2})$ as a distribution, so the classical identity $\partial_tu(t)=-(A^0(t,\cdot,u(t)))^{-1}[A^i(t,\cdot,u(t))\partial_iu(t)+B(t,\cdot,u(t))]$ holds for every $t$, both sides being continuous in $t$. The right-hand side is continuous in $(t,x)$: indeed $u\in C^0H^{s-1}$ gives $\partial_iu\in C^0H^{s-2}\subseteq C^0$ with $s-2>3/2$; the inverse coefficient is continuous by [L3]; hence $\partial_tu$ has a continuous representative in $(t,x)$. Passing to the limit in $u_{N_j}(t)-u_{N_j}(t')=\int_{t'}^t g_j(\tau)\,d\tau$ using the uniform $H^{s-2}$ convergence on the segment gives $u(t)-u(t')=\int_{t'}^t g(\tau)\,d\tau$; the continuous-curve fundamental theorem [L6] therefore makes $t\mapsto u(t)$ $C^1$ into $H^{s-2}$ with continuous derivative and the first spatial derivatives are continuous, so $u\in C^1((-T,T)\times\mathbb T^3_{2\pi})$ and $(\star)$ holds pointwise. Finally $u_{N_j}(0)=P_{N_j}u_0\to u_0$ in $H^{s-1}$ and $u_{N_j}(0)\to u(0)$ by the convergence of step 1.2, so $u(0)=u_0$.

boundaries.evidence: Statement assumes an infinite cofinal sequence N_j and a positive T; finite empty Fourier subsets in step 1.1 give the zero lower subsum.
Zero Fourier coefficients give zero limit class in step 1.1; inverse A0 in step 4.1 is protected by uniform positivity, irrespective of vanishing field values.
Statement allows one state component; the finite Fourier-sum passage in steps 1.1 and 2.1 then gives scalar norm and time-derivative bounds.
Step 4.1 inverts only the uniformly coercive time matrix; the limit stays in the closed admissible K1 by step 1.1, so no singular state is introduced.
All convergence in Statement and step 1.2 is local on compact subintervals of (-T,T); step 4.1 includes time zero by projection convergence, without extending to ±T.
Step 1.2 uses the rational diagonal supplier with the declared Countable Choice to extract time derivatives; the original subsequence is retained for the solution limit.
