smooth extensions $\tilde n$ of $n$ and $\tilde X$ of a tangent field with
$\tilde X_p=V$ ([[def-covariant-derivative-along-a-curve]],
[[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]]).

**(c) The induced metric and second fundamental form.** The **induced
metric** $h_p(V,W):=g_p(V,W)$ is a smooth Riemannian metric on $\Sigma$, and
$$K_p(V,W):=g_p(\nabla_Vn,W)\qquad(V,W\in T_p\Sigma)$$
(the **second fundamental form**) defines a smooth symmetric covariant
$2$-tensor field $K$ on $\Sigma$
([[def-gr-smooth-covariant-two-tensor-field]]) with
$$K_p(V,W)=-g_p(\nabla_VW,n_p),$$
where $\nabla_VW$ is the ambient covariant derivative at $p$ of any smooth
extension of a tangent field with value $W$ at $p$, in the direction of any
extension with value $V$ at $p$.

**(d) The shape operator.** The endomorphism $S_p:T_p\Sigma\to T_p\Sigma$
defined by $h_p(S_pV,W)=K_p(V,W)$ for all $W\in T_p\Sigma$ is well defined,
linear and self-adjoint for the positive definite form $h_p$, and the
Weingarten relation $\nabla_Vn=S_pV$ holds for every $V\in T_p\Sigma$.

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]) with metric-selected connection
$\nabla$ ([[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]]), whose existence and
uniqueness are supplied by
[[thm-gr-nondegenerate-levi-civita-and-tensor-derivative]]; that theorem also
extends $\nabla$ to a derivative on tensor fields commuting with contractions
and annihilating $g$ and $g^{-1}$. Let $U\subseteq M$ be open and let
$X,Y,Z$ be smooth vector fields on $U$; brackets are those of
[[def-lie-bracket-of-smooth-vector-fields]], and contractions those of
[[def-contraction-of-a-mixed-tensor]].

**(a) The curvature operator.** The **curvature operator** of $\nabla$ is the
assignment

$$R(X,Y)Z:=\nabla_X\nabla_YZ-\nabla_Y\nabla_XZ-\nabla_{[X,Y]}Z .$$

The right-hand side is a smooth vector field on $U$: $\nabla_YZ$ is smooth
because $\nabla$ is an affine connection
([[def-affine-connection-on-a-smooth-manifold]]), $[X,Y]$ is smooth, and
$\nabla_X(\cdot)$ and $\nabla_{[X,Y]}(\cdot)$ preserve smoothness. The
assignment is defined for the given smooth fields; that its value at a point
depends only on the values of $X,Y,Z$ at that point, so that $R$ is a smooth
tensor field of type $(1,3)$, is the content of
[[thm-gr-curvature-tensoriality-and-coordinate-formula]] clause (a), and
likewise the algebraic symmetries used below are proved in
[[thm-gr-curvature-algebraic-symmetries]].

**(b) Component functions.** Let $(V,x)$ be a smooth chart of $M$ and let
$\Gamma^a{}_{bc}$ be the Christoffel symbols of $\nabla$ in this chart,
characterized by $\nabla_{\partial_b}\partial_c=\sum_a\Gamma^a{}_{bc}\partial_a$
([[def-christoffel-symbols-of-an-affine-connection]]); the coordinate fields
commute, so $\nabla_{\partial_c}\partial_d$ and $\nabla_{\partial_d}\partial_c$
are obtained from the same symbols. The **components** of the curvature in the
chart are the smooth functions $R^a{}_{bcd}$ on $V$ defined by

$$R(\partial_c,\partial_d)\partial_b=\sum_a R^a{}_{bcd}\,\partial_a .$$

The first index is the output slot, the second is the differentiated slot and
the last two are the two directions of the loop; indices are $a,b,c,d=0,1,2,3$
and the Einstein summation convention of
[[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]] applies.

**(c) Lowered tensor, Ricci tensor, scalar curvature, Einstein tensor.** On
the chart domain define, using the inverse metric
$g^{ab}$ of [[def-gr-inverse-metric-and-musical-isomorphisms]],

$$R_{abcd}:=\sum_e g_{ae}R^e{}_{bcd},\qquad \operatorname{Ric}_{bd}:=\sum_{a,c}g^{ac}R_{abcd},\qquad S:=\sum_{b,d}g^{bd}\operatorname{Ric}_{bd},\qquad G_{ab}:=\operatorname{Ric}_{ab}-\tfrac12 S\,g_{ab}.$$

The fields $R_{abcd}$, $\operatorname{Ric}_{ab}$, $S$ and $G_{ab}$ are called
the **Riemann tensor with lowered indices**, the **Ricci tensor**, the
**scalar curvature** and the **Einstein tensor** of the metric-selected
connection. That $R_{abcd}$ are the components of a smooth $(0,4)$-tensor
field and that $\operatorname{Ric}_{ab}$ are the components of a smooth
symmetric $(0,2)$-tensor field, so that the contractions above are
basis-independent and do not depend on the chart, is proved in
[[thm-gr-curvature-algebraic-symmetries]] clauses (a)-(d); the Ricci symmetry
is part of that statement.

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold with
metric-selected connection $\nabla$
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]],
[[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]],
[[thm-gr-nondegenerate-levi-civita-and-tensor-derivative]]), and let $R$ be
the curvature operator of [[def-gr-curvature-tensor-and-derived-tensors]],
with components $R^a{}_{bcd}$ in a chart.

**(a) Tensoriality.** For all smooth functions $f$ on $M$ and smooth vector
fields $X,Y,Z$ on a common domain, $R(X,Y)Z=-R(Y,X)Z$ and
$$R(fX,Y)Z=fR(X,Y)Z,\qquad R(X,fY)Z=fR(X,Y)Z,\qquad R(X,Y)(fZ)=fR(X,Y)Z .$$
Consequently, for every $p\in M$, the value $R(X,Y)Z|_p$ depends only on
$X_p,Y_p,Z_p$, and $R$ is a smooth tensor field of type $(1,3)$ on $M$ whose
components in every smooth chart are the functions $R^a{}_{bcd}$ of
[[def-gr-curvature-tensor-and-derived-tensors]] clause (b).

**(b) Coordinate formula.** In every smooth chart $(U,x)$ with Christoffel
symbols $\Gamma^a{}_{bc}$ of $\nabla$
([[def-christoffel-symbols-of-an-affine-connection]]),
$$R^a{}_{bcd}=\partial_c\Gamma^a{}_{db}-\partial_d\Gamma^a{}_{cb} +\sum_e\bigl(\Gamma^a{}_{ce}\Gamma^e{}_{db}-\Gamma^a{}_{de}\Gamma^e{}_{cb}\bigr)$$
on $U$, for all $a,b,c,d\in\{0,1,2,3\}$.

**(c) Point-normal formula.** If the chart is point-normal at $p$, that is
$g_{ab}(p)=\eta_{ab}$, $\partial_ag_{bc}(p)=0$ and $\Gamma^a{}_{bc}(p)=0$
([[thm-gr-point-normal-and-exponential-coordinate-charts]]), then, writing
$g_{ad,bc}:=\partial_b\partial_cg_{ad}$,
$$R_{abcd}(p)=\tfrac12\bigl(g_{ad,bc}+g_{bc,ad}-g_{bd,ac}-g_{ac,bd}\bigr)(p) .$$
Equivalently, $R^a{}_{bcd}(p)=\tfrac12\,g^{ae}(p)\bigl(\partial_b\partial_cg_{ed}
+\partial_e\partial_dg_{bc}-\partial_e\partial_cg_{bd}-\partial_b\partial_dg_{ec}\bigr)(p)$.

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold with
metric-selected connection $\nabla$
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]],
[[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]],
[[thm-gr-nondegenerate-levi-civita-and-tensor-derivative]]), and let
$R$, $R_{abcd}$, $\operatorname{Ric}_{ab}$, $S$ and $G_{ab}$ be as in
[[def-gr-curvature-tensor-and-derived-tensors]]. Then the following
identities hold for all indices $a,b,c,d\in\{0,1,2,3\}$ and at every point of
every smooth chart:

**(a) Skew-symmetries.** $R_{abcd}=-R_{bacd}$ and $R_{abcd}=-R_{abdc}$.
Equivalently, for smooth vector fields,
$$g\bigl(R(X,Y)Z,W\bigr)=-g\bigl(R(X,Y)W,Z\bigr) \quad\text{and}\quad g\bigl(R(X,Y)Z,W\bigr)=-g\bigl(R(Y,X)Z,W\bigr).$$

**(b) Exchange of the index pairs.** $R_{abcd}=R_{cdab}$, equivalently
$g\bigl(R(X,Y)Z,W\bigr)=g\bigl(R(Z,W)X,Y\bigr)$.

**(c) First Bianchi identity.** $R_{a[bcd]}=0$, that is,
$$R_{abcd}+R_{acdb}+R_{adbc}=0 .$$

**(d) Ricci symmetry.** $\operatorname{Ric}_{ab}=\operatorname{Ric}_{ba}$;
consequently the Einstein tensor is symmetric, $G_{ab}=G_{ba}$.

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]) and let $r,s\ge0$ be integers.

**(a) Tensors at a point.** For $p\in M$, the tangent space $T_pM$ is the real
vector space of derivations at $p$
([[def-derivation-at-a-point-and-tangent-space]]) and the cotangent space is
its algebraic dual, $T_p^*M=(T_pM)^*$
([[def-cotangent-space-and-cotangent-bundle-as-a-disjoint-union]]). A **type
$(r,s)$ tensor at $p$** is a multilinear map

$$T_p:(T_p^*M)^r\times(T_pM)^s\longrightarrow\mathbb R,$$

in the sense of [[def-type-r-s-tensor-on-a-finite-dimensional-vector-space]]:
the first $r$ arguments are covectors and the last $s$ are vectors. In
particular a type $(1,0)$ tensor is a vector, a type $(0,1)$ tensor is a
covector and a type $(0,2)$ tensor is a bilinear form, so the covariant
$2$-tensors of [[def-gr-smooth-covariant-two-tensor-field]] are exactly the
type $(0,2)$ tensors of this definition.

**(b) The tensor bundle and smooth fields.** The **type $(r,s)$ tensor bundle**
$T^r_sM$ is the disjoint union of the fibres $T^r_sM|_p=\operatorname{Mult}((T_p^*M)^r\times(T_pM)^s,\mathbb R)$
over $p\in M$ ([[def-type-r-s-tensor-bundle]]); it carries the smooth
vector-bundle structure defined by the tensor-coordinate change rules
([[thm-tensor-transition-laws-define-a-smooth-vector-bundle]]). A **smooth
tensor field of type $(r,s)$** on $M$ is a family $T=(T_p)_{p\in M}$ assigning
to each $p$ a type $(r,s)$ tensor at $p$, such that for every smooth chart
$(U,x)$ of the maximal smooth atlas the **component functions**

$$T^{a_1\cdots a_r}{}_{b_1\cdots b_s}(q):=T_q\bigl(dx^{a_1}|_q,\dots,dx^{a_r}|_q,\ \partial_{b_1}|_q,\dots,\partial_{b_s}|_q\bigr),\qquad q\in U,$$

are $C^\infty$ on $U$; here the coordinate derivations
$\partial_b|_q=\partial/\partial x^b|_q$ form a basis of $T_qM$
([[thm-coordinate-derivations-form-a-basis-of-the-tangent-space]]) and the
coordinate differentials $dx^a|_q$ form the dual basis of $T_q^*M$
([[thm-coordinate-differentials-form-the-dual-cotangent-basis]]). This is
equivalent to $T$ being a smooth section of $T^r_sM$ in the sense of
[[def-smooth-tensor-field]]: the component functions are the frame
coefficients of the section in the local frame induced by the chart. The
smoothness condition is independent of the chosen smooth atlas and the
components in two overlapping charts are related by the transformation law
proved in the lemma on this page; the definition is therefore chart
independent rather than merely chart-wise.

**(c) Index conventions.** Indices are written $a,b,c,\dots$ for components in
a chart, with the Einstein summation convention: a repeated index, once upper
and once lower, is summed over $0,1,2,3$. An upper index is a contravariant
slot in which a covector is evaluated, a lower index a covariant slot in which
a vector is evaluated. Slots are moved between these positions with the
musical isomorphisms $\flat_p,\sharp_p$ of
[[def-gr-inverse-metric-and-musical-isomorphisms]]; for example, lowering the
first slot of a type $(1,1)$ field uses $(g^\flat T)^a{}_b=g_{ac}T^c{}_b$ and
raising uses $g^{ac}$. This is an identification of slots, not a change of the
field into a field of another kind, and it uses the metric nondegeneracy.

**(d) Scope.** The definition is purely local and chart-based; no global
triviality of $T^r_sM$, no global frame and no choice of metric-compatible
fields is assumed or implied. All fields are smooth ($C^\infty$); no
lower-regularity or distributional tensor field is defined here. The smooth
structure of the tangent bundle, and hence of $T^r_sM$
([[thm-tensor-transition-laws-define-a-smooth-vector-bundle]]), inherits the
axiom $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ of [[def-countable-choice]] recorded with
[[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]; the component formulation of smoothness
itself makes no choice.

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold and let
$p\in M$ ([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]). The cotangent space $T_p^*M$ is
the algebraic dual of $T_pM$ ([[def-algebraic-dual-and-linear-functional]]).

**Musical isomorphisms.** Define the **flat map**

$$\flat_p:T_pM\longrightarrow T_p^*M,\qquad \flat_p(v):=g_p(v,\cdot),$$

so that $\flat_p(v)(w)=g_p(v,w)$; it is $\mathbb R$-linear by bilinearity of
$g_p$. Its kernel is $\{v:g_p(v,w)=0\text{ for all }w\}=\{0\}$ because $g_p$ is
nondegenerate, and $\dim_{\mathbb R}T_pM=\dim_{\mathbb R}T_p^*M=4$ since the
coordinate derivations of a chart form a basis of $T_pM$
([[thm-coordinate-derivations-form-a-basis-of-the-tangent-space]]); hence
$\flat_p$ is a linear isomorphism and has an inverse
$\sharp_p:T_p^*M\to T_pM$.

**Inverse metric.** The **inverse metric** at $p$ is the symmetric bilinear form

$$g_p^{-1}:T_p^*M\times T_p^*M\longrightarrow\mathbb R,\qquad g_p^{-1}(\alpha,\beta):=g_p(\sharp_p\alpha,\sharp_p\beta).$$

It is symmetric because $g_p$ is, and it is nondegenerate: if
$g_p^{-1}(\alpha,\beta)=0$ for all $\beta$, then $g_p(\sharp_p\alpha,\cdot)=0$,
so $\sharp_p\alpha=0$ and hence $\alpha=0$.

**Components in a chart.** Let $(U,x)$ be a smooth chart and
$g_{ab}(q)=g_q(\partial_a|_q,\partial_b|_q)$ the components of $g$; let
$dx^a|_q$ be the differential of the coordinate function $x^a$ at $q$
([[def-differential-of-a-smooth-map]]), so that
$dx^a|_q(\partial_b|_q)=\partial_b|_q(x^a)=\delta^a{}_b$. Define the components
of the inverse metric in this chart by

$$g^{ab}(q):=g_q^{-1}\bigl(dx^a|_q,\,dx^b|_q\bigr),\qquad q\in U,$$

so that $\sharp_q(dx^a|_q)=\sum_bg^{ab}(q)\,\partial_b|_q$; equivalently
$(g^{ab}(q))$ is the inverse matrix of $(g_{ab}(q))$ at every $q$, that is

$$g^{ac}(q)\,g_{cb}(q)=\delta^a{}_b=\delta^c{}_bg^{ab}(q),$$

because $g_q(\sharp_qdx^a|_q,\partial_c|_q)=dx^a|_q(\partial_c|_q)=\delta^a{}_c$
and also $g_q(\sharp_qdx^a|_q,\partial_c|_q)=\sum_bg^{ab}(q)g_{bc}(q)$. In
particular $g^{ab}=g^{ba}$. The components $g^{ab}$ depend smoothly on $q$;
this is proved in [[lem-gr-inverse-metric-is-smooth]].

**Raising, lowering and metric trace.** Let $A$ be a smooth symmetric covariant
$2$-tensor field on an open set $V\subseteq M$
([[def-gr-smooth-covariant-two-tensor-field]]). At each $p\in V$ define the
endomorphism

$$A^\sharp_p:T_pM\to T_pM,\qquad A^\sharp_p(v):=\sharp_p\bigl(A_p(v,\cdot)\bigr),$$

characterized by $g_p(A^\sharp_p(v),w)=A_p(v,w)$ for all $w\in T_pM$; it is
self-adjoint for $g_p$ because $A_p$ is symmetric. Its **metric trace** is

$$\operatorname{tr}_g(A)(p):=\operatorname{tr}\bigl(A^\sharp_p\bigr)$$

with the trace of an endomorphism as in [[def-trace-of-an-endomorphism]]. In a
chart the raised, mixed and doubly raised components are

$$A^{ab}:=g^{ac}g^{bd}A_{cd},\qquad A^a{}_b:=g^{ac}A_{cb},\qquad\text{and}\qquad \operatorname{tr}_g(A)=g^{ab}A_{ab},$$

the last identity obtained by evaluating in a $g_p$-orthonormal basis
$(e_0,e_1,e_2,e_3)$, where $g_p(e_a,e_b)=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)_{ab}$ by
[[lem-timelike-cone-has-two-convex-components]] so that
$g^{ab}A_{ab}=\sum_a g^{aa}A_{aa}=-A(e_0,e_0)+A(e_1,e_1)+A(e_2,e_2)+A(e_3,e_3)$,
which is the trace of the endomorphism $v\mapsto\sharp_p(A_p(v,\cdot))$ in that
basis. All these operations are pointwise and depend only on $g$, $A$ and the
duality pairing, not on a chart.

**Conventions.** Raising and lowering apply to one index at a time and preserve
index order; $A_{ab}$, $A^a{}_b$ and $A^{ab}$ denote the same tensor $A$ with
indices positioned by $g$. The musical isomorphisms and the inverse metric are
defined for every smooth Lorentzian four-manifold of this library; no choice
principle is used in this definition, every ingredient being pointwise linear
algebra over $\mathbb R$ together with the pointwise nondegeneracy of $g_p$.

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold with
metric-selected connection $\nabla$
([[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]],
[[thm-gr-nondegenerate-levi-civita-and-tensor-derivative]]), let $T$ be a
smooth symmetric covariant $2$-tensor field on $M$
([[def-gr-smooth-covariant-two-tensor-field]]), let $\kappa,\Lambda\in\mathbb R$
and let $G$ be the Einstein tensor of the metric-selected connection
([[def-gr-curvature-tensor-and-derived-tensors]]). Suppose that the field
equation
$$G+\Lambda g=\kappa T$$
holds at every point of $M$. Let $\Sigma\subseteq M$ be a spacelike embedded
hypersurface with future unit normal field $n$, induced metric $h$ and second
fundamental form $K$, and let $\rho:=T(n,n)$ and $j(V):=-T(n,V)$ for
$V\in T_p\Sigma$, $p\in\Sigma$, be the matter data of
[[def-gr-spacelike-initial-data-and-constraints]] clause (b). Then:

**(a)** The tuple $(\Sigma,h,K,\rho,j)$ satisfies the constraint equations
for $(\kappa,\Lambda)$ in the sense of
[[def-gr-spacelike-initial-data-and-constraints]] clause (b),
$$G(n,n)-\Lambda=\kappa\,\rho,\qquad G(n,V)=\kappa\,T(n,V) \quad\text{for every }V\in T_p\Sigma,\ p\in\Sigma;$$
equivalently $G(n,V)=-\kappa\,j(V)$ on $\Sigma$.

**(b)** The fields $\rho$ and $j$ are smooth on $\Sigma$: in every slice chart
their expressions in the slice coordinates are $C^\infty$.

derivations.claim:
(Induced connection.) On tangent fields define $D_XY=(
abla_XY)^	op$, where $V^	op=V+g(V,n)n$. This defines a smooth connection on $\Sigma$ because tangential differentiation is independent of ambient extensions. By [L1], $
abla_XY=D_XY+K(X,Y)n$ and $
abla_Xn=AX$ with $h(AX,Y)=K(X,Y)$. Projecting the torsion identity gives $D_XY-D_YX=[X,Y]$, and restricting metric compatibility gives $Xh(Y,Z)=h(D_XY,Z)+h(Y,D_XZ)$. Thus $D$ is torsion-free and $h$-compatible. Uniqueness follows directly by solving these two identities for $2h(D_XY,Z)$: it equals $Xh(Y,Z)+Yh(X,Z)-Zh(X,Y)-h(X,[Y,Z])+h(Y,[Z,X])+h(Z,[X,Y])$. Hence $D$ is the Levi-Civita connection of $h$, with its curvature and Ricci/scalar contractions defined in the same slot order as [L3].

(Full tangential and normal curvature decomposition.) Expand $
abla_X
abla_YZ$ using step 1.1: its tangential part is $D_XD_YZ+K(Y,Z)AX$, and its coefficient of $n$ is $K(X,D_YZ)+X(K(Y,Z))$. Subtract the analogous expression with $X,Y$ exchanged and subtract $
abla_{[X,Y]}Z$. The tangential part is $R^h(X,Y)Z+K(Y,Z)AX-K(X,Z)AY$. The coefficient of $n$ is $X(K(Y,Z))-Y(K(X,Z))+K(X,D_YZ)-K(Y,D_XZ)-K([X,Y],Z)$. Writing $(D_XK)(Y,Z)=X(K(Y,Z))-K(D_XY,Z)-K(Y,D_XZ)$, and using $D_XY-D_YX=[X,Y]$, that coefficient is $(D_XK)(Y,Z)-(D_YK)(X,Z)$. Pairing the tangential part with $W$ yields the operator Gauss display, and replacing $(X,Y,Z,W)$ by $(Z,W,Y,X)$ yields its lowered-slot display. Pairing the normal part with $n$ multiplies its coefficient by $g(n,n)=-1$, yielding exactly (b).

(Double tangential contraction.) Choose any tangent basis $e_i$ at $p$ and complete it by $e_0=n$. Then $g^{00}=-1$, $g^{0i}=0$ and $g^{ij}=h^{ij}$. Let $U_{ij}=R_{0i0j}$ and $Q=h^{ik}h^{jl}R_{ijkl}$ in the lowered-slot convention of [L3]. Contracting the Gauss identity of step 2.1 gives $Q=S_h+\tau^2-|K|_h^2$: its first contraction is the intrinsic scalar by definition, its $K_{ik}K_{jl}$ contraction is $\tau^2$, and its $K_{il}K_{jk}$ contraction is $|K|_h^2$. No normal derivative enters $Q$.

(Exact mixed contraction.) From step 2.1 in the same basis, $R_{0ijk}=g(R(e_j,e_k)e_i,n)=(D_{e_k}K)(e_j,e_i)-(D_{e_j}K)(e_k,e_i)$. First-pair antisymmetry gives $R_{i0jk}=(D_{e_j}K)(e_k,e_i)-(D_{e_k}K)(e_j,e_i)$. Therefore $\operatorname{Ric}_{0k}=h^{ij}R_{i0jk}=h^{ij}(D_{e_j}K)(e_k,e_i)-h^{ij}(D_{e_k}K)(e_j,e_i)=(\operatorname{div}_hK)_k-D_{e_k}\tau$, using symmetry of $K$ and $Dh^{-1}=0$. Since $g_{0k}=0$, $G_{0k}=\operatorname{Ric}_{0k}$. This proves the second formula in (c).

(Exact scalar and Einstein contractions.) By [L3] and the two pair antisymmetries, $\operatorname{Ric}_{00}=h^{ij}R_{i0j0}=h^{ij}U_{ij}$ and $\operatorname{Ric}_{ij}=-R_{0i0j}+h^{kl}R_{kilj}=-U_{ij}+h^{kl}R_{kilj}$. Hence $h^{ij}\operatorname{Ric}_{ij}=Q-h^{ij}U_{ij}=Q-\operatorname{Ric}_{00}$, and $S=-\operatorname{Ric}_{00}+h^{ij}\operatorname{Ric}_{ij}=Q-2\operatorname{Ric}_{00}$. Since $g_{00}=-1$, $G_{00}=\operatorname{Ric}_{00}+\tfrac12S=\tfrac12Q$. This proves the first formula in (c) without needing any value or normal derivative of $U$.

(Constraints.) Evaluate $G+\Lambda g=\kappa T$ on $(n,n)$ and $(n,Y)$. As $g(n,n)=-1$ and $g(n,Y)=0$, the results are $G(n,n)=\Lambda+\kappa T(n,n)$ and $G(n,Y)=\kappa T(n,Y)$; insert steps 3.1, 3.2 and 4.1 and multiply the first equation by $2$. The stated $j$ form follows from $j(Y)=-T(n,Y)$. No global, compactness, completeness or field-equation hypothesis is used in (a)-(c), and in (d) only the pointwise field equation is used.

boundaries.evidence: The Gauss/Codazzi Statement is quantified pointwise over a hypersurface; if that hypersurface is empty the equations have no instances and all assertions are vacuous.
Step 3.1 normal contractions allow K=0, zero curvature and T=0; no density or curvature norm is used as a denominator in the constraint formulas.
Step 3.1 contracts finite three-dimensional tangent indices; an individual tangent vector can be zero and its multilinear curvature equation remains valid.
Statement requires h Riemannian and g Lorentzian, giving an actual future unit normal for step 1.1; degenerate or null hypersurfaces are excluded.
The Statement proves constraints at every point where the Einstein equation holds, not continuation or extension of a hypersurface through its boundary.
The adapted frame used for contraction is local and finite; step 1.1 defines the induced connection intrinsically without choosing global tangent frames.
Step 2.1 derives the Gauss operator formula and substitutes (X,Y,Z,W)=(Z,W,Y,X) to obtain the displayed lowered-slot formula.
Statement (a) fixes mathcalR(A,B,C,D)=g(R(C,D)B,A), so reversing the same permutation in step 2.1 recovers the operator form with its exact K signs.

citations.quote:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$
([[def-countable-choice]]). Fix an integer $m\ge1$, an open set
$O\subseteq\mathbb R^m$ with the subspace topology and a nondegenerate open
interval $I\subseteq\mathbb R$ containing $0$. All functions on
$\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}$ are those of [[def-gr-periodic-torus-and-sobolev-spaces]],
and smoothness on $I\times\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}\times O$ means smoothness of the
representative in the sense of clause (e) of that item.

**(a) Coefficients.** A **periodic symmetric hyperbolic coefficient family** on
$O$ consists of smooth maps
$$A^\mu:I\times\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}\times O\to\operatorname{Sym}_m(\mathbb R)\quad(\mu=0,1,2,3),\qquad B:I\times\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}\times O\to\mathbb R^m,$$
such that $A^0(t,x,u)$ is positive definite for every
$(t,x,u)\in I\times\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}\times O$; here
$\operatorname{Sym}_m(\mathbb R)$ is the real vector space of symmetric
$m\times m$ matrices, identified with symmetric endomorphisms of $\mathbb R^m$
through the standard coordinate inner product, and positive definiteness means
$z^TA^0(t,x,u)z>0$ for every nonzero $z\in\mathbb R^m$
([[def-ck-and-multi-index-notation-in-several-variables]]).

**(b) The system.** The associated **symmetric hyperbolic system** is
$$A^0(t,x,u)\,\partial_tu+\sum_{i=1}^3A^i(t,x,u)\,\partial_iu+B(t,x,u)=0 .\qquad(\star)$$

**(c) Values and norms.** A map $u:J\to H^s(\mathbb T^3_{2\pi};\mathbb R^m)$
on an interval $J$ **takes values in a set $E\subseteq\mathbb R^m$** when
$u(t)(x)\in E$ for every $t\in J$ and every $x\in\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}$, with
$u(t)$ read through its continuous representative when $s>3/2$. For compact
$K\subseteq O$ and $R\ge0$ put
$$\mathcal S(K,R):=\bigl\{u_0\in H^s(\mathbb T^3_{2\pi};\mathbb R^m):u_0\text{ takes values in }K,\ \|u_0\|_{H^s}\le R\bigr\}.$$

**(d) Classical solutions.** Let $s\ge2$. A **classical solution of $(\star)$ on
$J\times\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}$** is a $C^1$ map
$u:J\times\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}\to\mathbb R^m$ with $u(t,x)\in O$ for all
$(t,x)$ and $(\star)$ satisfied at every point, such that
$u\in L^\infty(J;H^s)$ and $\partial_tu\in L^\infty(J;H^{s-1})$. (For $s\ge2$
the embedding clause gives a continuous representative, so the pointwise
conditions are meaningful.)

**(e) Sobolev solutions.** Let $s\ge5$ and let $J$ be an open interval. A map
$u:J\to H^s(\mathbb T^3_{2\pi};\mathbb R^m)$ is a **Sobolev solution of
$(\star)$ on $J$** when

1. $u\in L^\infty(J;H^s)\cap C^0(J;H^{s-1})$ and the distributional time
   derivative $\partial_tu$ lies in $L^\infty(J;H^{s-1})$;
2. $u$ takes values in $O$;
3. for almost every $t\in J$ the identity $(\star)$ holds in
   $L^2(\mathbb T^3_{2\pi};\mathbb R^m)$, the coefficients being composed with
   the continuous representative of $u(t)$; all products are defined because
   $A^0(t,\cdot,u(t))$ and $A^i(t,\cdot,u(t))$ lie in $H^s$ with norm bounded
   by a function of $\|u(t)\|_{H^s}$, $\partial_tu(t)$ and $\partial_iu(t)$ lie
   in $H^{s-1}$, and $B(t,\cdot,u(t))$ lies in $H^s$.

**(f) Initial data.** **Initial data for $(\star)$ at time $0$** are a class
$u_0\in H^s(\mathbb T^3_{2\pi};\mathbb R^m)$ with $s\ge5$ whose values lie in a
compact subset of $O$; a solution **has initial value $u_0$** when
$u(t)\to u_0$ in $H^{s-1}$ as $t\to0$ within $J$.

The definition introduces the system and its solution classes only; existence,
uniqueness, continuous dependence and smooth persistence are asserted and
proved in [[thm-gr-periodic-symmetric-hyperbolic-existence]],
[[thm-gr-periodic-symmetric-hyperbolic-uniqueness-stability]] and
[[thm-gr-periodic-symmetric-hyperbolic-smooth-persistence]].

Let $m\ge1$ and let $B\in\operatorname{Sym}_m(\mathbb R)$ be positive definite,
that is $B^{\mathsf T}=B$ and $z^{\mathsf T}Bz>0$ for every nonzero
$z\in\mathbb R^m$ with the standard coordinate inner product.

**(a)** There are real numbers $0<a\le b$ with $a\,|z|^2\le z^{\mathsf T}Bz\le b\,|z|^2$
for every $z\in\mathbb R^m$; equivalently $aI\le B\le bI$ in the Loewner
order. They can be taken to be the least and largest eigenvalues of $B$.

**(b)** $B$ is invertible and $\tfrac1bI\le B^{-1}\le\tfrac1aI$, so in
particular $\|B^{-1}z\|\le a^{-1}\|z\|$.

**(c)** Let $\Lambda$ be a compact topological space and let
$B:\Lambda\to\operatorname{Sym}_m(\mathbb R)$ be continuous with $B(\lambda)$
positive definite for every $\lambda\in\Lambda$. Then there are constants
$0<a\le b$ with $aI\le B(\lambda)\le bI$ for every $\lambda\in\Lambda$.

**(d)** Let $D\subseteq\mathbb R^p$ be open and let $B:D\to\operatorname{Sym}_m(\mathbb R)$
be smooth with $B(x)\ge aI$ for a constant $a>0$ and all $x\in D$. Then
$x\mapsto B(x)^{-1}$ is smooth on $D$ and $B(x)^{-1}\le a^{-1}I$ there.

Assume Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $s\ge5$, let $O\subseteq\mathbb R^m$ be open, let $I$ be an open time interval, let $I_0\subseteq I$ be a compact interval, and let $F:I\times\mathbb T^3\times O\to\mathbb R^{m'}$ and $A:I\times\mathbb T^3\times O\to M_{m'}(\mathbb R)$ be smooth. Fix compact $K\subseteq O$ and $R\ge0$. Constants below depend on these data and are uniform in $t\in I_0$. For $u,v\in H^s$ with values in $K$ and norms at most $R$:

**(a)** $\|F(t,\cdot,u)\|_{H^j}\le C(1+\|u\|_{H^s})$ for $0\le j\le s$.

**(b)** $\|F(t,\cdot,u)-F(t,\cdot,v)\|_{H^{s-1}}\le C\|u-v\|_{H^{s-1}}$. The same bound holds at order zero.

**(c)** For $1\le j=|\alpha|\le s-1$, $\|[D^\alpha,A(t,\cdot,u)]w\|_2\le C\|w\|_{H^{j-1}}$. For $|\alpha|=s$, $\|[D^\alpha,A(t,\cdot,u)]w\|_2\le C\|w\|_{H^{s-1}}$. Commutators are interpreted distributionally by their Leibniz expansion, even if the two individual order-$j$ terms are not separately in $L^2$.

**(d)** For $0\le j\le s-1$, $\|A(t,\cdot,u)w\|_{H^j}\le C\|w\|_{H^j}$.

**(e)** Let $n\ge6$, $\rho\ge0$ and $z\in H^n$ with values in $K$ and $\|z\|_{H^{n-1}}\le\rho$. Then $\|F(t,\cdot,z)\|_{H^n}\le C_\rho(1+\|z\|_{H^n})$. Moreover for $w\in H^{n-1}$ and $|\alpha|\le n$,
$$\|[D^\alpha,A(t,\cdot,z)]w\|_2\le C_\rho\bigl(\|w\|_{H^{n-1}}+(1+\|z\|_{H^n})\|w\|_{H^{n-2}}\bigr).$$
The same estimates apply to any smooth coefficient obtained from $F,A$ by differentiation or by a smooth matrix inverse where that inverse exists on a neighborhood of $I_0\times\mathbb T^3\times K$.

Assume Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $s\ge5$, let $O\subseteq\mathbb R^m$ be open, let $I$ be an open time interval, let $I_0\subseteq I$ be a compact interval, and let $F:I\times\mathbb T^3\times O\to\mathbb R^{m'}$ and $A:I\times\mathbb T^3\times O\to M_{m'}(\mathbb R)$ be smooth. Fix compact $K\subseteq O$ and $R\ge0$. Constants below depend on these data and are uniform in $t\in I_0$. For $u,v\in H^s$ with values in $K$ and norms at most $R$:

**(a)** $\|F(t,\cdot,u)\|_{H^j}\le C(1+\|u\|_{H^s})$ for $0\le j\le s$.

**(b)** $\|F(t,\cdot,u)-F(t,\cdot,v)\|_{H^{s-1}}\le C\|u-v\|_{H^{s-1}}$. The same bound holds at order zero.

**(c)** For $1\le j=|\alpha|\le s-1$, $\|[D^\alpha,A(t,\cdot,u)]w\|_2\le C\|w\|_{H^{j-1}}$. For $|\alpha|=s$, $\|[D^\alpha,A(t,\cdot,u)]w\|_2\le C\|w\|_{H^{s-1}}$. Commutators are interpreted distributionally by their Leibniz expansion, even if the two individual order-$j$ terms are not separately in $L^2$.

**(d)** For $0\le j\le s-1$, $\|A(t,\cdot,u)w\|_{H^j}\le C\|w\|_{H^j}$.

**(e)** Let $n\ge6$, $\rho\ge0$ and $z\in H^n$ with values in $K$ and $\|z\|_{H^{n-1}}\le\rho$. Then $\|F(t,\cdot,z)\|_{H^n}\le C_\rho(1+\|z\|_{H^n})$. Moreover for $w\in H^{n-1}$ and $|\alpha|\le n$,
$$\|[D^\alpha,A(t,\cdot,z)]w\|_2\le C_\rho\bigl(\|w\|_{H^{n-1}}+(1+\|z\|_{H^n})\|w\|_{H^{n-2}}\bigr).$$
The same estimates apply to any smooth coefficient obtained from $F,A$ by differentiation or by a smooth matrix inverse where that inverse exists on a neighborhood of $I_0\times\mathbb T^3\times K$.

**(b)** $B$ is invertible and $\tfrac1bI\le B^{-1}\le\tfrac1aI$, so in

Let $t_0\le T$, let $u,a,b:[t_0,T]\to\mathbb R$ be continuous, with $u,b\ge0$, and suppose

$$u(t)\le a(t)+\int_{t_0}^t b(s)u(s)\,ds.$$

Then

$$u(t)\le a(t)+\int_{t_0}^t a(s)b(s)\exp\!\left(\int_s^t b(r)\,dr\right)ds.$$

If $a$ is nondecreasing, this gives $u(t)\le a(t)\exp(\int_{t_0}^t b)$. The time-reflected form assumes $u(t)\le a(t)+\int_t^{t_0}b(s)u(s)\,ds$ for $t\le t_0$. In particular, when $a=A\ge0$ and $b=B\ge0$ are constant, the two orientations give $u(t)\le A e^{B|t-t_0|}$.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$
([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $m\ge1$, $N\ge0$, and let $P_N$ be the Galerkin
projection and $X_N$ the Galerkin space of [[def-gr-galerkin-fourier-projection]]
on $\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}$. Then:

**(a)** $P_N$ is linear on $L^2(\mathbb T^3_{2\pi};\mathbb R^m)$, self-adjoint
($\langle P_Nu,v\rangle_2=\langle u,P_Nv\rangle_2$ for all $u,v\in L^2$) and
idempotent ($P_N^2=P_N$), with range $X_N$ and kernel the classes with vanishing
coefficients on $\Lambda_N$;

**(b)** for every multi-index $\alpha$ with $|\alpha|\le s$ and every
$u\in H^s$, $P_ND^\alpha u=D^\alpha P_Nu$;

**(c)** for every $0\le r\le s$ and every $u\in H^r$,
$\|P_Nu\|_{H^r}\le\|u\|_{H^r}$;

**(d)** for every $0\le r\le s$ and every $u\in H^r$, $P_Nu\to u$ in $H^r$ as
$N\to\infty$;

**(e)** for every $s\ge1$, every $u\in H^s$ and every $N\ge0$,
$$\|u-P_Nu\|_{H^{s-1}}\le C_s\,(1+N^2)^{-1/2}\,\|u\|_{H^s}$$
with $C_s$ depending only on $s$.

derivations.claim: (Homogeneous forcing.) Put $r=s-1$ and $w=u-v$, and define $f=-(A^0(u)-A^0(v))\partial_tv-(A^i(u)-A^i(v))\partial_i v-B(u)+B(v)$. The difference bound of [L3] and the $H^r$ algebra bound give $\|f\|_{H^r}\le C\|w\|_{H^r}$, since the derivatives of $v$ have bounded $H^r$ norms by [L4]. Smooth cutoff extension in the proved supplier gives these estimates on the actual compact value sets without assuming convexity. Total coefficient derivatives $\dot a=A_t^0(u)+A_u^0(u)\partial_tu$ and $\partial_i a_i$ are bounded in $L^\infty$ by those same solution bounds.

($L^2$ uniqueness for all stated classical solutions.) Set $E_0(t)=\int w^{\mathsf T}a w$. Symmetry and integration by parts give $E_0'=\int w^{\mathsf T}(\dot a+\partial_i a_i)w+2\int w^{\mathsf T}f$. Pointwise coefficient Lipschitz bounds give $|f|\le C|w|$, since $\partial_tv$ and $\partial_i v$ are bounded in $L^\infty$. Thus $|E_0'|\le CE_0$. If $w(0)=0$, Gronwall on either oriented segment from $0$ to $t$ gives $E_0(t)=0$. As $t\in J$ was arbitrary, this proves (a).

(Energy identity at the stated regularity.) Work on any compact time segment and define $E=\sum_{|\alpha|\le r}\int(D^\alpha w)^{\mathsf T}aD^\alpha w$. Put $w_N=P_Nw$, $h=\partial_tw$, and $y_\alpha=D^\alpha w$, $h_\alpha=D^\alpha h$. Classical $C^1$ regularity makes each Fourier coefficient $C^1$ with derivative the coefficient of $h$, so $w_N$ is a $C^1$ finite-dimensional curve. The bounds $w\in H^{r+1}$ and $h\in H^r$ are uniform at every time: the former is assumed and the latter follows pointwise from the PDE and [L4]. The coefficients $a$ and $\dot a$ are continuous, with $a$ uniformly $C^1$ in space and $\dot a$ uniformly bounded. Let $E_N=\sum_{|\alpha|\le r}\int(P_Ny_\alpha)^{\mathsf T}a(P_Ny_\alpha)$. The tail bound [L6] gives uniform $L^2$ convergence $P_Ny_\alpha\to y_\alpha$ at rate $O((1+N^2)^{-1/2})$ since $y_\alpha\in H^1$ uniformly. Hence $E_N\to E$ uniformly. Finite-dimensional differentiation gives $E_N'=\sum_\alpha[2\langle P_Nh_\alpha,aP_Ny_\alpha\rangle+\langle P_Ny_\alpha,\dot aP_Ny_\alpha\rangle]$. By self-adjointness the first pairing equals $\langle h_\alpha,P_N(aP_Ny_\alpha)\rangle$. Now $ay_\alpha$ has uniformly bounded $H^1$ norm by the Leibniz rule, and $\|P_N(aP_Ny_\alpha)-ay_\alpha\|_2\le\|a\|_\infty\|P_Ny_\alpha-y_\alpha\|_2+\|(P_N-I)(ay_\alpha)\|_2\to0$ uniformly by [L6]. The quadratic terms also converge uniformly. Thus $E_N'$ converges uniformly to $G=\sum_\alpha[2\langle h_\alpha,ay_\alpha\rangle+\langle y_\alpha,\dot ay_\alpha\rangle]$. Integrating the scalar identities $E_N(t)-E_N(t')=\int_{t'}^tE_N'$ and passing uniformly to the limit gives $E(t)-E(t')=\int_{t'}^tG$; $G$ is continuous as a uniform limit of continuous functions. Therefore $E'=G$. The differentiated difference equation is an $L^2$ identity because $w\in H^{r+1}$ and $h\in H^r$; spatial integration by parts is justified by Fourier density and the $H^1$ bounds for $y_\alpha$. It may therefore be substituted into $G$ without additional time regularity assumptions.

(Homogeneous difference time derivative.) Invert $a$ in [L1]. Multiplier bounds at order $r-1$, the forcing estimate of step 1.1 and $\|\partial_iw\|_{H^{r-1}}\le\|w\|_{H^r}$ give $\|\partial_tw\|_{H^{r-1}}\le C\|w\|_{H^r}$.

(Order-$r$ difference energy.) Put $E=\sum_{|\alpha|\le r}\int(D^\alpha w)^{\mathsf T}aD^\alpha w$, so $a_0\|w\|_{H^r}^2\le E\le b_0\|w\|_{H^r}^2$. Differentiating [L1] gives $a\partial_tD^\alpha w+a_i\partial_iD^\alpha w=D^\alpha f-[D^\alpha,a]\partial_tw-[D^\alpha,a_i]\partial_iw$. After integration by parts the energy derivative consists of the $\dot a+\partial_i a_i$ quadratic terms and twice the pairings with these three right-side terms. Step 1.1 bounds the quadratic and forcing terms by $C\|w\|_{H^r}^2$. Homogeneous commutators from [L3], together with step 2.1, bound the time commutators by the same expression. Spatial commutators also have that bound since $\|\partial_iw\|_{H^{r-1}}\le\|w\|_{H^r}$. Therefore $|E'|\le CE$. The energy identity is justified at this regularity by step 1.3.

(Continuous dependence.) Gronwall in both directions gives $E(t)\le E(0)e^{C|t|}$. Equivalence yields $\|w(t)\|_{H^r}\le\sqrt{b_0/a_0}\,e^{C|t|/2}\|w(0)\|_{H^r}$. Choose $C'$ to dominate $\sqrt{b_0/a_0}$ and $C/2$. This proves (b).

boundaries.evidence: If the class of solution pairs in Statement is empty, the comparison assertions are vacuous; any given pair has the common nonempty time interval containing zero.
Step 1.2 proves identical initial data give E0=0 everywhere by homogeneous Gronwall; step 3.1 retains homogeneous |Eprime|<=CE for zero difference.
Statement allows a scalar difference w; steps 1.2 and 3.1 then use the same scalar weighted energy and do not require independent components.
The common compact value set supplies positive time-matrix constants a0,b0 in step 3.1; singular coefficients are excluded before the inverse estimate of step 2.1.
Step 4.1 uses both orientations from zero to any t with |t|<T; no continuous extension to ±T is part of the comparison Statement.
The projection approximants in step 1.3 are explicit P_Nw rather than separately chosen solutions; Countable Choice is the premise carried by the Fourier prerequisites.

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold, and let $\Sigma\subseteq M$ be a smooth spacelike embedded hypersurface with future unit normal $n$, induced Riemannian metric $h$ and second fundamental form $K(X,Y)=g(\nabla_Xn,Y)$ ([[def-gr-spacelike-hypersurfaces-and-cauchy-sets]], [[lem-gr-spacelike-hypersurface-normal-and-second-fundamental-form]]). Write $D$ for the Levi-Civita connection of $h$, $R^h$ for its curvature operator in the same operator convention as the ambient curvature, and $S_h$ for its scalar curvature. Explicitly distinguish the lowered tensor from the operator pairing by setting
$$\mathcal R^g(A,B,C,D):=g(R^g(C,D)B,A),\qquad \mathcal R^h(A,B,C,D):=h(R^h(C,D)B,A).$$
Thus $\mathcal R^g_{abcd}=R_{abcd}$ in [[def-gr-curvature-tensor-and-derived-tensors]]; in particular $g(R^g(X,Y)Z,W)=\mathcal R^g(W,Z,X,Y)$. Let $G$ be the Einstein tensor defined there. At every $p\in\Sigma$ and for all $X,Y,Z,W\in T_p\Sigma$:

**(a) Gauss equation.**
$$\mathcal R^g(X,Y,Z,W)=\mathcal R^h(X,Y,Z,W)+K(X,Z)K(Y,W)-K(X,W)K(Y,Z).$$
Equivalently, in operator order,
$$g(R^g(X,Y)Z,W)=h(R^h(X,Y)Z,W)+K(Y,Z)K(X,W)-K(X,Z)K(Y,W).$$

**(b) Codazzi equation.**
$$g(R^g(X,Y)Z,n)=(D_YK)(X,Z)-(D_XK)(Y,Z).$$

**(c) Normal projections.** Define $(\operatorname{div}_hK)(Y)=h^{ij}(D_{e_i}K)(e_j,Y)$, $\tau=\operatorname{tr}_hK=h^{ij}K_{ij}$ and $|K|_h^2=h^{ik}h^{jl}K_{ij}K_{kl}$. Then
$$G(n,n)=\tfrac12(S_h+\tau^2-|K|_h^2),\qquad G(n,Y)=(\operatorname{div}_hK)(Y)-D_Y\tau.$$

**(d) Constraint equations.** If the tensor equation $G+\Lambda g=\kappa T$ holds at $p$, for a smooth symmetric covariant $2$-tensor $T$ and real constants $\kappa,\Lambda$, then
$$S_h+\tau^2-|K|_h^2=2\Lambda+2\kappa T(n,n),\qquad (\operatorname{div}_hK)(Y)-D_Y\tau=\kappa T(n,Y).$$
With $\rho=T(n,n)$ and $j(Y)=-T(n,Y)$, the second equation is $(\operatorname{div}_hK)(Y)-D_Y\tau=-\kappa j(Y)$.

Work in the frame conventions of
[[def-gr-dust-reduction-variables-and-gauge]] and let $E_{ij},B_{ij}$ be
symmetric spatial tracefree fields, that is $E_{ij}U^j=B_{ij}U^j=0$ and $h^{ij}E_{ij}=h^{ij}B_{ij}=0$. Define $C$ by the
reconstruction formula of
[[def-gr-dust-electric-magnetic-weyl-variables-and-schouten]] clause (d). Then:

**(a)** $C_{ijkl}$ is antisymmetric in $(i,j)$ and in $(k,l)$, symmetric under
the exchange of the pairs $(ij)\leftrightarrow(kl)$, satisfies the first
Bianchi (cyclic) identity $C_{i[jkl]}=0$, and is trace-free in every pair of
contracted indices;

**(b)** the electric and magnetic parts of $C$ with respect to $U$ are
$C_{0i0j}=E_{ij}$ and $C^*{}_{0i0j}=B_{ij}$;

**(c)** consequently if $E,B$ are in addition trace-free with respect to $h$,
then $C$ is a Weyl tensor and the map $(E,B)\mapsto C$ is a bijection onto the
Weyl tensors with the given $U$-electric and $U$-magnetic parts.

Work in the reduction conventions of
[[def-gr-dust-reduction-variables-and-gauge]] with $q:=U(r)+r\chi=0$ (the
dust continuity equation in the comoving gauge) and let $E,B$ be the
electric-magnetic variables of
[[def-gr-dust-electric-magnetic-weyl-variables-and-schouten]]. Then:

**(a) [Weyl evolution]** the reduced Weyl equations are
$$0=P_{ij}=\mathcal L_UE_{ij}+D_kB_{l(i}\epsilon_{j)}{}^{kl}-3\chi_{(i}{}^lE_{j)l}-2\chi^l{}_{(i}E_{j)l}+h_{ij}\chi^{kl}E_{kl}+2\chi E_{ij}+\tfrac12\kappa r\bigl(\chi_{(ij)}-\tfrac13\chi h_{ij}\bigr),$$
$$0=Q_{ij}=\mathcal L_UB_{ij}-D_kE_{l(i}\epsilon_{j)}{}^{kl}-\chi^l{}_{(i}B_{j)l}-2\chi_{(i}{}^lB_{j)l}+\chi B_{ij}+\chi^{kl}B^{pq}\epsilon_{pk(i}\epsilon_{qlj)},$$
where $\mathcal L_U$ is the Lie derivative along $U$ and the bracket on the
indices $i,j$ has weight $\tfrac12$; they are obtained by projecting the
Bianchi identity of the prescribed curvature onto the symmetric tracefree
spatial parts, the density-derivative terms cancelling by $q=0$;

**(b) [trace preservation]** extend the displayed symmetric equations of (a) algebraically to all symmetric spatial $E,B$. Contracting this extension with $h^{ij}$ gives $U(t_E)+2\chi t_E=0$ and $U(t_B)=0$, where $t_T=h^{ij}T_{ij}$. Thus
$h^{ij}E_{ij}$ and $h^{ij}B_{ij}$ satisfy homogeneous transport equations along
$U$; consequently zero initial traces remain zero, and the evolution may be
restricted to the five-dimensional tracefree space;

**(c) [transport equations]** with the parallel-comoving gauge one has
$$\partial_se_a{}^\mu=-\Gamma_a{}^j{}_0e_j{}^\mu,\qquad \partial_s\Gamma_a{}^i{}_j=R^{\mathrm{pre}\,i}{}_{j0a}-\Gamma_k{}^i{}_j\Gamma_a{}^k{}_0,\qquad \partial_sr=-r\chi,$$
the first two expressing zero time torsion and zero time-curvature residual, the
third the continuity equation; for tentative data the frame bracket is used in
the curvature definition so that these hold identically;

**(d) [symmetric hyperbolicity]** the system of (a) and (c), together with the
definition of the extrinsic curvature variables, is a first-order quasilinear
system for $(e_a{}^\mu,\Gamma_a{}^i{}_j,E_{ij},B_{ij},r)$ which is symmetric
hyperbolic on a spacelike initial surface: with the positive spatial Frobenius
product, the principal symmetric-tensor curl
$$(C(\xi)B)_{ij}=\epsilon_{kl(i}\xi^kB_{j)}{}^l$$
is skew-adjoint with operator norm at most $|\xi|$ ([[lem-gr-dust-symmetric-hyperbolic-reduction]]), so the coupled block
$\left(\begin{smallmatrix}0&C(\xi)\\-C(\xi)&0\end{smallmatrix}\right)$ is
symmetric with the same bound, every other block is transport along $U$, and a
future-positive timelike conormal $\zeta$ (satisfying
$\zeta(U)>|\zeta_\perp|$) makes the total time matrix positive definite; in
particular the local well-posedness theorem for symmetric hyperbolic systems
applies to the reduced dust system.

Let $V$ be the real vector space of symmetric $3\times3$ matrices with the
positive Frobenius product $\langle B,B'\rangle=B^{ij}B'_{ij}$, and for
$\xi\in\mathbb R^3$ define
$$C(\xi):V\to V,\qquad (C(\xi)B)_{ij}=\epsilon_{kl(i}\xi^kB_{j)}{}^l ,$$
with indices raised and lowered by the Euclidean metric and $\epsilon$ the
Levi-Civita symbol on the spatial frame of
[[def-gr-dust-reduction-variables-and-gauge]]. Then:

**(a)** $C(\xi)$ is skew-adjoint: $\langle C(\xi)B,B'\rangle=-\langle B,C(\xi)B'\rangle$;

**(b)** $\|C(\xi)\|\le|\xi|$ for the operator norm induced by the Frobenius
product;

**(c)** the block operator $\left(\begin{smallmatrix}0&C(\xi)\\-C(\xi)&0\end{smallmatrix}\right)$
on $V\oplus V$ is symmetric (self-adjoint) with operator norm at most $|\xi|$;

**(d)** if $\zeta$ is a covector with $\zeta(U)=z$ and spatial part
$\zeta_\perp$, the symbol matrix
$\left(\begin{smallmatrix}zI&C(\zeta_\perp)\\-C(\zeta_\perp)&zI\end{smallmatrix}\right)$
is positive definite whenever $z>|\zeta_\perp|$, in particular for every
future-positive timelike conormal $\zeta$; hence the reduced dust system is
symmetric hyperbolic with positive time matrix on a spacelike initial surface.

Assume Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]) and Dependent Choice ([[def-dependent-choice]]), carrying the analytic uniqueness and causal-curve supplier hypotheses.

Let a smooth reduced dust solution have a nondegenerate tentative orthonormal frame for $\gamma$ of signature $(+---)$, a metric-compatible tentative connection, reconstructed algebraic Weyl tensor $C$, prescribed curvature $\overline R$, and dust Schouten tensor $S$ as in [[def-gr-dust-reduction-variables-and-gauge]] and [[def-gr-dust-electric-magnetic-weyl-variables-and-schouten]]. $$e_0=U,\quad\Gamma_0{}^i{}_j=0,\quad T^i{}_{0a}=0,\quad\Delta^i{}_{j0a}=0,\quad P_{ab}=Q_{ab}=0,\quad q=U(r)+r\chi=0.$$
Here $a,b=1,2,3$, the first torsion index is the output index, and $P_{ab},Q_{ab}$ are the symmetric tracefree evolution projections of [[lem-gr-dust-reduced-evolution-equations]]. No spatial torsion or spatial curvature residual is assumed zero. Define $F_{jkl}=\nabla^i(C_{ijkl}-\gamma_{i[k}S_{l]j})$, $P_a=F_{0a0}$, and $Q_a=-\epsilon_a{}^{bc}F_{0bc}/2$. Then the spatial components of $(T,\Delta)$ and the vectors $(P,Q)$ satisfy the explicit closed linear homogeneous system constructed in the proof. Its principal part is transport along $U$ for $T,\Delta$ and the curl pair
$$e_0(P_a)+\tfrac12\epsilon_a{}^{bc}e_b(Q_c),\qquad e_0(Q_a)-\tfrac12\epsilon_a{}^{bc}e_b(P_c).$$
It is symmetric hyperbolic on every spacelike initial hypersurface, including one tilted relative to $U$. If all residuals vanish initially, they vanish on its metric domain of determination. derivations.claim: (Admissible data and local normalization.) Locally let $\Sigma$ be a smooth oriented three-manifold with smooth positive definite metric $h$, smooth symmetric tensor $K$, smooth $\rho_{\rm mass}\ge0$, and constants $c>0,\kappa,\Lambda$. On $\mathcal V=\mathbb RN\oplus T\Sigma$ define $\gamma(N,N)=1$, $\gamma(N,X)=0$, $\gamma(X,Y)=-h(X,Y)$. Future means positive $N$ coefficient. The original metric is $g=-\gamma$; $K(X,Y)=g(\nabla_XN,Y)$. A smooth future $\gamma$-unit section $U_0$ is prescribed. Define $$\varepsilon=\rho_{\rm mass}c^2,\qquad T_0^\gamma=\varepsilon U_0^{\flat_\gamma}\otimes U_0^{\flat_\gamma},\qquad \mathcal T_0=\kappa T_0^\gamma.$$ Here $\mathcal T_0$ is the scaled Einstein right-hand side and $T_0^\gamma$ uses the energy coefficient of the dust supplier. For $G(\gamma)-\Lambda\gamma=\mathcal T_0$ the target Ricci tensor is $$J=\kappa\varepsilon U_0^{\flat_\gamma}\otimes U_0^{\flat_\gamma}-(\Lambda+\tfrac12\kappa\varepsilon)\gamma.$$ Its trace is $-4\Lambda-\kappa\varepsilon$, and $J-\tfrac12\operatorname{tr}_\gamma(J)\gamma=\mathcal T_0+\Lambda\gamma$. No density division occurs, including at $\varepsilon=0$; there $U_0$ remains the auxiliary gauge direction. Require the four corrected constraints for these data. Arbitrary $(h,K,U_0,\varepsilon)$ need not satisfy them.

(Proper boost and full tensor transformation.) Choose an oriented local $h$-orthonormal frame $f_a$, $f_0=N$. Write uniquely $$U_0=W(N+v^af_a),\qquad W=\gamma(U_0,N)=(1-|v|^2)^{-1/2},\qquad |v|<1.$$ The explicit boosted tetrad is $$e_0=U_0,\qquad e_a=f_a+\frac{W^2}{W+1}v_av^bf_b+Wv_aN.$$ The coefficient $W^2/(W+1)=(W-1)/|v|^2$ is smooth at $v=0$. Substitution gives $\gamma(e_A,e_B)=\eta_{AB}$. The determinant is $+1$ by continuity from $v=0$ and invertibility; $e_0$ remains future. Thus the volume orientation is preserved. Additional spatial frame rotations belong to $SO(3)$ when using the same magnetic orientation. For $e_A=L_A{}^If_I$ transform the entire covariant tensors: $$R'_{ABCD}=L_A{}^IL_B{}^JL_C{}^KL_D{}^LR_{IJKL},\qquad C'_{ABCD}=L_A{}^IL_B{}^JL_C{}^KL_D{}^LC_{IJKL}.$$ The right dual is $C^*_{IJKL}=\tfrac12C_{IJ}{}^{PQ}\epsilon_{KLPQ}$. Lorentz invariance of the metric and the oriented volume tensor gives $(C')^*_{ABCD}=L_A{}^IL_B{}^JL_C{}^KL_D{}^LC^*_{IJKL}$. Then define $$E'_{ab}=C(U_0,e_a,U_0,e_b),\qquad B'_{ab}=C^*(U_0,e_a,U_0,e_b).$$ A boost generally mixes electric and magnetic parts. Separate orthogonal transformations of $E$ and $B$ are false. Invertibility concerns the full Weyl tensor; its reconstruction lemma identifies these contractions with the reduction's prescribed curvature.

(Curvature construction using the corrected supplier.) Use [L1] with slots $R_{IJKL}=\gamma(R(f_K,f_L)f_J,f_I)$ and $\operatorname{Ric}_{JL}=\gamma^{IK}R_{IJKL}$. It supplies six independent $R_{abcd}$ and eight independent $R_{0abc}$, including the cyclic relation. Define the six symmetric remaining entries by $$R_{0a0b}=J_{ab}+\sum_{c=1}^3R_{cacb}.$$ This is exactly $\operatorname{Ric}_{ab}=R_{0a0b}-\sum_cR_{cacb}=J_{ab}$. Algebraic curvature symmetries fix all other entries. The four remaining equations $\operatorname{Ric}_{00}=J_{00}$ and $\operatorname{Ric}_{0a}=J_{0a}$ follow from the corrected Hamiltonian/momentum constraints. Set $S=J-\tfrac16\operatorname{tr}_\gamma(J)\gamma$, subtract its fixed Kulkarni--Nomizu term to obtain $C$, and perform the full tensor basis change above. No normal derivative of a constraint is needed. Gauss/Codazzi signs are owned by their supplier repair, not independently duplicated here.

(Explicit initial connection.) Let $D^h$ be the Levi--Civita connection and $S_K$ satisfy $h(S_KX,Y)=K(X,Y)$. In tangent directions define $$\nabla_X(aN+Y)=\bigl(X(a)+K(X,Y)\bigr)N+aS_KX+D^h_XY\qquad(X,Y\in T\Sigma).$$ Differentiating $\gamma(aN+Y,bN+Z)=ab-h(Y,Z)$ verifies compatibility. Tangential torsion is zero because $D^h$ is torsion-free and $K$ symmetric. Differentiate the explicit boost to find every $\nabla_Xe_J$, hence $\omega(X)$, from $(h,K,U_0)$ and tangential derivatives. Specify $\omega(U_0)=0$ in this tetrad. Since $\mathcal V=T\Sigma\oplus\mathbb RU_0$, these values determine the entire initial connection one-form. For the comoving chart $e_0=\partial_s=U_0$, $\Sigma=\{s=0\}$, its conormal $\zeta=ds$ satisfies $\zeta(U_0)=1$ and initially $\zeta=N^{\flat_\gamma}/W$. Therefore $\zeta(e_a)=v_a$. In particular $e_a=v_aU_0+X_a$ with $X_a\in T\Sigma$, and $\Gamma_a=\omega(e_a)=\omega(X_a)$. Rest-frame spatial directions must not be conflated with directions tangent to the tilted surface.

(Every initial zero quantity.) The torsion two-form is $\Theta(X,Y)=
abla_XY-
abla_YX-[X,Y]$. Its tangential pullback is zero by the connection formula. The reduced frame transport equation imposes $\iota_U\Theta=0$, meaning $T^i{}_{0a}=0$ for every output index $i$. A vector-valued two-form vanishing on tangent pairs and on every $(U,V)$ pair vanishes everywhere because $\mathcal V=T\Sigma\oplus\mathbb RU$. Hence all $T$ vanish initially. Tangential connection curvature uses only tangential derivatives of its initial values. Corrected Gauss/Codazzi matches $R^{m pre}$ on all tangent direction pairs and every endomorphism slot, so the tangential pullback of $\Delta$ is zero. Reduced connection transport gives $\iota_U\Delta=0$, meaning $\Delta^i{}_{j0a}=0$ for every $i,j,a$. The same two-form argument gives all $\Delta=0$. This uses reduced first jets, not a presumed Einstein development. The positive reduced time matrix below determines those jets uniquely. Density transport fixes $q=U(\varepsilon)+\varepsilon\chi=0$. Parallel gauge gives $
abla_UU=0$, hence $q_a=\varepsilon(
abla_UU)_a=0$ in the corrected residual normalization. No division by $\varepsilon$ occurs. The reduced Weyl equations give symmetric trace-free $P_{ab}=Q_{ab}=0$ at the initial first jet.

(Tilted differential Bianchi initialization.) By [L3], the explicit residual definition and $q_j=0$ give the identity $$\operatorname{cyclic}_{jkl}\nabla_jR^{\rm pre\,i}{}_{mkl}=\tfrac12\epsilon_{jkl}{}^pF_{prs}\epsilon_m{}^{irs}.$$ The identity uses left/right Hodge decomposition and contracted Schouten conservation. Pull back $D_\omega\Delta=-D_\omega R^{\rm pre}$ to three tangent slots. The pullback of $\Delta$ is identically zero along the slice, so its intrinsic covariant exterior derivative vanishes. Torsion pullback zero removes the exterior/covariant correction. Thus the displayed cyclic tensor vanishes on tangent triples. Contracting three tangent directions into the volume tensor gives a nonzero multiple of the normal conormal $\zeta^p$; invertibility of the endomorphism-pair Hodge map yields $\zeta^pF_{prs}=0$. This uses only tangential derivatives, and assumes no transverse derivative of constraints or residuals zero. With $P_{ab}=Q_{ab}=q=q_a=0$, the corrected split is $$F_{jkl}=2U_jP_{[k}U_{l]}+h_{j[k}P_{l]}+Q_i\bigl(U_j\epsilon^i{}_{kl}-\epsilon^i{}_{j[k}U_{l]}\bigr).$$ Here $P_a=F_{0a0}$, $Q_a=-\tfrac12\epsilon_a{}^{bc}F_{0bc}$, brackets have weight $1/2$, $h_{ab}=-\delta_{ab}$ and $\epsilon^i{}_{ab}=-\epsilon_{iab}$. All four component families are $$F_{0a0}=P_a,\quad F_{0ab}=-Q_i\epsilon_{iab},\quad F_{ba0}=\tfrac12Q_i\epsilon_{iba},\quad F_{bac}=\tfrac12(-\delta_{ba}P_c+\delta_{bc}P_a).$$ For $z=\zeta(U)>0$ and $w_a=\zeta(e_a)$, contract the $(a,0)$ components and take the negative half spatial dual of the $(a,c)$ components: $$zP+\tfrac12w\times Q=0,\qquad zQ-\tfrac12w\times P=0.$$ The exact matrix is $M=\left(\begin{smallmatrix}zI&X(w)/2\\-X(w)/2&zI\end{smallmatrix}\right)$ with $X(w)b=w\times b$. Since $X(w)^T=-X(w)$ it is symmetric, and $$\langle(P,Q),M(P,Q)\rangle=z(|P|^2+|Q|^2)+P\cdot(w\times Q)\ge(z-|w|/2)(|P|^2+|Q|^2).$$ Timelike $\zeta$ gives $z>|w|$, hence $P=Q=0$; the four component families give every $F=0$. All initial quantities $(T,\Delta,F,q)$ required by the subsidiary theorem are therefore zero, by its explicit corrected dual identity. For reduced Weyl evolution the separately established curl bound is $\|C(w)\|\le|w|$. Its symmetric time matrix has lower bound $(z-|w|)(|E|^2+|B|^2)$, while transport blocks have factor $z$. Initially $z=1,w=v$, so the evolution bound is $1-|v|>0$, and the residual bound is $1-|v|/2>0$. These are distinct matrices. Arbitrary $|v|<1$, vacuum points and every $c>0$ remain allowed.

Step 1.1 admits density epsilon=0 with separately specified U0; step 1.2 uses W²/(W+1), smooth at v=0, rather than the apparent singular quotient by |v|².

citations.quote:
Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]) and let $\Sigma\subseteq M$ be a
spacelike embedded hypersurface in the sense of
[[def-gr-spacelike-hypersurfaces-and-cauchy-sets]] clause (a), so that
$\Sigma$ is an embedded three-dimensional submanifold
([[def-embedded-submanifold-and-slice-chart]]) and the restriction of $g_p$
to $T_p\Sigma$ is positive definite for every $p\in\Sigma$
([[def-causal-classification-of-lorentz-vectors]]). In the notation of
[[def-gr-spacelike-initial-data-and-constraints]] clause (a), whose claims
this lemma establishes:

**(a) The future unit normal.** For every $p\in\Sigma$ the orthogonal
complement $T_p\Sigma^{\perp}$ is one-dimensional, nondegenerate for $g_p$,
and negative definite: every nonzero $u\in T_p\Sigma^{\perp}$ is timelike,
$g_p(u,u)<0$. Hence there is exactly one $n_p\in T_p\Sigma^{\perp}$ with
$g_p(n_p,n_p)=-1$ and $g_p(n_p,N_p)<0$.

**(b) Smoothness along the hypersurface.** The assignment $p\mapsto n_p$ is
smooth along $\Sigma$: for every $p\in\Sigma$ there are an open neighborhood
$O$ of $p$ in $M$ and a smooth vector field $\tilde n$ on $O$
([[def-smooth-vector-field-as-a-tangent-bundle-section]]) with
$\tilde n|_{\Sigma\cap O}=n|_{\Sigma\cap O}$, and for any two such local
extensions the covariant derivative at a point of $\Sigma$ in a direction
tangent to $\Sigma$ agrees. Thus for $V\in T_p\Sigma$ the vector
$\nabla_Vn\in T_pM$ is well defined as $\nabla_{\tilde X}\tilde n|_p$ for any
smooth extensions $\tilde n$ of $n$ and $\tilde X$ of a tangent field with
$\tilde X_p=V$ ([[def-covariant-derivative-along-a-curve]],
[[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]]).

**(c) The induced metric and second fundamental form.** The **induced
metric** $h_p(V,W):=g_p(V,W)$ is a smooth Riemannian metric on $\Sigma$, and
$$K_p(V,W):=g_p(\nabla_Vn,W)\qquad(V,W\in T_p\Sigma)$$
(the **second fundamental form**) defines a smooth symmetric covariant
$2$-tensor field $K$ on $\Sigma$
([[def-gr-smooth-covariant-two-tensor-field]]) with
$$K_p(V,W)=-g_p(\nabla_VW,n_p),$$
where $\nabla_VW$ is the ambient covariant derivative at $p$ of any smooth
extension of a tangent field with value $W$ at $p$, in the direction of any
extension with value $V$ at $p$.

**(d) The shape operator.** The endomorphism $S_p:T_p\Sigma\to T_p\Sigma$
defined by $h_p(S_pV,W)=K_p(V,W)$ for all $W\in T_p\Sigma$ is well defined,
linear and self-adjoint for the positive definite form $h_p$, and the
Weingarten relation $\nabla_Vn=S_pV$ holds for every $V\in T_p\Sigma$.

For an affine connection as in [[def-affine-connection-on-a-smooth-manifold]] and coordinates $(x^1,\ldots,x^n)$, its **Christoffel symbols** in this chart are the unique smooth functions $\Gamma^k{}_{ij}$ such that
$$\nabla_{\partial_i}\partial_j=\sum_k\Gamma^k{}_{ij}\partial_k.$$
The first lower index $i$ is the differentiating direction and the second lower index $j$ labels the differentiated vector field. In the coordinate frame, the one-forms from [[def-connection-one-form-in-a-local-frame]] are $\omega^k{}_j=\sum_i\Gamma^k{}_{ij}\,dx^i$. A different chart generally has different symbols. This definition asserts neither symmetry in $i,j$ nor tensorial transformation.

For dimension one there is one smooth coefficient $\Gamma^1{}_{11}$; in dimension zero there are no coefficients. All statements are local, and at a boundary chart the derivatives are the smooth up-to-boundary coordinate derivatives.

For an affine connection as in [[def-affine-connection-on-a-smooth-manifold]] and coordinates $(x^1,\ldots,x^n)$, its **Christoffel symbols** in this chart are the unique smooth functions $\Gamma^k{}_{ij}$ such that
$$\nabla_{\partial_i}\partial_j=\sum_k\Gamma^k{}_{ij}\partial_k.$$
The first lower index $i$ is the differentiating direction and the second lower index $j$ labels the differentiated vector field. In the coordinate frame, the one-forms from [[def-connection-one-form-in-a-local-frame]] are $\omega^k{}_j=\sum_i\Gamma^k{}_{ij}\,dx^i$. A different chart generally has different symbols. This definition asserts neither symmetry in $i,j$ nor tensorial transformation.

For dimension one there is one smooth coefficient $\Gamma^1{}_{11}$; in dimension zero there are no coefficients. All statements are local, and at a boundary chart the derivatives are the smooth up-to-boundary coordinate derivatives.

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]) and let $\nabla$ be an affine connection
on $M$ ([[def-affine-connection-on-a-smooth-manifold]]). Smooth vector fields
are smooth sections of the tangent bundle
([[def-smooth-vector-field-as-a-tangent-bundle-section]]); as there, their use
rests on the canonical smooth structure of $TM$, which assumes the axiom
$\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ of [[def-countable-choice]]. This is the only use of that
axiom in this definition.

**(a) Metric compatibility.** The connection $\nabla$ is **$g$-compatible**, or
**compatible with the metric** $g$, when for all smooth vector fields $X,Y,Z$ on
$M$ the identity of smooth functions

$$X\bigl(g(Y,Z)\bigr)=g(\nabla_XY,Z)+g(Y,\nabla_XZ)$$

holds on $M$. Here $g(Y,Z)$ is the smooth function $p\mapsto g_p(Y_p,Z_p)$ and
$X$ acts on functions as a derivation; the identity uses only the action of
$\nabla$ on vector fields and requires no extension of $\nabla$ to tensor
fields. When such an extension is available, this identity is the statement
$\nabla_Xg=0$, and the compatibility of $\nabla$ with the inverse metric
$g^{-1}$ follows; neither statement is part of this definition.

**(b) Torsion freedom.** The **torsion** of $\nabla$ is the tangent-valued
$2$-tensor $T(X,Y)=\nabla_XY-\nabla_YX-[X,Y]$ of
[[def-torsion-tensor-of-an-affine-connection]], with bracket as in
[[def-lie-bracket-of-smooth-vector-fields]]. The connection is **torsion-free**
when $T(X,Y)=0$ for all smooth $X,Y$, that is, when
$\nabla_XY-\nabla_YX=[X,Y]$ identically.

**(c) Metric-selected connections.** A **metric-selected connection** for
$(M,g)$ is an affine connection on $M$ that is both torsion-free and
$g$-compatible. Equivalently, it is an element of the class

$$\operatorname{LC}(M,g):=\{\nabla:\nabla\text{ is an affine connection on }M,\ \nabla\text{ is torsion-free and }g\text{-compatible}\}.$$

The name records that the pair of conditions selects the connection out of all
affine connections; it is the pair of conditions imposed on the connection that
conventional general relativity uses, and the connection so selected is called
the **Levi–Civita connection** of $g$.

For an affine connection as in [[def-affine-connection-on-a-smooth-manifold]] and coordinates $(x^1,\ldots,x^n)$, its **Christoffel symbols** in this chart are the unique smooth functions $\Gamma^k{}_{ij}$ such that
$$\nabla_{\partial_i}\partial_j=\sum_k\Gamma^k{}_{ij}\partial_k.$$
The first lower index $i$ is the differentiating direction and the second lower index $j$ labels the differentiated vector field. In the coordinate frame, the one-forms from [[def-connection-one-form-in-a-local-frame]] are $\omega^k{}_j=\sum_i\Gamma^k{}_{ij}\,dx^i$. A different chart generally has different symbols. This definition asserts neither symmetry in $i,j$ nor tensorial transformation.

For dimension one there is one smooth coefficient $\Gamma^1{}_{11}$; in dimension zero there are no coefficients. All statements are local, and at a boundary chart the derivatives are the smooth up-to-boundary coordinate derivatives.

Let $M$ and $N$ be smooth manifolds, let $F:M\to N$ be a map, let $p\in M$ and
let $r\in\mathbb N_0\cup\{\infty\}$, where $\mathbb N_0=\{0,1,2,\ldots\}$.
For $m,q\in\mathbb N_0$ and an open set $E\subseteq\mathbb R^m$, a map
$g:E\to\mathbb R^q$ is **of class $C^r$** as follows. When $m=0$, every such
map is declared $C^r$. When $m\ge1$, each component $g_l$ with $l<q$ must be
$C^r$ in the sense of
[[def-ck-and-multi-index-notation-in-several-variables]]; when $q=0$ this
component condition is vacuous.
Suppose $F$ is continuous at $p$. Then $F$ is **of class $C^r$ at $p$** when
there are smooth charts $(U,\varphi)$ of $M$ at $p$ and $(V,\psi)$ of $N$ at
$F(p)$ with $F(U)\subseteq V$ such that the coordinate representative

$$\psi\circ F\circ\varphi^{-1}:\varphi(U)\longrightarrow\psi(V)$$

([[def-coordinate-representation-of-a-map]]) is of class $C^r$ on a
neighbourhood of $\varphi(p)$ in this componentwise Euclidean sense. By
[[lem-chart-independence-of-c-r-smoothness]], this condition is independent of
the chosen charts: if one such representative is $C^r$, then every one is, so
"some charts" may be read as "any charts". A map is **$C^r$ on an open set**
$W\subseteq M$ when it is continuous on $W$ and $C^r$ at every point of $W$. A
map that is $C^r$ for every finite $r$ — equivalently $C^\infty$ — is called
**smooth**; the term **$C^r$ map between smooth manifolds** is reserved for the
case where $F$ is continuous and the representative condition holds at every
point of $M$.

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]) with metric-selected connection $\nabla$
([[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]],
[[thm-gr-nondegenerate-levi-civita-and-tensor-derivative]]) and let
$U\subseteq M$ be an open set carrying a fixed smooth **background metric**
$\bar g$ with Levi-Civita connection $\bar\nabla$
([[thm-gr-nondegenerate-levi-civita-and-tensor-derivative]]), whose Christoffel
symbols in any chart are $\bar\Gamma^a{}_{bc}$
([[def-christoffel-symbols-of-an-affine-connection]]); the same symbol
$\Gamma^a{}_{bc}$ denotes those of $g$. Let $\kappa>0$ and $\Lambda\in\mathbb R$
be constants and let $T$ be a smooth symmetric covariant $2$-tensor field on $U$
([[def-gr-smooth-covariant-two-tensor-field]]), the **matter stress-energy
tensor**, with $T=g^{ab}T_{ab}$ its metric trace
([[def-gr-inverse-metric-and-musical-isomorphisms]]).

**(a) Gauge vector.** The **harmonic-gauge vector field** of the pair
$(g,\bar g)$ is the smooth vector field
$$H^a:=g^{bc}\bigl(\Gamma^a{}_{bc}-\bar\Gamma^a{}_{bc}\bigr) .$$
The difference of the connection coefficients is a $(1,2)$-tensor, so $H$ is a
well-defined smooth vector field independent of the chart used to express the
symbols ([[def-gr-tensor-fields-and-components]]).

**(b) Reduced Einstein equation.** The **reduced Einstein equation** for the
pair $(g,T)$ with respect to $\bar g$ is the second-order quasilinear system
$$\operatorname{Ric}_{ab}-\nabla_{(a}H_{b)}=\kappa\bigl(T_{ab}-\tfrac12Tg_{ab}\bigr)+\Lambda g_{ab},$$
where $\operatorname{Ric}_{ab}$ is the Ricci tensor of $g$
([[def-gr-curvature-tensor-and-derived-tensors]]),
$H_b=g_{bc}H^c$ and $\nabla_{(a}H_{b)}=\tfrac12(\nabla_aH_b+\nabla_bH_a)$.

**(c) Reduced solutions.** A **reduced solution** on $U$ is a pair $(g,T)$ of a
smooth Lorentzian metric and a smooth symmetric $2$-tensor on $U$ satisfying
(b) for the fixed background $\bar g$.

**(d) Einstein residual.** The **Einstein residual** of a pair $(g,T)$ is the
smooth symmetric $2$-tensor
$$E_{ab}:=G_{ab}+\Lambda g_{ab}-\kappa T_{ab},\qquad G_{ab}=\operatorname{Ric}_{ab}-\tfrac12Sg_{ab},$$
with $S=g^{ab}\operatorname{Ric}_{ab}$ the scalar curvature
([[def-gr-curvature-tensor-and-derived-tensors]]). The pair solves the Einstein
equation exactly when $E=0$.

**(e) Constraint equations.** If $g$ is defined on a neighborhood of a spacelike
hypersurface $\Sigma$ with future unit normal field $\mathfrak n$ and tangential
frame $(e_i)$ ([[def-gr-spacelike-initial-data-and-constraints]]), the
**constraint residuals** are the functions $E(\mathfrak n,\mathfrak n)$ and
$E(\mathfrak n,e_i)$ on $\Sigma$; that these are the normal and
normal-tangential projections of the field equation, and that they agree with
the Hamiltonian and momentum constraint equations of the initial data, is
recorded in [[lem-gr-constraint-projections]] and
[[def-gr-spacelike-initial-data-and-constraints]].

The definition introduces the objects only. The principal part of (b), its
first-order symmetric hyperbolic reduction, the identity expressing $E$ through
$H$, the wave equation satisfied by $H$ and the propagation of the constraint
residuals are proved in [[lem-gr-reduced-einstein-principal-part]],
[[thm-gr-reduced-einstein-local-existence]],
[[lem-gr-einstein-residual-and-subsidiary-identity]] and
[[thm-gr-harmonic-constraint-propagation]].

derivations.claim: (Existence of the metric germ and its slice geometry (a).) Prescribe a smooth metric on a product neighborhood whose value and $s$-derivative on $\Sigma$ are the displayed jet and whose higher jets are chosen arbitrarily smooth; such a metric germ exists because a smooth function and its first normal derivative can be prescribed on a hypersurface and extended smoothly. On $\Sigma$, $g_{00}=-1$, $g_{0i}=0$, $g_{ij}=h_{ij}$, so $g$ restricted to $T\Sigma$ is $h$ and $\partial_s$ is a unit timelike vector orthogonal to $\Sigma$; by [L1] it is the future unit normal (with the orientation of the statement) and the second fundamental form is $\tfrac12\partial_sg_{ij}=K_{ij}$. This is (a).

(Computation of $H^0$.) Insert the Christoffel components [L2], [L3] into [L4]: $H^0=g^{00}(\Gamma^0{}_{00}-\bar\Gamma^0{}_{00})+g^{ij}(\Gamma^0{}_{ij}-\bar\Gamma^0{}_{ij})+2g^{0i}(\Gamma^0{}_{0i}-\bar\Gamma^0{}_{0i})=-(\operatorname{tr}_hK-0)+h^{ij}(K_{ij}-0)+0=-\operatorname{tr}_hK+\operatorname{tr}_hK=0$ on $\Sigma$.

(Computation of $H^i$.) Work in the reduction conventions of
[[def-gr-dust-reduction-variables-and-gauge]], with a smooth tentative frame
$(e_0,e_1,e_2,e_3)$, $e_0=U$, dual coframe $\theta^i(e_j)=\delta^i_j$ and smooth
metric-compatible tentative connection coefficients $\Gamma_i{}^k{}_j$.
The connection acts on every tensor index by the tensor product rule and
annihilates $\gamma$; torsion-freeness is not assumed. A differential $k$-form
is a smooth alternating covariant $k$-tensor. The wedge is its alternating
tensor product, normalized so that for a $p$-form $\alpha$ and a $q$-form
$\beta$, $\alpha\wedge\beta$ is the sum over $(p,q)$ shuffles with their signs.
The exterior derivative is specified, for smooth fields $X_0,\ldots,X_k$, by
$$d\alpha(X_0,\ldots,X_k)=\sum_{a=0}^k(-1)^aX_a\bigl(\alpha(X_0,\ldots,\widehat X_a,\ldots,X_k)\bigr)+\sum_{a<b}(-1)^{a+b}\alpha([X_a,X_b],X_0,\ldots,\widehat X_a,\ldots,\widehat X_b,\ldots,X_k).$$
Here a hat deletes a slot, and the undeleted slots in the second sum retain
their order. These definitions fix the local frame-coordinate calculus.

**(a) Connection forms.** The **connection $1$-forms** are
$\omega^i{}_j:=\Gamma_k{}^i{}_j\,\theta^k$, and the **torsion $2$-forms** and
**curvature $2$-forms** are the Cartan expressions
$$\Theta^i:=d\theta^i+\omega^i{}_j\wedge\theta^j,\qquad \Omega^i{}_j:=d\omega^i{}_j+\omega^i{}_k\wedge\omega^k{}_j .$$
Components are denoted
$\Theta^i=\tfrac12\Theta^i{}_{jk}\theta^j\wedge\theta^k$ and similarly for
$\Omega$. The actual curvature uses the frame bracket in its component formula:
$R^i{}_{jkl}=\partial_k\Gamma_l{}^i{}_j-\partial_l\Gamma_k{}^i{}_j+\Gamma_k{}^i{}_m\Gamma_l{}^m{}_j-\Gamma_l{}^i{}_m\Gamma_k{}^m{}_j-\Gamma_m{}^i{}_j\,[e_k,e_l]^m$,
not the antisymmetrized connection coefficients alone, precisely so that no
torsion conclusion is assumed.

**(b) Curvature residual.** With the prescribed curvature $R^{\mathrm{pre}}$
of [[def-gr-dust-electric-magnetic-weyl-variables-and-schouten]] the
**curvature residual $2$-forms** are
$$\Delta^i{}_j:=\Omega^i{}_j-\tfrac12R^{\mathrm{pre}\,i}{}_{jkl}\,\theta^k\wedge\theta^l .$$

**(c) Bianchi and matter residuals.** Using the reconstructed $C$ and
prescribed $S$ of [[def-gr-dust-electric-magnetic-weyl-variables-and-schouten]],
define
$$F_{jkl}:=\nabla_i\bigl(C^i{}_{jkl}-\delta^i{}_{[k}S_{l]j}\bigr),\qquad q_j:=\nabla_i(rU^iU_j),\qquad q:=U(r)+r\chi,$$
with brackets of weight $\tfrac12$. The full flux covector satisfies
$q_j=qU_j+r\nabla_UU_j$, since $\nabla_iU^i=\chi$ in the acceleration-free
gauge. In particular $q=0$ and $\nabla_UU=0$ imply $q_j=0$ even where $r=0$.
This normalization uses the coefficient $r$ of the source tensor and does
not divide by $r$ or $\kappa$.

**(d) Zero quantities and reduced premises.** Write
$\mathcal T^i{}_{jk}:=\Theta^i(e_j,e_k)$, also denoted $T^i{}_{jk}$ when
unambiguous; this torsion tensor is distinct from the stress-energy tensor.
The **zero quantities** are
$$z:=\bigl(\mathcal T^i{}_{jk},\ \Delta^i{}_{jkl},\ F_{jkl},\ q_j\bigr).$$
The reduced transport equations impose only
$\mathcal T^i{}_{0a}=0$ and $\Delta^i{}_{j0a}=0$, and density transport imposes
$q=0$; the gauge gives $\nabla_UU=0$. Weyl evolution imposes the symmetric
spatial evolution projections of $F$. The reduced evolution does not itself
impose every component of $z=0$. The subsidiary theorem propagates the
remaining zero quantities from constrained initial data.

For vector-valued forms define $D_\omega\alpha=d\alpha+\omega\wedge\alpha$;
for an endomorphism-valued $k$-form define
$D_\omega\alpha=d\alpha+\omega\wedge\alpha-(-1)^k\alpha\wedge\omega$, with
matrix multiplication of endomorphism indices. These conventions specify the
Cartan identities used in [[thm-gr-dust-subsidiary-and-residual-vanishing]].

Work in the reduction conventions of
[[def-gr-dust-reduction-variables-and-gauge]]: $\gamma$ is the signature
$(+---)$ metric, $U$ the unit future timelike vector $U=n$, $r=\rho c^2$, the
frame $(e_0,e_1,e_2,e_3)$ is $\gamma$-orthonormal with $e_0=U$,
$\gamma(e_i,e_j)=\eta_{ij}$ on spatial pairs, and indices are moved with
$\gamma$.

**(a) Schouten tensor.** The **reduction Schouten tensor** of $\gamma$ is
$$S_{ij}:=\operatorname{Ric}_{ij}-\tfrac16S_\gamma\,\gamma_{ij},$$
where $\operatorname{Ric}$ and $S_\gamma=\gamma^{ab}\operatorname{Ric}_{ab}$ are
the Ricci tensor and scalar curvature of $\gamma$
([[def-gr-curvature-tensor-and-derived-tensors]]). If the dust field equation
$G(\gamma)-\Lambda\gamma=\kappa\,r\,U^\flat\otimes U^\flat$ holds, then
$$S_{ij}=\kappa r\Bigl(U_iU_j-\tfrac13\gamma_{ij}\Bigr)-\tfrac13\Lambda\,\gamma_{ij}.$$
This normalization is fixed so that the standard Kulkarni--Nomizu decomposition
$$R_{ijkl}=C_{ijkl}+\tfrac12\bigl(S_{ik}\gamma_{jl}-S_{il}\gamma_{jk}+S_{jl}\gamma_{ik}-S_{jk}\gamma_{il}\bigr)$$
holds for every metric of dimension four, with $C$ the Weyl tensor
([[def-gr-curvature-tensor-and-derived-tensors]]); the identity is checked on
constant-curvature metrics in the Remarks.

**(b) Prescribed curvature.** The **prescribed curvature tensor** of a
configuration $(C,E,B,r)$ is the tensor field with frame components
$$R^{\mathrm{pre}}{}_{ijkl}:=C_{ijkl}+\tfrac12\bigl(S_{ik}\gamma_{jl}-S_{il}\gamma_{jk}+S_{jl}\gamma_{ik}-S_{jk}\gamma_{il}\bigr),\qquad S_{ij}\text{ as in (a)} ,$$
where $C=C[E,B]$ is the Weyl tensor reconstructed from the electric and
magnetic variables in (d). A **tentative reduced configuration** is a smooth assignment
$(e_a{}^\mu,\Gamma_a{}^i{}_j,E_{ij},B_{ij},r)$ in the gauge of
[[def-gr-dust-reduction-variables-and-gauge]]. Equality of its actual curvature
with $R^{\mathrm{pre}}$ is the curvature constraint, rather than an assumption
on the independent unknowns. Reduced evolution enforces its time components;
the residual theorem establishes the remaining components from constrained
initial data. This distinction keeps the tentative connection available before
torsion-freeness and the full curvature constraint are proved.

**(c) Electric and magnetic Weyl variables.** For a smooth Weyl-type tensor $C$
of type $(0,4)$ with the curvature symmetries write
$C^*{}_{ijkl}:=\tfrac12C_{ij}{}^{pq}\epsilon_{klpq}$ for its right dual
([[def-gr-dust-reduction-variables-and-gauge]] clause (c) for
$\epsilon_{ijkl}$). The **electric and magnetic parts with respect to $U$** are
the spatial fields
$$E_{ij}:=C_{0i0j},\qquad B_{ij}:=C^*{}_{0i0j},$$
with frame indices; they are symmetric and spatial in all indices and
trace-free with respect to $h$ whenever $C$ has the Weyl symmetries.

**(d) Reconstruction formula.** Define the dependent tensor
$$C_{ijkl}:=2\bigl(l_{j[k}E_{l]i}-l_{i[k}E_{l]j}\bigr)-2\bigl(U_{[k}B_{l]p}\epsilon^p{}_{ij}+U_{[i}B_{j]p}\epsilon^p{}_{kl}\bigr),$$
with brackets of weight $\tfrac12$ and $l_{ij}=h_{ij}-U_iU_j$; this expression
is the **reconstruction** of a Weyl tensor from a pair $(E,B)$ of symmetric
spatial trace-free fields. The verification that the reconstructed tensor has
the curvature antisymmetries, pair symmetry, cyclic identity and zero traces —
and that its electric and magnetic parts recover $(E,B)$ — is the content of
[[lem-gr-dust-weyl-reconstruction-from-electric-magnetic]].

The definition fixes the objects and conventions only; the evolution and
subsidiary equations, the initial-data determination and the local existence
theorem are proved in the items named above and in
[[lem-gr-dust-reduced-evolution-equations]] and
[[thm-gr-dust-local-evolution]].

Work in the frame conventions of
[[def-gr-dust-reduction-variables-and-gauge]] and let $E_{ij},B_{ij}$ be
symmetric spatial tracefree fields, that is $E_{ij}U^j=B_{ij}U^j=0$ and $h^{ij}E_{ij}=h^{ij}B_{ij}=0$. Define $C$ by the
reconstruction formula of
[[def-gr-dust-electric-magnetic-weyl-variables-and-schouten]] clause (d). Then:

**(a)** $C_{ijkl}$ is antisymmetric in $(i,j)$ and in $(k,l)$, symmetric under
the exchange of the pairs $(ij)\leftrightarrow(kl)$, satisfies the first
Bianchi (cyclic) identity $C_{i[jkl]}=0$, and is trace-free in every pair of
contracted indices;

**(b)** the electric and magnetic parts of $C$ with respect to $U$ are
$C_{0i0j}=E_{ij}$ and $C^*{}_{0i0j}=B_{ij}$;

**(c)** consequently if $E,B$ are in addition trace-free with respect to $h$,
then $C$ is a Weyl tensor and the map $(E,B)\mapsto C$ is a bijection onto the
Weyl tensors with the given $U$-electric and $U$-magnetic parts.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$
([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $s\ge5$, let $A^\mu,B$ be a periodic symmetric
hyperbolic coefficient family on the open set $O\subseteq\mathbb R^m$, let
$K\subseteq O$ be compact and $R\ge0$.

**(a) Uniqueness.** Let $J\ni0$ be an open interval and let
$u,v:J\to H^s(\mathbb T^3_{2\pi};\mathbb R^m)$ be classical solutions of
$(\star)$ in the sense of clause (d) of
[[def-gr-periodic-symmetric-hyperbolic-system]], both taking values in $K$ and
satisfying $\sup_{t\in J}\|u(t)\|_{H^s}\le R$, $\sup_{t\in J}\|v(t)\|_{H^s}\le R$.
If $u(0)=v(0)$, then $u=v$ on $J$.

**(b) Continuous dependence.** Let $K'\subseteq O$ be compact with
$K\subseteq\operatorname{int}K'$ and let $T>0$ be a time for which the existence
theorem [[thm-gr-periodic-symmetric-hyperbolic-existence]] produces solutions
from every datum with values in $K$ and norm at most $R$, with values in $K'$
and the bounds $C(1+R)$ of that theorem. Then for all such data $u_0,v_0$ with
solutions $u,v$
$$\|u(t)-v(t)\|_{H^{s-1}}\le C'\,e^{C'|t|}\,\|u_0-v_0\|_{H^{s-1}}\qquad(|t|<T),$$
with $C'=C'(A^\mu,B,K',R,s)$, the fixed compact coefficient time slab containing $[-T,T]$ being included in the coefficient data.

The gauge gives $
abla_UU=0$; therefore the full conservation vector $q_j:=
abla^i(rU_iU_j)=qU_j+r(
abla_UU)_j$ vanishes, including at $r=0$. Since $S=\kappa r(UU-\gamma/3)$ plus a parallel constant metric multiple, $
abla^jS_{lj}=-\kappa
abla_lr/3=
abla_l\operatorname{tr}_\gamma S$. The Weyl cyclic and trace identities now decompose $F$, with the reduced evolution projections zero, into the linear map $A$ defined by $$A(P,Q)_{jkl}:=2U_jP_{[k}U_{l]}+h_{j[k}P_{l]}+Q_i(U_j\epsilon^i{}_{kl}-\epsilon^i{}_{j[k}U_{l]}),\qquad F=A(P,Q).$$ Indeed the unreduced decomposition has the additional terms $-2P_{j[k}U_{l]}-Q_{ji}\epsilon^i{}_{kl}-\kappa h_{j[k}q_{l]}/2-\kappa qh_{j[k}U_{l]}/3$; the symmetric tracefree parts are $P_{ab},Q_{ab}$, its traces are the conservation quantities, and the remaining antisymmetric parts are fixed by the cyclic identity. All these additional terms vanish by the reduced equations and gauge. Thus every Bianchi residual is represented by the two constraint vectors.

Cartan differentiation gives $D_\omega\Theta=\Omega\wedge\theta$ and $D_\omega\Omega=0$ by $d^2=0$. Algebraic cyclic symmetry gives $\overline R^{\mathrm{form}}\wedge\theta=0$, hence $D_\omega\Theta=\Delta\wedge\theta$. The reduced equations mean exactly $\iota_U\Theta=\iota_U\Delta=0$, while the gauge gives $\iota_U\omega=0$. Contracting yields the exact torsion transport equation $$\mathcal L_U\Theta^i=\Delta^i{}_0.$$ The right side has endomorphism input index $0$, not a time form index. Its principal derivative is $e_0(T^i{}_{ab})$; converting the Lie derivative to frame components adds only coefficient times $T$, since $[U,e_a]=-\Gamma_a{}^k{}_0e_k$. In particular $T^0{}_{ab}$ need not vanish.

Put $\overline B^i{}_{mjkl}:=\sum_{\mathrm{cyc}(jkl)}
abla_j\overline R^i{}_{mkl}$. The algebraic dual identity, using conservation from step 1.1, is $$\overline B^i{}_{mjkl}=	frac12\epsilon_{jkl}{}^pF_{prs}\epsilon_m{}^{irs}.$$ For completeness split $\overline R=C+E+G$, where $E$ is its tracefree-Schouten part and $G$ its scalar-curvature part. Left and right Hodge duals agree on $C,G$ and have opposite sign on $E$, as follows by inserting $\gamma_{i[k}S_{l]j}-\gamma_{j[k}S_{l]i}$ and contracting the two volume tensors. Apply these identities to $
abla\overline R$ and contract the derivative with the right dual. The Weyl and Schouten derivative terms give $F$; the remaining trace terms are $
abla^jS_{lj}-
abla_l\operatorname{tr}S=\kappa q_l=0$. This proves the displayed identity without assuming vanishing torsion. The principal derivative is $e_0(\Delta^i{}_{mab})$; all frame conversion terms are algebraic in $\Delta$.

Define the following linear lower-order maps of $v=(P,Q)$ by exact subtraction: $$L(v)_a:=\nabla^jA(v)_{ja0}-e_0(P_a)-\tfrac12\epsilon_a{}^{bc}e_b(Q_c),$$ $$M(v)_a:=-\tfrac12\epsilon_a{}^{bc}\nabla^jA(v)_{jbc}-e_0(Q_a)+\tfrac12\epsilon_a{}^{bc}e_b(P_c).$$ Inserting $A$ shows that all derivatives of $P,Q$ cancel in these definitions; $L,M$ depend only linearly on $v$, with coefficients from $\Gamma$. Indeed its rest-frame families are $A_{0a0}=P_a$, $A_{0ab}=Q_i\epsilon^i{}_{ab}$, $A_{ba0}=-Q_i\epsilon^i{}_{ba}/2$, and $A_{bac}=h_{b[a}P_{c]}$. Contracting step 2.1 now gives the exact curl equations $$e_0(P_a)+\tfrac12\epsilon_a{}^{bc}e_b(Q_c)=H_{a0}-L(v)_a,$$ $$e_0(Q_a)-\tfrac12\epsilon_a{}^{bc}e_b(P_c)=-\tfrac12\epsilon_a{}^{bc}H_{bc}-M(v)_a.$$ Together with steps 1.2--2.2 these constitute a closed linear homogeneous system in spatial $T$, spatial $\Delta$, $P,Q$. Its coefficient functions are smooth functions of the fixed reduced solution and its first derivatives; no derivative of a residual occurs on a right side.

With the positive Euclidean spatial product, the curl symbol $X(w)v=w\times v$ is skew-adjoint and has norm at most $|w|$. At a future-positive timelike conormal $\zeta$, put $z=\zeta(U)$ and $w_a=\zeta(e_a)$. The curl-pair symbol is the symmetric block $\left(\begin{smallmatrix}zI&X(w)/2\\-X(w)/2&zI\end{smallmatrix}\right)$, bounded below by $z-|w|/2$; the transport blocks are $zI$.
