Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold, let $\bar g$
be a smooth background metric with Levi-Civita connection $\bar\nabla$, and let
$H^a=g^{bc}(\Gamma^a{}_{bc}-\bar\Gamma^a{}_{bc})$ be the harmonic-gauge vector
of [[def-gr-harmonic-gauge-and-reduced-equations]]. Then:

**(a) [principal part]** Let $\hat g$ be a smooth Lorentzian metric on an open
set $U\subseteq M$ and let $h$ be a smooth symmetric covariant $2$-tensor on
$U$. The derivative at $\hat g$ in the direction $h$ of the operator
$g\mapsto\operatorname{Ric}_{ab}[g]-\bar\nabla_{(a}H_{b)}[g]$ equals
$$-\tfrac12\hat g^{cd}\,\bar\nabla_c\bar\nabla_d h_{ab}+L_{ab}(h,\bar\nabla h;\hat g,\bar g),$$
where $L$ is a smooth expression linear in $h$ and its first
$\bar\nabla$-derivatives with coefficients built from $\hat g,\hat g^{-1},\bar g$
and the background curvature. In particular the principal symbol is
$-\tfrac12\hat g^{cd}\xi_c\xi_d$ times the identity on the metric slot at every
covector $\xi$.

**(b) [first-order reduction]** Fix a chart $(x^0,x^1,x^2,x^3)$ with
$x^0=t$. Introduce the metric variables
$$u:=\bigl(g_{ab},\ p_{ab}:=\bar\nabla_0g_{ab},\ q_{abi}:=\bar\nabla_ig_{ab}\bigr)$$
(symmetry in $a,b$ understood) and the relation variables $\bar\nabla_0g_{ab}-p_{ab}=0$ and $\bar\nabla_0q_{abi}-\bar\nabla_ip_{ab}=\mathcal C_{abi}$, where $\mathcal C_{abi}=-\bar R^c{}_{a0i}g_{cb}-\bar R^c{}_{b0i}g_{ac}$. Second covariant derivatives include their derivative-slot connection. These known background-curvature terms are zeroth order in the first-order state and vanish for the flat coordinate background. Then the reduced Einstein equation can be solved for the second time derivatives in the form
$$\bar\nabla_0p_{ab}=-(g^{00})^{-1}\Bigl[2g^{0i}\bar\nabla_ip_{ab}+g^{ij}\bar\nabla_iq_{abj}+R_{ab}(u;\bar g)\Bigr],$$
and the resulting first-order system for $u$ is symmetric hyperbolic on every
region where $g^{00}<0$ and the spatial block $(g^{ij})$ is positive definite:
the coefficient of $\bar\nabla_0u$ is the block diagonal
$\operatorname{diag}(I,-g^{00}I,g^{ij}I)$ (on the three slots
$g,p,q$), which is positive definite there, and the coefficients of the spatial
derivatives are symmetric.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$
([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $s\ge5$, let $A^\mu,B$ be a periodic symmetric
hyperbolic coefficient family on the open set $O\subseteq\mathbb R^m$, let
$K\subseteq\operatorname{int}K'\subseteq O$ be compact, let $R\ge0$, and let
$T>0$ and $C$ be as in [[thm-gr-periodic-symmetric-hyperbolic-existence]] for
the class $\mathcal S(K,R)$; for every datum $u_0\in\mathcal S(K,R)$ let $u$ be
the solution produced there on $(-T,T)$ with values in $K'$. Then:

**(a) [local existence]** For every $u_0\in\mathcal S(K,R)$ and every
$x_0\in\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}$ the solution $u$ is $C^1$ on a neighborhood of
$(0,x_0)$ in $(-T,T)\times\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}$ and solves $(\star)$ pointwise
there.

**(b) [finite speed / independence of the extension]** Let $\lambda_0>0$ be
determined by the coefficient bounds on a compact set containing the values of
the solutions in the following sense: for a truncated cone
$$D:=\{(t,x):0\le t\le t_0,\ d(x,x_0)\le\lambda(t_0-t)\}$$
with $t_0<T$, $\lambda\ge\lambda_0$, lying in a single chart of $\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}$
in which the coordinate representation of $A^\mu$ satisfies
$\lambda\,A^0+\xi_iA^i\ge0$ for all unit $\xi$ (which holds for $\lambda$ large
enough by clause (a) of [[lem-gr-finite-speed-independence-of-extension]]),
let $u,v$ be solutions of two periodic symmetric hyperbolic systems whose
coefficient functions agree on a neighborhood of $D$ in the independent variables and on one common open state set containing both solution ranges, with
$u(0,\cdot)=v(0,\cdot)$ on the ball $\{d(x,x_0)\le\lambda t_0\}$. Then
$u=v$ on $D$.

**(c) [local uniqueness and stability]** If two classical solutions of the same
system on a common interval have values in $K$, $H^s$ norms at most $R$ and the
same initial value, they coincide; and the continuous-dependence estimate of
[[thm-gr-periodic-symmetric-hyperbolic-uniqueness-stability]] clause (b) holds
for the solutions of clause (a).

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$
([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $s\ge5$, let $A^\mu,B$ be a periodic symmetric
hyperbolic coefficient family on the open set $O\subseteq\mathbb R^m$
([[def-gr-periodic-symmetric-hyperbolic-system]]) and let $K\subseteq O$ be
compact, and let $K'\subseteq O$ be compact with $K$ contained in the
interior of $K'$. Then for every $R\ge0$ there are a time $T>0$ and a constant
$C$ (depending on $A^\mu,B,K,K',s$ and on $R$) such that:

for every $u_0\in H^s(\mathbb T^3_{2\pi};\mathbb R^m)$ taking values in $K$ with
$\|u_0\|_{H^s}\le R$ there is a Sobolev solution
$u:(-T,T)\to H^s(\mathbb T^3_{2\pi};\mathbb R^m)$ of $(\star)$ with
$u(0)=u_0$ which is classical and satisfies
$$u\in L^\infty((-T,T);H^s)\cap C^0((-T,T);H^{s-1}),\quad \partial_tu\in L^\infty((-T,T);H^{s-1}),$$
$$\sup_{|t|<T}\|u(t)\|_{H^s}\le C(1+R),\qquad \sup_{|t|<T}\|\partial_tu(t)\|_{H^{s-1}}\le C(1+R),$$
and whose values lie in $K'$.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$
([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $s\ge5$, let $A^\mu,B$ be a periodic symmetric
hyperbolic coefficient family on the open set $O\subseteq\mathbb R^m$, let
$K\subseteq\operatorname{int}K'\subseteq O$ be compact, let $R\ge0$, and let
$T>0$ and $C$ be as in [[thm-gr-periodic-symmetric-hyperbolic-existence]] for
the data class $\mathcal S(K,R)$. Let $u_0\in C^\infty(\mathbb T^3_{2\pi};\mathbb R^m)$
take values in $K$ and satisfy $\|u_0\|_{H^s}\le R$. Then the solution $u\in L^\infty((-T,T);H^s)\cap C^0H^{s-1}$
of that theorem with $u(0)=u_0$ satisfies $u\in L^\infty((-T,T);H^m)$ and
$\partial_tu\in L^\infty((-T,T);H^{m-1})$ for every $m\ge s$, with bounds
depending only on $m$, $T$, $R$, the coefficient family, $K'$ and the $H^j$ bounds
of $u_0$ for $j\le m$; consequently $u\in C^\infty((-T,T)\times\mathbb T^3_{2\pi})$
and solves $(\star)$ classically.

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]) and let $\Sigma\subseteq M$ be a
spacelike embedded hypersurface in the sense of
[[def-gr-spacelike-hypersurfaces-and-cauchy-sets]] clause (a), so that
$\Sigma$ is an embedded three-dimensional submanifold
([[def-embedded-submanifold-and-slice-chart]]) and the restriction of $g_p$
to $T_p\Sigma$ is positive definite for every $p\in\Sigma$
([[def-causal-classification-of-lorentz-vectors]]). In the notation of
[[def-gr-spacelike-initial-data-and-constraints]] clause (a), whose claims
this lemma establishes:

**(a) The future unit normal.** For every $p\in\Sigma$ the orthogonal
complement $T_p\Sigma^{\perp}$ is one-dimensional, nondegenerate for $g_p$,
and negative definite: every nonzero $u\in T_p\Sigma^{\perp}$ is timelike,
$g_p(u,u)<0$. Hence there is exactly one $n_p\in T_p\Sigma^{\perp}$ with
$g_p(n_p,n_p)=-1$ and $g_p(n_p,N_p)<0$.

**(b) Smoothness along the hypersurface.** The assignment $p\mapsto n_p$ is
smooth along $\Sigma$: for every $p\in\Sigma$ there are an open neighborhood
$O$ of $p$ in $M$ and a smooth vector field $\tilde n$ on $O$
([[def-smooth-vector-field-as-a-tangent-bundle-section]]) with
$\tilde n|_{\Sigma\cap O}=n|_{\Sigma\cap O}$, and for any two such local
extensions the covariant derivative at a point of $\Sigma$ in a direction
tangent to $\Sigma$ agrees. Thus for $V\in T_p\Sigma$ the vector
$\nabla_Vn\in T_pM$ is well defined as $\nabla_{\tilde X}\tilde n|_p$ for any
smooth extensions $\tilde n$ of $n$ and $\tilde X$ of a tangent field with
$\tilde X_p=V$ ([[def-covariant-derivative-along-a-curve]],
[[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]]).

**(c) The induced metric and second fundamental form.** The **induced
metric** $h_p(V,W):=g_p(V,W)$ is a smooth Riemannian metric on $\Sigma$, and
$$K_p(V,W):=g_p(\nabla_Vn,W)\qquad(V,W\in T_p\Sigma)$$
(the **second fundamental form**) defines a smooth symmetric covariant
$2$-tensor field $K$ on $\Sigma$
([[def-gr-smooth-covariant-two-tensor-field]]) with
$$K_p(V,W)=-g_p(\nabla_VW,n_p),$$
where $\nabla_VW$ is the ambient covariant derivative at $p$ of any smooth
extension of a tangent field with value $W$ at $p$, in the direction of any
extension with value $V$ at $p$.

**(d) The shape operator.** The endomorphism $S_p:T_p\Sigma\to T_p\Sigma$
defined by $h_p(S_pV,W)=K_p(V,W)$ for all $W\in T_p\Sigma$ is well defined,
linear and self-adjoint for the positive definite form $h_p$, and the
Weingarten relation $\nabla_Vn=S_pV$ holds for every $V\in T_p\Sigma$.

For an affine connection as in [[def-affine-connection-on-a-smooth-manifold]] and coordinates $(x^1,\ldots,x^n)$, its **Christoffel symbols** in this chart are the unique smooth functions $\Gamma^k{}_{ij}$ such that
$$\nabla_{\partial_i}\partial_j=\sum_k\Gamma^k{}_{ij}\partial_k.$$
The first lower index $i$ is the differentiating direction and the second lower index $j$ labels the differentiated vector field. In the coordinate frame, the one-forms from [[def-connection-one-form-in-a-local-frame]] are $\omega^k{}_j=\sum_i\Gamma^k{}_{ij}\,dx^i$. A different chart generally has different symbols. This definition asserts neither symmetry in $i,j$ nor tensorial transformation.

For dimension one there is one smooth coefficient $\Gamma^1{}_{11}$; in dimension zero there are no coefficients. All statements are local, and at a boundary chart the derivatives are the smooth up-to-boundary coordinate derivatives.

Let $F:M\to N$ be a smooth map and let $p\in M$. If $dF_p:T_pM\to T_{F(p)}N$ is
an isomorphism, then there are open neighbourhoods $U$ of $p$ and $V$ of
$F(p)$ such that $F|_U:U\to V$ is a diffeomorphism.

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold and let
$\nabla$ be its metric-selected connection, whose existence and uniqueness are
supplied by [[thm-gr-nondegenerate-levi-civita-and-tensor-derivative]]; its
Christoffel symbols are the smooth chart functions of
[[def-christoffel-symbols-of-an-affine-connection]]. Recall that a **geodesic**
is a curve with $D_t\gamma'=0$ in its parameter
([[def-geodesic-of-an-affine-connection]],
[[def-covariant-derivative-along-a-curve]]).

**(a) Local existence, uniqueness and maximality.** For every $(p,v)\in TM$
there is a unique maximal geodesic $\gamma_{p,v}:I_{p,v}\to M$ with
$\gamma_{p,v}(0)=p$ and $\gamma_{p,v}'(0)=v$; its domain $I_{p,v}$ is an open
interval containing $0$ and is not asserted to be all of $\mathbb R$.

**(b) Smooth dependence.** The set
$\mathcal G:=\{(t,p,v):t\in I_{p,v}\}\subseteq\mathbb R\times TM$ is open, and
the evaluation map $(t,p,v)\mapsto\gamma_{p,v}(t)$ is smooth on $\mathcal G$.

**(c) Scaling.** For every $s\in\mathbb R$ and every $t\in\mathbb R$,
$t\in I_{p,sv}$ if and only if $st\in I_{p,v}$, and then
$\gamma_{p,sv}(t)=\gamma_{p,v}(st)$.

**(d) The exponential map.** Define $\mathcal E_p:=\{v\in T_pM:1\in I_{p,v}\}$
and $\exp_p:\mathcal E_p\to M$, $\exp_p(v):=\gamma_{p,v}(1)$, and let
$\psi_p:T_pM\to\mathbb R^4$ be the coordinate isomorphism of a basis
$e_0,\dots,e_3$ of $T_pM$. Then $\mathcal E_p$ is open and star-shaped about
$0$ (if $v\in\mathcal E_p$ and $0\le s\le1$, then $sv\in\mathcal E_p$),
$\exp_p$ is smooth, $\exp_p(0)=p$, and, under the canonical identification
$T_0(T_pM)\cong T_pM$ and the chart $x=\psi_p$ on $T_0M$,
$$d(\exp_p)_0=\operatorname{id}_{T_pM}.$$
Consequently there is a star-shaped open neighborhood $W_p\subseteq\mathcal E_p$
of $0$ such that $\exp_p|_{W_p}$ is a diffeomorphism onto an open subset of
$M$.

Let $M$ be a smooth four-manifold without boundary and let $g$ be a smooth
symmetric covariant $2$-tensor field on $M$ such that $g_p$ is nondegenerate at
every $p\in M$ ([[def-gr-smooth-covariant-two-tensor-field]],
[[def-gr-inverse-metric-and-musical-isomorphisms]]). This holds in particular
when $(M,g,N)$ is a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold and $g$ is
its metric ([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]). For smooth vector fields
$X,Y,Z$ put

$$K(X,Y,Z):=X\bigl(g(Y,Z)\bigr)+Y\bigl(g(Z,X)\bigr)-Z\bigl(g(X,Y)\bigr)+g([X,Y],Z)+g([Z,X],Y)-g([Y,Z],X),$$

with brackets as in [[def-lie-bracket-of-smooth-vector-fields]].

**(a) Existence and formulas.** There is exactly one affine connection
$\nabla$ on $M$ ([[def-affine-connection-on-a-smooth-manifold]]) satisfying

$$2g(\nabla_XY,Z)=K(X,Y,Z)\qquad\text{for all smooth }X,Y,Z .$$

It is torsion-free and $g$-compatible, so it is a metric-selected connection
for $(M,g)$ ([[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]]); in every smooth chart its
Christoffel symbols are

$$\Gamma^a{}_{bc}=\tfrac12\,g^{ad}\bigl(\partial_bg_{dc}+\partial_cg_{bd}-\partial_dg_{bc}\bigr),$$

with $g^{ad}$ the inverse-metric components
([[def-gr-inverse-metric-and-musical-isomorphisms]],
[[def-christoffel-symbols-of-an-affine-connection]]).

**(b) Uniqueness.** If an affine connection $\nabla'$ on $M$ is torsion-free
and $g$-compatible, then $\nabla'=\nabla$. Consequently the class
$\operatorname{LC}(M,g)$ of metric-selected connections has exactly one
element; it is the **Levi–Civita connection** of $g$.

**(c) Induced derivative on tensor fields.** Let $\nabla^*$ be the dual
connection on $T^*M$ and let the product connection of
[[def-product-connection-on-tensor-and-hom-bundles]] act on the tensor bundles
of [[def-gr-tensor-fields-and-components]]. Then, in every smooth chart, for
every smooth tensor field $T$ of type $(r,s)$,

$$T^{a_1\cdots a_r}{}_{b_1\cdots b_s;c}=\partial_cT^{a_1\cdots a_r}{}_{b_1\cdots b_s}+\sum_{i=1}^{r}\Gamma^{a_i}{}_{dc}\,T^{a_1\cdots d\cdots a_r}{}_{b_1\cdots b_s}-\sum_{j=1}^{s}\Gamma^{d}{}_{b_jc}\,T^{a_1\cdots a_r}{}_{b_1\cdots d\cdots b_s},$$

where the slot marked $d$ replaces the named index; this derivative commutes
with every contraction in the sense of [[def-contraction-of-a-mixed-tensor]],
and it annihilates the metric and the inverse metric:

$$g_{ab;c}=0,\qquad g^{ab}{}_{;c}=0 .$$

If Omega has the specified finite piecewise $C^1$ presentation and $F\in C^1(\overline\Omega;\mathbb R^n)$, then $\int_\Omega\operatorname{div}F=\sum_j\int_{S_j}F\cdot\nu_j\,dS$, with faces counted once off E. Let $t_0\le T$, let $u,a,b:[t_0,T]\to\mathbb R$ be continuous, with $u,b\ge0$, and suppose

$$u(t)\le a(t)+\int_{t_0}^t b(s)u(s)\,ds.$$

Then

$$u(t)\le a(t)+\int_{t_0}^t a(s)b(s)\exp\!\left(\int_s^t b(r)\,dr\right)ds.$$

If $a$ is nondecreasing, this gives $u(t)\le a(t)\exp(\int_{t_0}^t b)$. The time-reflected form assumes $u(t)\le a(t)+\int_t^{t_0}b(s)u(s)\,ds$ for $t\le t_0$. In particular, when $a=A\ge0$ and $b=B\ge0$ are constant, the two orientations give $u(t)\le A e^{B|t-t_0|}$.

Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ ([[def-countable-choice]]). Every open cover of a smooth manifold has a countable cover by coordinate balls with compact closures, each closure contained in one member of the original cover.

Assume countable choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. Let $(U_n)_{n\ge 1}$ be a countable cover of a smooth manifold $M$ by coordinate balls with compact closures. Then there is an at-most-countable index set $I$ and families of open sets $(W_k)_{k\in I}$ and coordinate balls $(V_k)_{k\in I}$ such that $M=\bigcup_{k\in I} W_k$, each $\overline{W_k}\subseteq V_k\subseteq \overline{V_k}\subseteq U_{n(k)}$ for some index $n(k)$, and the family $(V_k)$ is locally finite. The index set may be finite or empty.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $X$ be a smooth vector field on $M$ with maximal flow $\Phi$, and let
$S\hookrightarrow M$ be an embedded codimension-one submanifold. If $X_p\notin T_pS$
for every $p\in S$, then there is an open neighbourhood
$\mathcal O\subseteq \mathbb R\times S$ of $\{0\}\times S$ such that the map

$$ F:\mathcal O\to M,\qquad F(t,p)=\Phi_t(p), $$

is an embedding. Its image is a flowout of $S$ along $X$.

On each physical development solve $$\Box_gx^\mu=0,\quad x^0|_\Sigma=0,\quad x^i|_\Sigma=y^i,\quad n(x^0)|_\Sigma=1,\quad n(x^i)|_\Sigma=0.$$ Start in an orthogonal slice chart obtained by normal geodesic flow [L3]. For each scalar use $(f,P=\partial_0f,Q_i=\partial_if)$, with $\partial_0f=P$, $\partial_0Q_i=\partial_iP$, and the wave equation. Integrating the difference energy over a shrinking ball with speed $\lambda>b/a$ gives nonnegative lateral flux and $E\prime\le CE$, so zero common initial data imply zero difference by Gronwall. This removes dependence on the extensions. Since $\partial_0(Q_i-\partial_if)=0$ and the residual vanishes initially, the resulting scalars solve the original wave equations. (Injective normal collars for arbitrary embedded initial surfaces.) Apply [L5]'s flowout theorem to the global smooth future orientation field $N$, which is transverse to the spacelike hypersurface. Restrict the flowout domain to a variable-width product strip, obtaining an open ambient neighborhood $U$ of the surface with smooth projection $\pi:U	o\Sigma$ and with $j(\Sigma)$ closed relative to $U$ as the zero section. Obtain a countable locally finite cover $W_i$ with $K_i=\overline{W_i}\subset V_i$ compact and with $V_i$ relatively compact and locally finite, using [L5]. Compactness and continuity give a width $\epsilon_i>0$ such that $E$ is defined, has invertible derivative, and has $E(( -\epsilon_i,\epsilon_i)	imes K_i)\subset\pi^{-1}(V_i)$. For every pair $(i,j)$ with $V_i\cap V_j
e\varnothing$, there is a symmetric pair width $	au_{ij}=	au_{ji}>0$ excluding collisions between distinct $(s,p),(t,q)$ with $p\in K_i,q\in K_j$ and $|s|,|t|<	au_{ij}$: around each diagonal pair $(p,p)$, local injectivity supplies an open product neighborhood with such a width; finitely many cover the compact diagonal part. Outside their union the remaining subset of $K_i	imes K_j$ is compact and contains no diagonal pair, so $E(0,p)=j(p)
e j(q)=E(0,q)$. The Hausdorff property gives disjoint neighborhoods of these two images, and continuity and a finite subcover give a uniform positive width preventing collisions on that remaining compact subset. Thus the pair width exists without any global closedness of $j(\Sigma)$ in $M$. Each $\overline{V_i}$ meets only finitely many $V_j$, by compactness and local finiteness; choose $\delta_i>0$ less than $\epsilon_i$ and all these finitely many pair widths. Then $E$ is injective and a local diffeomorphism on $ igcup_i(-\delta_i,\delta_i)	imes W_i$: a collision would force $V_i\cap V_j
e\varnothing$ by the projection confinement and is then excluded by $	au_{ij}$. It is therefore a diffeomorphism onto an open neighborhood of $j(\Sigma)$. A positive smooth width can be chosen inside this union: let $ho_i$ be a locally finite partition subordinate to $W_i$ and put $f(p)=	frac12\sum_i\delta_iho_i(p)$. At each point the finite weighted average is at most the largest active $\delta_i$, and the corresponding active index has $p\in W_i$, so $|s|<f(p)$ lies in the union. (Matched Cauchy jets.) In these physical wave charts $\Box_gx^\mu=-g^{ab}\Gamma^\mu{}_{ab}=0$ throughout, hence harmonic gauge holds relative to the flat comparison metric. Initially $g_{00}=-1,g_{0i}=0,g_{ij}=h_{ij}$ and $\partial_0=n$. Their tangential derivatives agree, and [L2] gives $\partial_0g_{ij}=2K_{ij}$. The Christoffel formula yields $$g^{ab}\Gamma^0{}_{ab}=\tfrac12\partial_0g_{00}+\operatorname{tr}_hK,\qquad g^{ab}\Gamma^\ell{}_{ab}=-h^{\ell i}\partial_0g_{0i}+h^{jk}\Gamma(h)^\ell{}_{jk}.$$ Therefore both metric initial jets are identical, with $$\partial_0g_{00}=-2\operatorname{tr}_hK,\qquad \partial_0g_{0i}=h_{i\ell}h^{jk}\Gamma(h)^\ell{}_{jk}.$$ The admissibility hypothesis gives identical initial matter variables $w=\mathcal I(h,K,d)$. No second jet of a gauge map is inferred from its first jet.

(Same coupled PDE uniqueness.) On a common smaller coordinate cylinder the extracted variables $z_1,z_2$ solve the identical coefficient system by covariance and the reduction hypothesis. Write $v=z_1-z_2$. Subtraction and the integral mean-value formula for the coefficients give $$A^\mu(x,z_1)\partial_\mu v+C(x)v=0,$$ with $C$ smooth and bounded; coefficient differences multiply bounded first derivatives of $z_2$. Let $a>0$ bound $A^0$ below and let $b$ bound $\sup_{|\xi|=1}\|\sum_i\xi_iA^i\|$ on this cylinder. Choose $\lambda>b/a$. For the shrinking ball $B_t$ of radius $r-\lambda t$, differentiation of $E(t)=\int_{B_t}v^{\mathsf T}A^0v$, the difference equation and [L4] give $$E'(t)\le cE(t)-\int_{\partial B_t}v^{\mathsf T}(\lambda A^0+\nu_iA^i)v\,dS\le cE(t).$$ Indeed the lateral matrix is at least $(\lambda a-b)I$, and coefficient derivatives are bounded. Step 2.1 gives $E(0)=0$, so Gronwall gives $v=0$ in the cone. Repeat with reversed time; the two cone interiors contain a neighborhood of the smaller initial ball. Reconstruction gives equality of metric, all matter fields and stress tensors. This compares the entire coupled model, not an evolution equation for $T$ inferred from conservation.

(Isometry and overlap uniqueness.) If $X,X'$ are the wave-coordinate maps, step 3.1 gives $\Phi=(X')^{-1}\circ X$ with the stated pullback equalities. Their data give $\Phi\circ j=j'$ and $d\Phi(n)=n'$; shrink to preserve future orientation. Any other future isometry fixing the initial patch has the same differential on $T\Sigma$ and sends $n$ to $n'$ by normal uniqueness. It preserves the connection by [L3] and therefore the affinely parametrized normal geodesics. Both maps satisfy $$\Phi(\exp_{j(\sigma)}(sn_\sigma))=\exp'_{j'(\sigma)}(sn'_\sigma).$$ The normal exponential map has differential $(V,c)\mapsto dj(V)+cn$ at the zero section, an isomorphism, so its local charts prove equality of the two maps near the patch. This is uniqueness of the isometry germ, not uniqueness of arbitrary diffeomorphisms that restrict to the identity.

(Whole-surface isometry.) In the injective normal collars of step 1.2, every local isometry of step 4.1 is the single map $E'\circ E^{-1}$ wherever its normal geodesic segment stays in its local domain. Take the union of all smaller open normal-coordinate product domains on which the entire segment stays in one local isometry domain; each initial point lies in one such domain, so this union contains the entire zero section without a point-indexed choice. Restrict both collars to that same union. The resulting map is a smooth diffeomorphism between open neighborhoods of the initial surfaces and locally is the isometry of step 4.1, so it preserves the metric, all matter fields and future orientation everywhere. No uniform collar width, additional global closedness or additional matter hypothesis is used.

boundaries.evidence: The Statement compares two actual developments of prescribed data; empty Sigma leaves only a vacuous neighborhood comparison, while step 1.2 treats nonempty collar patches.
Zero matter stress or zero K is permitted by the fixed model, but step 2.1 still compares its complete matter Cauchy variables, not just a zero stress tensor.
Step 1.1 solves the four scalar wave-coordinate equations separately with fixed initial labels; the Statement does not vary spacetime dimension.
The nonzero coordinate Jacobian in step 1.1 and spacelike normal collar in step 1.2 give genuine chart and overlap identifications; degenerate metric data are excluded.
The isometry Statement is near the entire initial surface with variable widths; step 1.2 constructs injective collars without promising a uniform noncompact time interval.
The countable locally finite collar construction in step 1.2 uses the declared Countable Choice; no arbitrary family of full developments is selected for comparison.

Fix $\kappa>0$, $\Lambda\in\mathbb R$ and one covariant matter model: specified smooth tensor fields $\Psi$, specified equations $\mathcal E(g,\Psi)=0$, and a specified stress expression $T=\mathcal T(g,\Psi)$. Covariance means pullback by a local diffeomorphism commutes with these equations and stress expression. Fix complete smooth matter Cauchy data $d$ for this model, a smooth Riemannian metric $h$ and smooth symmetric tensor $K$ on a smooth three-manifold $\Sigma$, with $K(V,W)=g(\nabla_Vn,W)$ for the future unit normal.

The following explicit harmonic-reduction hypothesis is required. On each relatively compact initial coordinate ball, with flat comparison metric $\bar g=-(dx^0)^2+\sum_i(dx^i)^2$, specify finite first-order variables
$$z=(g_{ab},p_{ab}=\partial_0g_{ab},q_{abi}=\partial_ig_{ab},w),$$
fixed smooth extraction and reconstruction rules for $w,\Psi$, and fixed smooth coefficient functions $A^\mu(x,z),B(x,z)$ on an open state set $O$, shared by both solutions, such that:

**(R1)** Every smooth solution of this same model written in harmonic coordinates has extracted variables satisfying
$$A^0(x,z)\partial_0z+\sum_iA^i(x,z)\partial_iz+B(x,z)=0,$$

**(R3)** After shrinking a closed cylinder, both state ranges lie in one compact convex subset of $O$, coefficient first derivatives are bounded and $A^0\ge aI$ for some $a>0$.

Its germ along the initial patch is unique. These germs glue to one such isometry between open neighborhoods of the entire embedded initial surfaces. No uniform collar width or global-in-time assertion is made. This is a conditional assertion; it promises no converse characterization of its hypotheses. The iff-forward case has no additional implication to prove.

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold, let $\bar g$
be a smooth background metric with Levi-Civita connection $\bar\nabla$, and let
$H^a=g^{bc}(\Gamma^a{}_{bc}-\bar\Gamma^a{}_{bc})$ be the harmonic-gauge vector
of [[def-gr-harmonic-gauge-and-reduced-equations]]. Then:

**(a) [principal part]** Let $\hat g$ be a smooth Lorentzian metric on an open
set $U\subseteq M$ and let $h$ be a smooth symmetric covariant $2$-tensor on
$U$. The derivative at $\hat g$ in the direction $h$ of the operator
$g\mapsto\operatorname{Ric}_{ab}[g]-\bar\nabla_{(a}H_{b)}[g]$ equals
$$-\tfrac12\hat g^{cd}\,\bar\nabla_c\bar\nabla_d h_{ab}+L_{ab}(h,\bar\nabla h;\hat g,\bar g),$$
where $L$ is a smooth expression linear in $h$ and its first
$\bar\nabla$-derivatives with coefficients built from $\hat g,\hat g^{-1},\bar g$
and the background curvature. In particular the principal symbol is
$-\tfrac12\hat g^{cd}\xi_c\xi_d$ times the identity on the metric slot at every
covector $\xi$.

**(b) [first-order reduction]** Fix a chart $(x^0,x^1,x^2,x^3)$ with
$x^0=t$. Introduce the metric variables
$$u:=\bigl(g_{ab},\ p_{ab}:=\bar\nabla_0g_{ab},\ q_{abi}:=\bar\nabla_ig_{ab}\bigr)$$
(symmetry in $a,b$ understood) and the relation variables $\bar\nabla_0g_{ab}-p_{ab}=0$ and $\bar\nabla_0q_{abi}-\bar\nabla_ip_{ab}=\mathcal C_{abi}$, where $\mathcal C_{abi}=-\bar R^c{}_{a0i}g_{cb}-\bar R^c{}_{b0i}g_{ac}$. Second covariant derivatives include their derivative-slot connection. These known background-curvature terms are zeroth order in the first-order state and vanish for the flat coordinate background. Then the reduced Einstein equation can be solved for the second time derivatives in the form
$$\bar\nabla_0p_{ab}=-(g^{00})^{-1}\Bigl[2g^{0i}\bar\nabla_ip_{ab}+g^{ij}\bar\nabla_iq_{abj}+R_{ab}(u;\bar g)\Bigr],$$
and the resulting first-order system for $u$ is symmetric hyperbolic on every
region where $g^{00}<0$ and the spatial block $(g^{ij})$ is positive definite:
the coefficient of $\bar\nabla_0u$ is the block diagonal
$\operatorname{diag}(I,-g^{00}I,g^{ij}I)$ (on the three slots
$g,p,q$), which is positive definite there, and the coefficients of the spatial
derivatives are symmetric.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$
([[def-countable-choice]]). Fix an integer $m\ge1$, an open set
$O\subseteq\mathbb R^m$ with the subspace topology and a nondegenerate open
interval $I\subseteq\mathbb R$ containing $0$. All functions on
$\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}$ are those of [[def-gr-periodic-torus-and-sobolev-spaces]],
and smoothness on $I\times\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}\times O$ means smoothness of the
representative in the sense of clause (e) of that item.

**(a) Coefficients.** A **periodic symmetric hyperbolic coefficient family** on
$O$ consists of smooth maps
$$A^\mu:I\times\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}\times O\to\operatorname{Sym}_m(\mathbb R)\quad(\mu=0,1,2,3),\qquad B:I\times\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}\times O\to\mathbb R^m,$$
such that $A^0(t,x,u)$ is positive definite for every
$(t,x,u)\in I\times\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}\times O$; here
$\operatorname{Sym}_m(\mathbb R)$ is the real vector space of symmetric
$m\times m$ matrices, identified with symmetric endomorphisms of $\mathbb R^m$
through the standard coordinate inner product, and positive definiteness means
$z^TA^0(t,x,u)z>0$ for every nonzero $z\in\mathbb R^m$
([[def-ck-and-multi-index-notation-in-several-variables]]).

**(b) The system.** The associated **symmetric hyperbolic system** is
$$A^0(t,x,u)\,\partial_tu+\sum_{i=1}^3A^i(t,x,u)\,\partial_iu+B(t,x,u)=0 .\qquad(\star)$$

**(c) Values and norms.** A map $u:J\to H^s(\mathbb T^3_{2\pi};\mathbb R^m)$
on an interval $J$ **takes values in a set $E\subseteq\mathbb R^m$** when
$u(t)(x)\in E$ for every $t\in J$ and every $x\in\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}$, with
$u(t)$ read through its continuous representative when $s>3/2$. For compact
$K\subseteq O$ and $R\ge0$ put
$$\mathcal S(K,R):=\bigl\{u_0\in H^s(\mathbb T^3_{2\pi};\mathbb R^m):u_0\text{ takes values in }K,\ \|u_0\|_{H^s}\le R\bigr\}.$$

**(d) Classical solutions.** Let $s\ge2$. A **classical solution of $(\star)$ on
$J\times\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}$** is a $C^1$ map
$u:J\times\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}\to\mathbb R^m$ with $u(t,x)\in O$ for all
$(t,x)$ and $(\star)$ satisfied at every point, such that
$u\in L^\infty(J;H^s)$ and $\partial_tu\in L^\infty(J;H^{s-1})$. (For $s\ge2$
the embedding clause gives a continuous representative, so the pointwise
conditions are meaningful.)

**(e) Sobolev solutions.** Let $s\ge5$ and let $J$ be an open interval. A map
$u:J\to H^s(\mathbb T^3_{2\pi};\mathbb R^m)$ is a **Sobolev solution of
$(\star)$ on $J$** when

1. $u\in L^\infty(J;H^s)\cap C^0(J;H^{s-1})$ and the distributional time
   derivative $\partial_tu$ lies in $L^\infty(J;H^{s-1})$;
2. $u$ takes values in $O$;
3. for almost every $t\in J$ the identity $(\star)$ holds in
   $L^2(\mathbb T^3_{2\pi};\mathbb R^m)$, the coefficients being composed with
   the continuous representative of $u(t)$; all products are defined because
   $A^0(t,\cdot,u(t))$ and $A^i(t,\cdot,u(t))$ lie in $H^s$ with norm bounded
   by a function of $\|u(t)\|_{H^s}$, $\partial_tu(t)$ and $\partial_iu(t)$ lie
   in $H^{s-1}$, and $B(t,\cdot,u(t))$ lies in $H^s$.

**(f) Initial data.** **Initial data for $(\star)$ at time $0$** are a class
$u_0\in H^s(\mathbb T^3_{2\pi};\mathbb R^m)$ with $s\ge5$ whose values lie in a
compact subset of $O$; a solution **has initial value $u_0$** when
$u(t)\to u_0$ in $H^{s-1}$ as $t\to0$ within $J$.

The definition introduces the system and its solution classes only; existence,
uniqueness, continuous dependence and smooth persistence are asserted and
proved in [[thm-gr-periodic-symmetric-hyperbolic-existence]],
[[thm-gr-periodic-symmetric-hyperbolic-uniqueness-stability]] and
[[thm-gr-periodic-symmetric-hyperbolic-smooth-persistence]].

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$
([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $s\ge5$, let $A^\mu,B$ be a periodic symmetric
hyperbolic coefficient family on the open set $O\subseteq\mathbb R^m$
([[def-gr-periodic-symmetric-hyperbolic-system]]) and let $K\subseteq O$ be
compact, and let $K'\subseteq O$ be compact with $K$ contained in the
interior of $K'$. Then for every $R\ge0$ there are a time $T>0$ and a constant
$C$ (depending on $A^\mu,B,K,K',s$ and on $R$) such that:

for every $u_0\in H^s(\mathbb T^3_{2\pi};\mathbb R^m)$ taking values in $K$ with
$\|u_0\|_{H^s}\le R$ there is a Sobolev solution
$u:(-T,T)\to H^s(\mathbb T^3_{2\pi};\mathbb R^m)$ of $(\star)$ with
$u(0)=u_0$ which is classical and satisfies
$$u\in L^\infty((-T,T);H^s)\cap C^0((-T,T);H^{s-1}),\quad \partial_tu\in L^\infty((-T,T);H^{s-1}),$$
$$\sup_{|t|<T}\|u(t)\|_{H^s}\le C(1+R),\qquad \sup_{|t|<T}\|\partial_tu(t)\|_{H^{s-1}}\le C(1+R),$$
and whose values lie in $K'$.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$
([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $s\ge5$, let $A^\mu,B$ be a periodic symmetric
hyperbolic coefficient family on the open set $O\subseteq\mathbb R^m$, let
$K\subseteq\operatorname{int}K'\subseteq O$ be compact, let $R\ge0$, and let
$T>0$ and $C$ be as in [[thm-gr-periodic-symmetric-hyperbolic-existence]] for
the data class $\mathcal S(K,R)$. Let $u_0\in C^\infty(\mathbb T^3_{2\pi};\mathbb R^m)$
take values in $K$ and satisfy $\|u_0\|_{H^s}\le R$. Then the solution $u\in L^\infty((-T,T);H^s)\cap C^0H^{s-1}$
of that theorem with $u(0)=u_0$ satisfies $u\in L^\infty((-T,T);H^m)$ and
$\partial_tu\in L^\infty((-T,T);H^{m-1})$ for every $m\ge s$, with bounds
depending only on $m$, $T$, $R$, the coefficient family, $K'$ and the $H^j$ bounds
of $u_0$ for $j\le m$; consequently $u\in C^\infty((-T,T)\times\mathbb T^3_{2\pi})$
and solves $(\star)$ classically.

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a smooth time-oriented Lorentzian four-manifold, let
$\Sigma\subseteq M$ be a smooth spacelike hypersurface
([[def-gr-spacelike-hypersurfaces-and-cauchy-sets]]) with future unit normal
field $\mathfrak n$ and tangential frame $(e_i)$
([[lem-gr-spacelike-hypersurface-normal-and-second-fundamental-form]]), and let
$U$ be an open neighborhood of $\Sigma$ carrying a smooth background metric
$\bar g$ and a smooth symmetric tensor $T$ with $\nabla^aT_{ab}=0$ on $U$. Let
$H$ and $E$ be the gauge vector and Einstein residual of
[[def-gr-harmonic-gauge-and-reduced-equations]]. Suppose:

1. $(g,T)$ solves the reduced Einstein equation on $U$;
2. $H=0$ on $\Sigma$;
3. the constraint residuals vanish on $\Sigma$: $E(\mathfrak n,\mathfrak n)=0$
   and $E(\mathfrak n,e_i)=0$ for all $i$.

Then there is an open neighborhood $W\subseteq U$ of $\Sigma$ on which $H=0$ and
$E=0$; consequently $G_{ab}+\Lambda g_{ab}=\kappa T_{ab}$ on $W$, so $g$ solves
the Einstein equation with the prescribed matter tensor there.

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold, and let $\Sigma\subseteq M$ be a smooth spacelike embedded hypersurface with future unit normal $n$, induced Riemannian metric $h$ and second fundamental form $K(X,Y)=g(\nabla_Xn,Y)$ ([[def-gr-spacelike-hypersurfaces-and-cauchy-sets]], [[lem-gr-spacelike-hypersurface-normal-and-second-fundamental-form]]). Write $D$ for the Levi-Civita connection of $h$, $R^h$ for its curvature operator in the same operator convention as the ambient curvature, and $S_h$ for its scalar curvature. Explicitly distinguish the lowered tensor from the operator pairing by setting
$$\mathcal R^g(A,B,C,D):=g(R^g(C,D)B,A),\qquad \mathcal R^h(A,B,C,D):=h(R^h(C,D)B,A).$$
Thus $\mathcal R^g_{abcd}=R_{abcd}$ in [[def-gr-curvature-tensor-and-derived-tensors]]; in particular $g(R^g(X,Y)Z,W)=\mathcal R^g(W,Z,X,Y)$. Let $G$ be the Einstein tensor defined there. At every $p\in\Sigma$ and for all $X,Y,Z,W\in T_p\Sigma$:

**(a) Gauss equation.**
$$\mathcal R^g(X,Y,Z,W)=\mathcal R^h(X,Y,Z,W)+K(X,Z)K(Y,W)-K(X,W)K(Y,Z).$$
Equivalently, in operator order,
$$g(R^g(X,Y)Z,W)=h(R^h(X,Y)Z,W)+K(Y,Z)K(X,W)-K(X,Z)K(Y,W).$$

**(b) Codazzi equation.**
$$g(R^g(X,Y)Z,n)=(D_YK)(X,Z)-(D_XK)(Y,Z).$$

**(c) Normal projections.** Define $(\operatorname{div}_hK)(Y)=h^{ij}(D_{e_i}K)(e_j,Y)$, $\tau=\operatorname{tr}_hK=h^{ij}K_{ij}$ and $|K|_h^2=h^{ik}h^{jl}K_{ij}K_{kl}$. Then
$$G(n,n)=\tfrac12(S_h+\tau^2-|K|_h^2),\qquad G(n,Y)=(\operatorname{div}_hK)(Y)-D_Y\tau.$$

**(d) Constraint equations.** If the tensor equation $G+\Lambda g=\kappa T$ holds at $p$, for a smooth symmetric covariant $2$-tensor $T$ and real constants $\kappa,\Lambda$, then
$$S_h+\tau^2-|K|_h^2=2\Lambda+2\kappa T(n,n),\qquad (\operatorname{div}_hK)(Y)-D_Y\tau=\kappa T(n,Y).$$
With $\rho=T(n,n)$ and $j(Y)=-T(n,Y)$, the second equation is $(\operatorname{div}_hK)(Y)-D_Y\tau=-\kappa j(Y)$.

Assume Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ ([[def-countable-choice]]). Fix $\kappa>0$, $\Lambda\in\mathbb R$ and one covariant matter model: specified smooth tensor fields $\Psi$, specified equations $\mathcal E(g,\Psi)=0$, and a specified stress expression $T=\mathcal T(g,\Psi)$. Covariance means pullback by a local diffeomorphism commutes with these equations and stress expression. Fix complete smooth matter Cauchy data $d$ for this model, a smooth Riemannian metric $h$ and smooth symmetric tensor $K$ on a smooth three-manifold $\Sigma$, with $K(V,W)=g(\nabla_Vn,W)$ for the future unit normal.

The following explicit harmonic-reduction hypothesis is required. On each relatively compact initial coordinate ball, with flat comparison metric $\bar g=-(dx^0)^2+\sum_i(dx^i)^2$, specify finite first-order variables
$$z=(g_{ab},p_{ab}=\partial_0g_{ab},q_{abi}=\partial_ig_{ab},w),$$
fixed smooth extraction and reconstruction rules for $w,\Psi$, and fixed smooth coefficient functions $A^\mu(x,z),B(x,z)$ on an open state set $O$, shared by both solutions, such that:

**(R1)** Every smooth solution of this same model written in harmonic coordinates has extracted variables satisfying
$$A^0(x,z)\partial_0z+\sum_iA^i(x,z)\partial_iz+B(x,z)=0,$$
where all $A^\mu$ are symmetric and $A^0$ is positive definite. Reconstruction recovers all matter fields and $T$ from $z$. Any internal matter gauge has already been fixed with its specified data and equations; otherwise the conclusion must include the appropriate internal gauge equivalence.
**(R2)** The initial value of $w$ is a specified smooth expression $\mathcal I(h,K,d)$ in the full data in this coordinate gauge. Thus $d$ determines every initial first-order variable, not merely initial stress tensor jets.
**(R3)** After shrinking a closed cylinder, both state ranges lie in one compact convex subset of $O$, coefficient first derivatives are bounded and $A^0\ge aI$ for some $a>0$.

These are PDE and extraction hypotheses, not an assumption of geometric uniqueness. Let $(M,g,\Psi,j)$ and $(M',g',\Psi',j')$ be two smooth time-oriented developments of this same model, solving the same Einstein equation $G+\Lambda g=\kappa\mathcal T(g,\Psi)$ and the same matter equations, whose spacelike embeddings induce $(h,K,d)$. Then near each initial point there is a smooth time-orientation-preserving isometry $\Phi$ with $\Phi\circ j=j'$ on the initial patch, $\Phi^*\Psi'=\Psi$ and consequently $\Phi^*T'=T$. Its germ along the initial patch is unique. These germs glue to one such isometry between open neighborhoods of the entire embedded initial surfaces. No uniform collar width or global-in-time assertion is made.

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold and let
$\nabla$ be its metric-selected connection, whose existence and uniqueness are
supplied by [[thm-gr-nondegenerate-levi-civita-and-tensor-derivative]]; its
Christoffel symbols are the smooth chart functions of
[[def-christoffel-symbols-of-an-affine-connection]]. Recall that a **geodesic**
is a curve with $D_t\gamma'=0$ in its parameter
([[def-geodesic-of-an-affine-connection]],
[[def-covariant-derivative-along-a-curve]]).

**(a) Local existence, uniqueness and maximality.** For every $(p,v)\in TM$
there is a unique maximal geodesic $\gamma_{p,v}:I_{p,v}\to M$ with
$\gamma_{p,v}(0)=p$ and $\gamma_{p,v}'(0)=v$; its domain $I_{p,v}$ is an open
interval containing $0$ and is not asserted to be all of $\mathbb R$.

**(b) Smooth dependence.** The set
$\mathcal G:=\{(t,p,v):t\in I_{p,v}\}\subseteq\mathbb R\times TM$ is open, and
the evaluation map $(t,p,v)\mapsto\gamma_{p,v}(t)$ is smooth on $\mathcal G$.

**(c) Scaling.** For every $s\in\mathbb R$ and every $t\in\mathbb R$,
$t\in I_{p,sv}$ if and only if $st\in I_{p,v}$, and then
$\gamma_{p,sv}(t)=\gamma_{p,v}(st)$.

**(d) The exponential map.** Define $\mathcal E_p:=\{v\in T_pM:1\in I_{p,v}\}$
and $\exp_p:\mathcal E_p\to M$, $\exp_p(v):=\gamma_{p,v}(1)$, and let
$\psi_p:T_pM\to\mathbb R^4$ be the coordinate isomorphism of a basis
$e_0,\dots,e_3$ of $T_pM$. Then $\mathcal E_p$ is open and star-shaped about
$0$ (if $v\in\mathcal E_p$ and $0\le s\le1$, then $sv\in\mathcal E_p$),
$\exp_p$ is smooth, $\exp_p(0)=p$, and, under the canonical identification
$T_0(T_pM)\cong T_pM$ and the chart $x=\psi_p$ on $T_0M$,
$$d(\exp_p)_0=\operatorname{id}_{T_pM}.$$
Consequently there is a star-shaped open neighborhood $W_p\subseteq\mathcal E_p$
of $0$ such that $\exp_p|_{W_p}$ is a diffeomorphism onto an open subset of
$M$.

Let $F:M\to N$ be a smooth map and let $p\in M$. If $dF_p:T_pM\to T_{F(p)}N$ is
an isomorphism, then there are open neighbourhoods $U$ of $p$ and $V$ of
$F(p)$ such that $F|_U:U\to V$ is a diffeomorphism.

Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ ([[def-countable-choice]]). Every open cover of a smooth manifold has a countable cover by coordinate balls with compact closures, each closure contained in one member of the original cover.

Assume countable choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. Let $(U_n)_{n\ge 1}$ be a countable cover of a smooth manifold $M$ by coordinate balls with compact closures. Then there is an at-most-countable index set $I$ and families of open sets $(W_k)_{k\in I}$ and coordinate balls $(V_k)_{k\in I}$ such that $M=\bigcup_{k\in I} W_k$, each $\overline{W_k}\subseteq V_k\subseteq \overline{V_k}\subseteq U_{n(k)}$ for some index $n(k)$, and the family $(V_k)$ is locally finite. The index set may be finite or empty.
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. Every open cover of a smooth manifold admits a smooth partition of unity subordinate to it.

Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. If Omega has the specified finite piecewise $C^1$ presentation and $F\in C^1(\overline\Omega;\mathbb R^n)$, then $\int_\Omega\operatorname{div}F=\sum_j\int_{S_j}F\cdot\nu_j\,dS$, with faces counted once off E. All integrals are finite. In a specified finite gluing, the two fluxes on every shared face cancel.

Let $t_0\le T$, let $u,a,b:[t_0,T]\to\mathbb R$ be continuous, with $u,b\ge0$, and suppose

$$u(t)\le a(t)+\int_{t_0}^t b(s)u(s)\,ds.$$

Then

$$u(t)\le a(t)+\int_{t_0}^t a(s)b(s)\exp\!\left(\int_s^t b(r)\,dr\right)ds.$$

If $a$ is nondecreasing, this gives $u(t)\le a(t)\exp(\int_{t_0}^t b)$. The time-reflected form assumes $u(t)\le a(t)+\int_t^{t_0}b(s)u(s)\,ds$ for $t\le t_0$. In particular, when $a=A\ge0$ and $b=B\ge0$ are constant, the two orientations give $u(t)\le A e^{B|t-t_0|}$.

Assume Countable Choice and Dependent Choice ([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-dependent-choice]]). Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold ([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]), with the locally absolutely continuous causal curves of [[def-gr-causal-curves-and-reachability]]. Let $I\subseteq\mathbb R$ be an open interval containing $0$, and let $B_R\subseteq\mathbb R^3$ be the open ball of radius $R>0$ centered at $0$, with Euclidean norm $|\cdot|$. Suppose $(s,\sigma):U\to I\times B_R$ is a diffeomorphism of an open set $U\subseteq M$, satisfying:

**(C1)** $\partial_s$ is future timelike and every $s$-level is spacelike;

**(C2)** there is $K\ge1$ such that $|d\sigma(v)|\le Kds(v)$ for every nonzero future causal vector $v$ based in $U$.

Write $S=s^{-1}(0)$, and compute the domains of dependence intrinsically in $U$:
$$D^+_U(S)=\{p\in U:\text{every past-inextendible causal curve in }U\text{ through }p\text{ meets }S\},\qquad D^-_U(S)=\{p\in U:\text{every future-inextendible causal curve in }U\text{ through }p\text{ meets }S\}.$$
Here inextendibility means absence of an endpoint limit in the specified open submanifold, and Cauchy intersection means exactly one parameter visit ([[def-gr-spacelike-hypersurfaces-and-cauchy-sets]]). Then:

**(a)** $D^+_U(S)\subseteq\{s\ge0\}$ and $D^-_U(S)\subseteq\{s\le0\}$.

**(b)** The corrected open collar
$$Q=\{q\in U:|\sigma(q)|+K|s(q)|<R\}$$
is a neighborhood of the entire slice $S$ in $U$ and is contained in $D^+_U(S)\cup D^-_U(S)$; more precisely $Q\cap\{s>0\}\subseteq D^+_U(S)$ and $Q\cap\{s<0\}\subseteq D^-_U(S)$.

**(c)** The open set $W=\operatorname{int}_U(D^+_U(S)\cup D^-_U(S))$ contains $Q$, and $S$ is a Cauchy hypersurface of $(W,g|_W,N|_W)$. Consequently $W$ is globally hyperbolic by [[thm-gr-cauchy-surface-implies-globally-hyperbolic]].

**(d) Generic spacelike and noncompact scope.** For every smooth embedded spacelike hypersurface $\Sigma\subseteq M$ without boundary there exist an open neighborhood $U_\Sigma$ of $\Sigma$, a smooth positive function $\delta:\Sigma\to(0,\infty)$, and a diffeomorphism
$$F:\Omega\to U_\Sigma,\qquad\Omega=\{(s,x)\in\mathbb R\times\Sigma:|s|<\delta(x)\},\qquad F(0,x)=x,$$
such that $s$ is temporal and $F_*\partial_s$ is future timelike. The intrinsic set $W_\Sigma=\operatorname{int}_{U_\Sigma}(D^+_{U_\Sigma}(\Sigma)\cup D^-_{U_\Sigma}(\Sigma))$ is an open neighborhood in which $\Sigma$ is Cauchy, hence is globally hyperbolic. Neither compactness nor global acausality of $\Sigma$ in $M$ is assumed. No positive uniform lower bound for $\delta$ is asserted.

derivations.claim: (Complete harmonic initial value.) On a small initial coordinate ball set $g_{00}=-1$, $g_{0i}=0$, $g_{ij}=h_{ij}$, $p_{ij}=2K_{ij}$ and $q_{abi}=\partial_i g^0_{ab}$. For the flat comparison metric the Christoffel contraction at the surface is $$H^0=\tfrac12p_{00}+\operatorname{tr}_hK,\qquad H^\ell=-h^{\ell i}p_{0i}+h^{jk}\Gamma(h)^\ell{}_{jk}.$$ Thus prescribe $p_{00}=-2\operatorname{tr}_hK$ and $p_{0i}=h_{i\ell}h^{jk}\Gamma(h)^\ell{}_{jk}$, giving $H=0$ initially. The spatial derivative definitions and the initialization $w=\mathcal I(h,K,d)$ supply every remaining initial value and every auxiliary compatibility constraint. In this coordinate gauge $\partial_0=n$ initially, so $K_{ij}=\tfrac12p_{ij}$ and the reconstructed matter data are exactly $d$. The generally nonzero $p_{0i}$ is essential for the flat comparison metric; the special background $-dt^2+h$ instead gives $p_{0i}=0$.

(Local coupled reduced existence.) Shrink about each initial point so the initial state values lie in a compact ball strictly inside a convex admissible state ball $O_*\Subset O$. Extend the smooth data to a torus by a spatial cutoff interpolating to a fixed value in $O_*$; convexity keeps all interpolated values admissible. On a smaller initial cylinder extend the coefficient functions by a smooth spatial cutoff, keeping the original functions on the smaller patch and interpolating $A^0$ to the identity, $A^i$ to zero and $B$ to zero outside the larger patch. Symmetry persists and the convex positive-matrix cone preserves positivity. Choose compact sets $C\subset\operatorname{int}C'\Subset O_*$ containing the extended data and a finite $H^s$ norm bound $R$ for one integer $s\ge5$. On the compact time, spatial and state ranges the coefficient derivatives are bounded and $A^0\ge aI$ for some $a>0$. These are the actual hypotheses of [L1]; the periodic existence and smooth persistence theorems give a smooth solution on a nonzero interval. Restrict to the original patch, where it solves the original coupled system. No theorem for a prescribed spacetime tensor $T$ has been substituted for this coupled existence argument.

(Removal of extensions.) For two smooth solutions of systems agreeing near a smaller initial cone, subtract their equations and put $v=z_1-z_2$. On a smaller compact cylinder their states lie in a common convex admissible compact neighborhood. The coefficient mean-value formula gives $$A^\mu(x,z_1)\partial_\mu v+C(x)v=0,$$ where $C$ includes the bounded terms obtained from coefficient differences multiplying $\partial_\mu z_2$ and from the source difference. Let $b=\sup_{|\xi|=1}\|\sum_i\xi_iA^i(x,z_1)\|$ there and choose $\lambda>b/a$. On the shrinking ball of radius $r-\lambda t$, [L5] gives $$\frac{d}{dt}\int_{B_{r-\lambda t}}v^{\mathsf T}A^0v\le c\int_{B_{r-\lambda t}}v^{\mathsf T}A^0v-\int_{\partial B_{r-\lambda t}}v^{\mathsf T}(\lambda A^0+\nu_iA^i)v\le c\int_{B_{r-\lambda t}}v^{\mathsf T}A^0v.$$ The boundary matrix is positive since $\lambda a>b$. Equal initial values give zero energy by Gronwall. Reverse time for the other half. This proves independence of the extensions on an actual open initial neighborhood, with the combined spatial-symbol bound rather than an incorrect bound on each separate $A^i$.

(Recovery without circularity.) By hypothesis 2, the auxiliary constraints propagate and the reconstructed reduced solution solves the original matter equations, giving the exact initial stress and data. Hypothesis 3 therefore gives $
abla^aT_{ab}=0$ on this reduced solution before Einstein recovery. Its initial geometric jet gives $H=0$ by step 1.1 and the Gauss-Codazzi constraint equations give $E(n,n)=E(n,e_i)=0$. On a reduced solution one has $E_{ab}=	frac12(
abla_aH_b+
abla_bH_a-g_{ab}
abla_cH^c)$; since tangential derivatives of $H$ vanish initially, this reads $E_{00}=	frac12
abla_0H_0$ and $E_{0i}=	frac12
abla_0H_i$ in the initial orthogonal frame. Thus $
abla_nH=0$ initially. Conservation gives the homogeneous subsidiary equation and [L2] forces $H=0$, hence $E=0$, on a smaller neighborhood. The local solution is now a full physical development.

(Common normal collar representatives.) For each local full development define $E_i(s,p)=\exp_{j_i(p)}(sn_i(p))$. Its differential at $(0,p)$ is $(c,V)\mapsto cn_i+dj_i(V)$, an isomorphism. The inverse function theorem [L3] gives, after local shrinking, an injective normal collar over a smaller initial ball. Pull its metric and matter fields back to its normal domain in $\mathbb R\times\Sigma$. If two initial balls intersect, [L3] gives a future data-fixing isometry germ on the intersection. Its differential is the identity on the slice tangent directions and sends $n_i$ to $n_j$ by uniqueness of the future unit normal. Preservation and uniqueness of affinely parametrized geodesics give $$\Phi(E_i(s,p))=E_j(s,p)$$ for every sufficiently small segment staying in its domain. Consequently the two pulled-back full fields agree on an open neighborhood of the zero section over the intersection. This uses uniqueness of isometry germs and normal parametrization; fixing the slice alone does not make a general map the identity off it. No geometric uniqueness is used to create the reduced solution or to propagate its constraints.

(Locally finite literal patching.) Choose [L4]'s countable locally finite shrinking $\overline{W_i}=K_i\subset V_i\subset\overline{V_i}\subset O_i$, with $O_i$ normal-collar existence patches from step 4.1 and $K_i$ compact. Each $K_i$ meets only finitely many $K_j$, since $(V_j)$ is locally finite and $K_j\subset V_j$. Compactness supplies $t_i>0$ for which the $i$th normal representative exists on $(-t_i,t_i)\times K_i$. On each nonempty compact $K_i\cap K_j$, step 4.1 supplies an open equality neighborhood; a finite subcover gives a symmetric width $t_{ij}=t_{ji}>0$ on which the representatives agree over that compact intersection. Countable Choice selects widths for the countably many indices and pairs. Set $$\delta_i=\tfrac12\min\bigl(\{t_i\}\cup\{t_{ij}:K_i\cap K_j\ne\varnothing\}\bigr)>0.$$ The minimum is finite. The normal representatives agree on every overlap of $(-\delta_i,\delta_i)\times W_i$ and so define single smooth tensor fields on their literal open union $\Omega\subset\mathbb R\times\Sigma$. Ordinary equality supplies the triple-overlap cocycle, with no quotient construction or Hausdorffness issue. For a subordinate locally finite partition $(\rho_i)$ set $\alpha(p)=\tfrac12\sum_i\delta_i\rho_i(p)>0$. At each point the finite weighted average is at most the largest active width, whose $W_i$ contains that point; hence $\{|s|<\alpha(p)\}\subset\Omega$. Restriction gives a smooth positive variable-width collar and the exact full data. No positive uniform lower bound is required.

(Causal neighborhood and uniqueness.) Apply [L5]'s generic embedded-spacelike clause to the surface $\{0\}\times\Sigma$ in this glued development. It furnishes a further temporal variable-width collar $U$ and an open set $W=\operatorname{int}_U(D^+_U(\Sigma)\cup D^-_U(\Sigma))$ containing the entire initial surface, where $\Sigma$ is Cauchy and $W$ is globally hyperbolic. The domains are intrinsic to $U$; no assertion that the one-sided domain itself is open is needed. Finally the fixed model, same reconstruction and complete data meet all hypotheses of [L3]'s uniqueness theorem. Two full developments are therefore isometric near the whole initial surface, matching all matter fields and future orientation. These are the asserted existence, causal and uniqueness conclusions.

Vanishing initial stress does not replace the fixed-model reconstruction assumptions in Statement; gauge and Einstein residuals are zero only after the proved recovery step.
The Statement permits a scalar matter model but retains four metric dimensions and the full first-order initialization, not merely one normal stress projection.
Step 2.1: Its reduced coefficients must have a positive time matrix on admissible neighborhoods; the complete model/reconstruction contract excludes singular states before analytic existence.
Steps 5.1 and 6.1: The local solution is obtained near Sigma with a variable-width collar and then restricted to its intrinsic Cauchy neighborhood; no global completeness or uniform slab is asserted.
Step 5.1: The declared Countable Choice is used to select local construction and comparison widths in the countable locally finite patching, with causal suppliers retaining Dependent Choice.

$$S_h+(\operatorname{tr}_hK)^2-|K|_h^2=2\Lambda+2\kappa T_0(N,N),\qquad \operatorname{div}_hK-d\operatorname{tr}_hK=\kappa T_0(N,\cdot).$$

Then the data have a smooth time-oriented local development $(g,\Psi)$ on an open variable-width neighborhood of $\{0\}\times\Sigma$ in the literal manifold $\mathbb R\times\Sigma$, with induced data $(h,K,d)$, solving
$$G(g)+\Lambda g=\kappa\mathcal T(g,\Psi),\qquad\mathcal E(g,\Psi)=0.$$
After restriction to a smaller collar, $\Sigma$ lies in the interior of its intrinsic domain of dependence. The interior of that domain is a globally hyperbolic neighborhood with $\Sigma$ Cauchy. Any two developments of this same model and these complete data are related near the entire initial surface by a data-fixing time-orientation-preserving isometry matching all matter fields. There is no uniform noncompact time width or global-in-time conclusion. This is a conditional assertion; it promises no converse characterization of its hypotheses. The iff-reverse case has no additional implication to prove.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice for the integral below
([[def-countable-choice]]). Let a perfect-fluid model on a Lorentzian manifold
be given with smooth equation of state $p=p(\epsilon)$ defined on an open
interval $J\subseteq\mathbb R$, with $\epsilon+p(\epsilon)>0$ and
$p'(\epsilon)>0$ for all $\epsilon\in J$
([[def-gr-perfect-fluid-matter-model]]). Fix a base point
$\epsilon_*\in J$ and define the **barotropic enthalpy variable**
$$r:J\to\mathbb R,\qquad r(\epsilon):=\int_{\epsilon_*}^{\epsilon}\frac{\sqrt{p'(z)}}{z+p(z)}\,dz .$$
The integrand is continuous on $J$ ([[thm-continuous-implies-integrable]]), so
$r$ is well defined and $C^1$ with $r'(\epsilon)=\sqrt{p'(\epsilon)}/(\epsilon+p(\epsilon))>0$
([[cor-ftc-integral-function-differentiable-almost-everywhere]]); hence $r$
maps $J$ diffeomorphically onto the open interval $r(J)$, and we write
$\epsilon(r)$ for its inverse and $c_s:=\sqrt{p'}$ for the **sound-speed
function**, so that $r'(\epsilon)=c_s(\epsilon)/(\epsilon+p(\epsilon))$ and
$c_s\in(0,1)$ when $0<p'<1$ is assumed.

The definition and the two displayed equivalences are the form in which the
fluid system is fed into [[lem-gr-barotropic-fluid-symmetric-hyperbolic-system]];
no existence theorem is asserted here.

Assume Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]) for the enthalpy integral. Fix a smooth EOS $p=p(\epsilon)$ on an open interval $J$ satisfying $\epsilon+p>0$ and $0<p'(\epsilon)<1$. Fix the integration reference in the enthalpy variable $r$ of [[def-gr-barotropic-enthalpy-variable]], and put $c_s=\sqrt{p'}$. Let $u$ be the future unit fluid velocity, $D=\nabla_u$, $\vartheta=\nabla_a u^a$, $a=\nabla_u u$ and $\Pi^{ab}=g^{ab}+u^au^b$ ([[def-gr-perfect-fluid-matter-model]]). Then:

**(a)** The full fluid equations are equivalent to
$$Dr+c_s\vartheta=0,\qquad \nabla_u u^b+c_s\Pi^{ba}\partial_ar=0.$$
The fluid stress $T^{ab}=(\epsilon+p)u^au^b+pg^{ab}$ is divergence-free precisely when these fluid equations hold.

**(b)** For variations $\eta=(\delta r,\delta u)$ with $g(u,\delta u)=0$, the smooth symmetric principal bilinear form at a covector $\zeta$ is
$$Q_\zeta(\eta,\eta')=\zeta(u)\left[\delta r\delta r'+g(\delta u,\delta u')\right]+c_s\left[\delta r\zeta(\delta u')+\delta r'\zeta(\delta u)\right].$$
For every timelike covector positively evaluated on future timelike vectors, it is positive definite. In a rest orthonormal basis it has eigenvalues $\zeta(u)$ twice and $\zeta(u)\pm c_s|\zeta_\perp|$, where $\zeta=-\zeta(u)u^\flat+\zeta_\perp$. Smooth velocity coordinates turn this bilinear form into actual smooth symmetric coefficient matrices.

**(c)** Appending the harmonic reduced Einstein metric block gives a smooth coupled first-order symmetric hyperbolic family on a local open admissible state set, with zeroth-order coupling in derivatives of the first-order variables. In an initially orthogonal chart, complete fluid data are $(\epsilon_0,v_0)$ with $h(v_0,v_0)<1$, or the corresponding bundle velocity $U_0=W_0(N+v_0)$, $W_0=(1-h(v_0,v_0))^{-1/2}$ in $\mathbb RN\oplus T\Sigma$. They initialize $r=r(\epsilon_0)$, $u^0=W_0$ and $u^i=W_0v_0^i$. Normalization is enforced by reconstruction, and a reduced solution recovers the full fluid equations and conserved stress before imposing Einstein's unreduced equations. Every full fluid solution extracts to the same system. No vanishing-sound-speed or dust conclusion is asserted.

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold with
metric-selected connection $\nabla$ and let $U\subseteq M$ be a nonempty open
matter domain ([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]],
[[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]],
[[thm-gr-nondegenerate-levi-civita-and-tensor-derivative]],
[[prop-an-open-subset-of-a-smooth-manifold-has-a-canonical-restricted-smooth-structure]]).

**(a) Dust.** Let $(\rho,u,T)$ be a dust model on $U$
([[def-gr-dust-matter-model]]). Then

$$\nabla^aT_{ab}=0\ \text{on }U\qquad\Longleftrightarrow\qquad \nabla_a(\rho u^a)=0\ \text{and}\ u^a\nabla_au^b=0\ \text{on }U .$$

**(b) Perfect fluid.** Let $(\varepsilon,p,n,T)$ be a perfect-fluid model on
$U$ with comoving derivative $D$, expansion $\vartheta$, acceleration $a$ and
projection $h$ ([[def-gr-perfect-fluid-matter-model]]). Then

$$\nabla^aT_{ab}=0\ \text{on }U\qquad\Longleftrightarrow\qquad D\varepsilon+(\varepsilon+p)\vartheta=0\quad\text{and}\quad (\varepsilon+p)a^b+h^{ba}\partial_ap=0\ \text{on }U .$$

Assume Countable Choice and Dependent Choice ([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-dependent-choice]]). Fix $\kappa>0$, $\Lambda\in\mathbb R$ and one covariant matter model: specified smooth fields $\Psi$, equations $\mathcal E(g,\Psi)=0$ and stress expression $\mathcal T(g,\Psi)$. Pullback by local diffeomorphisms commutes with these equations and stress expression. Let $\Sigma$ be a smooth three-manifold without boundary, with smooth Riemannian metric $h$, smooth symmetric tensor $K$ and complete smooth matter Cauchy data $d$. The sign convention is $K(V,W)=g(\nabla_Vn,W)$ for the future unit normal. Initial matter tensors involving normal directions are specified on the abstract bundle $\mathcal V=\mathbb RN\oplus T\Sigma$, with metric $g_0(aN+X,bN+Y)=-ab+h(X,Y)$, rather than on a pre-existing spacetime.

Require the following explicit reduction hypotheses on each sufficiently small relatively compact initial coordinate ball with labels $x^i$, flat comparison metric $\bar g=-(dx^0)^2+\sum_i(dx^i)^2$, and finite variables
$$z=(g_{ab},p_{ab}=\partial_0g_{ab},q_{abi}=\partial_ig_{ab},w).$$

1. There are fixed smooth extraction and reconstruction rules and fixed smooth coefficient functions $A^\mu(x,z),B(x,z)$ on an open state set $O$ giving a system
$$A^0(x,z)\partial_0z+\sum_i A^i(x,z)\partial_iz+B(x,z)=0,$$
with symmetric $A^\mu$ and positive definite $A^0$. Its metric equations are exactly the first-order reduction of the reduced Einstein equations of [[def-gr-harmonic-gauge-and-reduced-equations]], with stress $T=\mathcal T(g,\Psi)$. Every smooth physical solution of this fixed model in harmonic coordinates extracts to this same system. Any internal matter gauge is already fixed with its specified equations and complete data; otherwise state the corresponding internal gauge equivalence in the conclusion.
2. Complete data determine a smooth initial value $w=\mathcal I(h,K,d)$, including all auxiliary variables and their compatibility constraints. The initial metric jet displayed in step 1.1 and this value lie in $O$. The reduction propagates its auxiliary compatibility constraints, so the reconstructed fields solve $\mathcal E(g,\Psi)=0$ on the reduced solution, before imposing $H=0$ or the unreduced Einstein equations. The initial reconstruction induces exactly $d$ and the specified initial stress.
3. Whenever the reconstructed metric and fields satisfy those matter equations, their stress obeys $\nabla^a\mathcal T(g,\Psi)_{ab}=0$, independently of the unreduced Einstein equations. In particular this applies to the reduced solution furnished by clause 2. This is stronger than conservation asserted only after the full coupled equations have been proved.

These are concrete PDE, initialization and reconstruction hypotheses; they do not assume existence or geometric uniqueness. Require the constraints of [[thm-gr-constraint-equations-in-normal-frame]] for the stress determined by $(h,K,d)$:
$$S_h+(\operatorname{tr}_hK)^2-|K|_h^2=2\Lambda+2\kappa T_0(N,N),\qquad \operatorname{div}_hK-d\operatorname{tr}_hK=\kappa T_0(N,\cdot).$$

Then the data have a smooth time-oriented local development $(g,\Psi)$ on an open variable-width neighborhood of $\{0\}\times\Sigma$ in the literal manifold $\mathbb R\times\Sigma$, with induced data $(h,K,d)$, solving
$$G(g)+\Lambda g=\kappa\mathcal T(g,\Psi),\qquad\mathcal E(g,\Psi)=0.$$
After restriction to a smaller collar, $\Sigma$ lies in the interior of its intrinsic domain of dependence. The interior of that domain is a globally hyperbolic neighborhood with $\Sigma$ Cauchy. Any two developments of this same model and these complete data are related near the entire initial surface by a data-fixing time-orientation-preserving isometry matching all matter fields. There is no uniform noncompact time width or global-in-time conclusion.

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold, let
$\Sigma\subseteq M$ be a spacelike embedded hypersurface with induced metric
$h$, future unit normal field $n$ and second fundamental form
$K(V,W)=g(\nabla_Vn,W)$ ([[def-gr-spacelike-hypersurfaces-and-cauchy-sets]],
[[lem-gr-spacelike-hypersurface-normal-and-second-fundamental-form]]). Let
$s$ be a smooth function defined near $\Sigma$ with $s=0$ exactly on $\Sigma$
and $ds(n)=1$ (a normal time coordinate), and let $h_0$ be a smooth metric on a
product neighborhood of $\Sigma$ with $h_0|_{\Sigma}=h$ and
$\partial_sh_0=0$. Put $\bar g:=-ds^2+h_0$ as background metric. Define a smooth
metric germ $g_0$ on $\Sigma$ by the initial jet
$$g_{ij}=h_{ij},\qquad g_{00}=-1,\qquad g_{0i}=0,\qquad \partial_sg_{ij}=2K_{ij},\qquad \partial_sg_{0i}=0,\qquad \partial_sg_{00}=-2\operatorname{tr}_hK .$$
Then:

**(a)** $g_0$ is the germ of a smooth Lorentzian metric for which $\Sigma$ is
spacelike with induced metric $h$, future unit normal $n=\partial_s$ and second
fundamental form $K$;

**(b)** the harmonic-gauge vector of $(g_0,\bar g)$ vanishes on $\Sigma$:
$H^a|_\Sigma=0$.

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold, and let $\Sigma\subseteq M$ be a smooth spacelike embedded hypersurface with future unit normal $n$, induced Riemannian metric $h$ and second fundamental form $K(X,Y)=g(\nabla_Xn,Y)$ ([[def-gr-spacelike-hypersurfaces-and-cauchy-sets]], [[lem-gr-spacelike-hypersurface-normal-and-second-fundamental-form]]). Write $D$ for the Levi-Civita connection of $h$, $R^h$ for its curvature operator in the same operator convention as the ambient curvature, and $S_h$ for its scalar curvature. Explicitly distinguish the lowered tensor from the operator pairing by setting
$$\mathcal R^g(A,B,C,D):=g(R^g(C,D)B,A),\qquad \mathcal R^h(A,B,C,D):=h(R^h(C,D)B,A).$$
Thus $\mathcal R^g_{abcd}=R_{abcd}$ in [[def-gr-curvature-tensor-and-derived-tensors]]; in particular $g(R^g(X,Y)Z,W)=\mathcal R^g(W,Z,X,Y)$. Let $G$ be the Einstein tensor defined there. At every $p\in\Sigma$ and for all $X,Y,Z,W\in T_p\Sigma$:

**(a) Gauss equation.**
$$\mathcal R^g(X,Y,Z,W)=\mathcal R^h(X,Y,Z,W)+K(X,Z)K(Y,W)-K(X,W)K(Y,Z).$$
Equivalently, in operator order,
$$g(R^g(X,Y)Z,W)=h(R^h(X,Y)Z,W)+K(Y,Z)K(X,W)-K(X,Z)K(Y,W).$$

**(b) Codazzi equation.**
$$g(R^g(X,Y)Z,n)=(D_YK)(X,Z)-(D_XK)(Y,Z).$$

**(c) Normal projections.** Define $(\operatorname{div}_hK)(Y)=h^{ij}(D_{e_i}K)(e_j,Y)$, $\tau=\operatorname{tr}_hK=h^{ij}K_{ij}$ and $|K|_h^2=h^{ik}h^{jl}K_{ij}K_{kl}$. Then
$$G(n,n)=\tfrac12(S_h+\tau^2-|K|_h^2),\qquad G(n,Y)=(\operatorname{div}_hK)(Y)-D_Y\tau.$$

**(d) Constraint equations.** If the tensor equation $G+\Lambda g=\kappa T$ holds at $p$, for a smooth symmetric covariant $2$-tensor $T$ and real constants $\kappa,\Lambda$, then
$$S_h+\tau^2-|K|_h^2=2\Lambda+2\kappa T(n,n),\qquad (\operatorname{div}_hK)(Y)-D_Y\tau=\kappa T(n,Y).$$
With $\rho=T(n,n)$ and $j(Y)=-T(n,Y)$, the second equation is $(\operatorname{div}_hK)(Y)-D_Y\tau=-\kappa j(Y)$.

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold with
metric-selected connection $\nabla$ ([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]],
[[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]],
[[thm-gr-nondegenerate-levi-civita-and-tensor-derivative]]) and let
$U\subseteq M$ be a nonempty open matter domain
([[prop-an-open-subset-of-a-smooth-manifold-has-a-canonical-restricted-smooth-structure]]).

**(a) Data.** A **perfect-fluid model** on $U$ is a triple $(\varepsilon,p,n)$
consisting of two smooth functions $\varepsilon,p:U\to\mathbb R$, the **rest
energy density** and the **pressure**, and a smooth future-directed unit
timelike vector field $n$ on $U$ with $g_p(n_p,n_p)=-1$ and
$g_p(n_p,N_p)<0$ at every $p$ ([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]],
[[def-c-r-and-smooth-maps-between-smooth-manifolds]]). No positivity of
$\varepsilon$ or of $p$ is required or implied. A model may carry the
additional data of an **equation of state**: a function
$P:D_P\to\mathbb R$ on a subset $D_P\subseteq\mathbb R$ with
$\varepsilon(U)\subseteq D_P$, together with the relation $p=P(\varepsilon)$;
the relation is a further assumption and is not part of the basic triple.

**(b) Stress-energy tensor and derived fields.** The model's
**stress-energy tensor** is

$$T^{ab}:=(\varepsilon+p)n^an^b+p\,g^{ab},$$

a smooth symmetric contravariant $2$-tensor field ([[def-gr-smooth-covariant-two-tensor-field]],
[[def-gr-inverse-metric-and-musical-isomorphisms]]). The **comoving
derivative**, **expansion** and **acceleration** of $n$ are

$$D f:=n^a\partial_af\quad(f\in C^\infty(U)),\qquad \vartheta:=\nabla_an^a,\qquad a^b:=n^a\nabla_an^b ,$$

and the **rest-space projection** is the smooth tensor field

$$h^{ab}:=g^{ab}+n^an^b .$$

The physical reading of $\varepsilon$ and $p$ as a rest-frame energy density
and pressure, and their units, are fixed by the framework's matter postulate,
not by this definition.

**(c) Fluid equations.** The **perfect-fluid equations** on $U$ are

$$D\varepsilon+(\varepsilon+p)\vartheta=0,\qquad (\varepsilon+p)a^b+h^{ba}\partial_ap=0 .$$

That the stress-energy tensor is divergence-free if and only if these two
equations hold is proved in
[[prop-gr-dust-and-perfect-fluid-conservation-equations]]; the definition
asserts neither divergence-freedom nor the equations.

derivations.claim: (Full fluid contract.) In the initially orthogonal metric gauge, $U_0$ gives $u^0=W_0$ and $u^i=W_0v_0^i$. Thus $(r(\epsilon_0),u_0^i)$ initializes every independent fluid variable in [L1]'s reduction, while its positive-branch reconstruction enforces unit future normalization. That supplier gives smooth symmetric coefficients and positivity for the initial timelike conormal, and proves full fluid recovery and conserved stress on the reduced metric before Einstein recovery. Together with [L2]'s complete metric jet and [L3]'s constraints, every fixed-model hypothesis of [L2] holds.

(Development and comparison.) Apply [L2]. The resulting full solution has exactly the stated geometric and bundle matter data and satisfies the displayed Einstein-fluid equations. Its normal-collar patching and intrinsic Cauchy restriction give the claimed neighborhood and causal properties. Uniqueness uses the same EOS and full density/velocity data and yields a future data-fixing isometry matching both fields. No vanishing-sound-speed branch has been inferred.

Step 2.1 invokes a local variable-width development and explicitly excludes continuation through shocks, vacuum boundaries or vanishing sound speed.
The application in step 2.1 retains Countable Choice and Dependent Choice from its full geometric local-development supplier, including countable patching and causal curves.
