Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold with
signature $(-+++)$ and metric-selected connection $\nabla$. Fix mathematical
parameters $c>0$, $\kappa>0$ and $\Lambda\in\mathbb R$. On an open set
$U_0\subseteq M$, prescribe a smooth function $\rho\ge0$ and a smooth
future-directed unit timelike field $u$, with $g(u,u)=-1$. Set
$\varepsilon:=\rho c^2$ and $T^{ab}:=\varepsilon u^au^b$. On the open positive
subset $\{\rho>0\}$, the tuple $(\varepsilon,u)$, rather than $(\rho,u)$, is
exactly the dust model of [[def-gr-dust-matter-model]]: that supplier's density
is the coefficient of $u\otimes u$. Here $\rho$ denotes its mass-normalized
parameter and $\varepsilon$ its energy-normalized coefficient. On zero-density
regions the smooth unit field is prescribed separately; the geodesic equation
is imposed there as well and is not deduced from conservation of the zero
tensor. This is the smooth geodesic-dust extension, without a free boundary
or a division by density. Make the following
**reduction conventions**, all local to an open set $U\subseteq U_0$:

**(a) Signature flip.** Put $\gamma:=-g$, a smooth metric of signature
$(+---)$ on $U$, with inverse $\gamma^{-1}=-g^{-1}$; all indices in the
reduction are raised and lowered with $\gamma$
([[def-gr-inverse-metric-and-musical-isomorphisms]]). Put
$$U:=u,\qquad r:=\rho c^2 .$$
Then $\gamma(U,U)=1$. Whenever the mathematical model equation
$G(g)+\Lambda g=\kappa T$ holds, it reads
$G(\gamma)-\Lambda\gamma=\kappa\,r\,U^\flat_\gamma\otimes U^\flat_\gamma$ with
the same constant $\kappa$ and the Einstein tensor of $\gamma$
([[def-gr-curvature-tensor-and-derived-tensors]]). Indeed the constant metric
flip leaves the connection and mixed curvature unchanged, so Ricci is unchanged,
the scalar changes sign and $G(\gamma)=G(g)$; both lower factors in $T$
change sign together. The original metric is recovered by $g=-\gamma$.
Physical identification of these mathematical parameters is made by the
consuming physical model, not assumed by this definition.

**(b) Orthonormal frame.** Choose a smooth orthonormal frame
$(e_0,e_1,e_2,e_3)$ on $U$ with $e_0=U$ and
$\gamma(e_i,e_j)=\eta_{ij}:=\operatorname{diag}(1,-1,-1,-1)_{ij}$
([[def-gr-local-frame-and-tetrad-fields]], [[def-gr-observer-congruence-and-adapted-charts]]).
Its connection coefficients are defined by
$$\nabla_ie_j=\Gamma_i{}^k{}_j\,e_k,\qquad \Gamma_{ijk}:=\gamma_{kl}\Gamma_i{}^l{}_j=-\Gamma_{ikj},$$
and the frame components of $U$ are $U^i=\delta^i_0$.
The **spatial projection** onto the $\gamma$-orthogonal complement of $U$ and the tensor
$$h_{ij}:=\gamma_{ij}-U_iU_j,\qquad l_{ij}:=h_{ij}-U_iU_j$$
coincide with $\gamma$-orthogonal projection onto $\operatorname{span}(e_1,e_2,e_3)$
when restricted to spatial pairs.

**(c) Kinematics.** With $\nabla$ the metric connection of $\gamma$
([[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]],
[[thm-gr-nondegenerate-levi-civita-and-tensor-derivative]]) put
$$\chi_{ij}:=h_i{}^k\nabla_kU_j,\qquad \chi:=h^{ij}\chi_{ij},\qquad \chi^{ij}:=h^{ik}h^{jl}\chi_{kl},$$
and let $D$ denote fully projected covariant differentiation: for a spatial
tensor field $T$, $(DT)_{i\ldots}:=(h_i{}^j\cdots)\nabla_j(T_\ldots)$, so
$D_ih_{jk}=0$ and $D_i\epsilon_{jkl}=0$. Let $\epsilon_{ijkl}$ be the
$\gamma$-volume tensor with $\epsilon_{0123}=1$ and set
$\epsilon_{ijk}:=\epsilon_{0ijk}$ (so $\epsilon_{123}=1$).

**(d) Comoving-parallel gauge.** Assume the coordinates
$(x^0=s,x^1,x^2,x^3)$ on $U$ are **comoving** ($e_0=\partial_s$ and $x^\alpha$
constant along the flow lines of $e_0$, $s$ a parameter on them) and
**parallel** ($\Gamma_0{}^i{}_j=0$, i.e. the spatial frame is parallelly
transported along $U$). This gauge is admissible for tilted configurations: the
initial surface $s=0$ is the given spacelike surface and need not be orthogonal
to $U$.

**(e) Unknowns.** The unknowns of the reduction are the coefficients
$$u_{\mathrm{red}}:=\bigl(e_a{}^\mu,\ \Gamma_a{}^i{}_j,\ E_{ij},\ B_{ij},\ r\bigr),\qquad a=1,2,3,$$
where $E$ and $B$ are the electric and magnetic parts of the Weyl curvature
defined in [[def-gr-dust-electric-magnetic-weyl-variables-and-schouten]]; the transport,
evolution and subsidiary equations they satisfy are stated and derived in
[[def-gr-dust-electric-magnetic-weyl-variables-and-schouten]],
[[lem-gr-dust-reduced-evolution-equations]],
[[lem-gr-dust-symmetric-hyperbolic-reduction]] and
[[thm-gr-dust-subsidiary-and-residual-vanishing]].

During the independent reduced evolution, the frame and the coefficients
$\Gamma_a{}^i{}_j$ are tentative smooth unknowns. The coefficients define a
metric-compatible connection by $\widehat\nabla_{e_a}e_j=\Gamma_a{}^i{}_j e_i$
and the tensor product rule; impose the same coefficient antisymmetry and
parallel gauge, but do not assume its torsion vanishes or that it is the
metric-selected connection. In reduction calculations $\nabla$ denotes this
tentative connection. The residual theorem establishes that it equals the
metric-selected connection for constrained solutions. The frame is required
to remain a basis, so it defines the tentative metric by its constant
orthonormal components.

Work in the reduction conventions of
[[def-gr-dust-reduction-variables-and-gauge]]: $\gamma$ is the signature
$(+---)$ metric, $U$ the unit future timelike vector $U=n$, $r=\rho c^2$, the
frame $(e_0,e_1,e_2,e_3)$ is $\gamma$-orthonormal with $e_0=U$,
$\gamma(e_i,e_j)=\eta_{ij}$ on spatial pairs, and indices are moved with
$\gamma$.

**(a) Schouten tensor.** The **reduction Schouten tensor** of $\gamma$ is
$$S_{ij}:=\operatorname{Ric}_{ij}-\tfrac16S_\gamma\,\gamma_{ij},$$
where $\operatorname{Ric}$ and $S_\gamma=\gamma^{ab}\operatorname{Ric}_{ab}$ are
the Ricci tensor and scalar curvature of $\gamma$
([[def-gr-curvature-tensor-and-derived-tensors]]). If the dust field equation
$G(\gamma)-\Lambda\gamma=\kappa\,r\,U^\flat\otimes U^\flat$ holds, then
$$S_{ij}=\kappa r\Bigl(U_iU_j-\tfrac13\gamma_{ij}\Bigr)-\tfrac13\Lambda\,\gamma_{ij}.$$
This normalization is fixed so that the standard Kulkarni--Nomizu decomposition
$$R_{ijkl}=C_{ijkl}+\tfrac12\bigl(S_{ik}\gamma_{jl}-S_{il}\gamma_{jk}+S_{jl}\gamma_{ik}-S_{jk}\gamma_{il}\bigr)$$
holds for every metric of dimension four, with $C$ the Weyl tensor
([[def-gr-curvature-tensor-and-derived-tensors]]); the identity is checked on
constant-curvature metrics in the Remarks.

**(b) Prescribed curvature.** The **prescribed curvature tensor** of a
configuration $(C,E,B,r)$ is the tensor field with frame components
$$R^{\mathrm{pre}}{}_{ijkl}:=C_{ijkl}+\tfrac12\bigl(S_{ik}\gamma_{jl}-S_{il}\gamma_{jk}+S_{jl}\gamma_{ik}-S_{jk}\gamma_{il}\bigr),\qquad S_{ij}\text{ as in (a)} ,$$
where $C=C[E,B]$ is the Weyl tensor reconstructed from the electric and
magnetic variables in (d). A **tentative reduced configuration** is a smooth assignment
$(e_a{}^\mu,\Gamma_a{}^i{}_j,E_{ij},B_{ij},r)$ in the gauge of
[[def-gr-dust-reduction-variables-and-gauge]]. Equality of its actual curvature
with $R^{\mathrm{pre}}$ is the curvature constraint, rather than an assumption
on the independent unknowns. Reduced evolution enforces its time components;
the residual theorem establishes the remaining components from constrained
initial data. This distinction keeps the tentative connection available before
torsion-freeness and the full curvature constraint are proved.

**(c) Electric and magnetic Weyl variables.** For a smooth Weyl-type tensor $C$
of type $(0,4)$ with the curvature symmetries write
$C^*{}_{ijkl}:=\tfrac12C_{ij}{}^{pq}\epsilon_{klpq}$ for its right dual
([[def-gr-dust-reduction-variables-and-gauge]] clause (c) for
$\epsilon_{ijkl}$). The **electric and magnetic parts with respect to $U$** are
the spatial fields
$$E_{ij}:=C_{0i0j},\qquad B_{ij}:=C^*{}_{0i0j},$$
with frame indices; they are symmetric and spatial in all indices and
trace-free with respect to $h$ whenever $C$ has the Weyl symmetries.

**(d) Reconstruction formula.** Define the dependent tensor
$$C_{ijkl}:=2\bigl(l_{j[k}E_{l]i}-l_{i[k}E_{l]j}\bigr)-2\bigl(U_{[k}B_{l]p}\epsilon^p{}_{ij}+U_{[i}B_{j]p}\epsilon^p{}_{kl}\bigr),$$
with brackets of weight $\tfrac12$ and $l_{ij}=h_{ij}-U_iU_j$; this expression
is the **reconstruction** of a Weyl tensor from a pair $(E,B)$ of symmetric
spatial trace-free fields. The verification that the reconstructed tensor has
the curvature antisymmetries, pair symmetry, cyclic identity and zero traces —
and that its electric and magnetic parts recover $(E,B)$ — is the content of
[[lem-gr-dust-weyl-reconstruction-from-electric-magnetic]].

The definition fixes the objects and conventions only; the evolution and
subsidiary equations, the initial-data determination and the local existence
theorem are proved in the items named above and in
[[lem-gr-dust-reduced-evolution-equations]] and
[[thm-gr-dust-local-evolution]].

Work in the reduction conventions of
[[def-gr-dust-reduction-variables-and-gauge]] with $q:=U(r)+r\chi=0$ (the
dust continuity equation in the comoving gauge) and let $E,B$ be the
electric-magnetic variables of
[[def-gr-dust-electric-magnetic-weyl-variables-and-schouten]]. Then:

**(a) [Weyl evolution]** the reduced Weyl equations are
$$0=P_{ij}=\mathcal L_UE_{ij}+D_kB_{l(i}\epsilon_{j)}{}^{kl}-3\chi_{(i}{}^lE_{j)l}-2\chi^l{}_{(i}E_{j)l}+h_{ij}\chi^{kl}E_{kl}+2\chi E_{ij}+\tfrac12\kappa r\bigl(\chi_{(ij)}-\tfrac13\chi h_{ij}\bigr),$$
$$0=Q_{ij}=\mathcal L_UB_{ij}-D_kE_{l(i}\epsilon_{j)}{}^{kl}-\chi^l{}_{(i}B_{j)l}-2\chi_{(i}{}^lB_{j)l}+\chi B_{ij}+\chi^{kl}B^{pq}\epsilon_{pk(i}\epsilon_{qlj)},$$
where $\mathcal L_U$ is the Lie derivative along $U$ and the bracket on the
indices $i,j$ has weight $\tfrac12$; they are obtained by projecting the
Bianchi identity of the prescribed curvature onto the symmetric tracefree
spatial parts, the density-derivative terms cancelling by $q=0$;

**(b) [trace preservation]** extend the displayed symmetric equations of (a) algebraically to all symmetric spatial $E,B$. Contracting this extension with $h^{ij}$ gives $U(t_E)+2\chi t_E=0$ and $U(t_B)=0$, where $t_T=h^{ij}T_{ij}$. Thus
$h^{ij}E_{ij}$ and $h^{ij}B_{ij}$ satisfy homogeneous transport equations along
$U$; consequently zero initial traces remain zero, and the evolution may be
restricted to the five-dimensional tracefree space;

**(c) [transport equations]** with the parallel-comoving gauge one has
$$\partial_se_a{}^\mu=-\Gamma_a{}^j{}_0e_j{}^\mu,\qquad \partial_s\Gamma_a{}^i{}_j=R^{\mathrm{pre}\,i}{}_{j0a}-\Gamma_k{}^i{}_j\Gamma_a{}^k{}_0,\qquad \partial_sr=-r\chi,$$
the first two expressing zero time torsion and zero time-curvature residual, the
third the continuity equation; for tentative data the frame bracket is used in
the curvature definition so that these hold identically;

**(d) [symmetric hyperbolicity]** the system of (a) and (c), together with the
definition of the extrinsic curvature variables, is a first-order quasilinear
system for $(e_a{}^\mu,\Gamma_a{}^i{}_j,E_{ij},B_{ij},r)$ which is symmetric
hyperbolic on a spacelike initial surface: with the positive spatial Frobenius
product, the principal symmetric-tensor curl
$$(C(\xi)B)_{ij}=\epsilon_{kl(i}\xi^kB_{j)}{}^l$$
is skew-adjoint with operator norm at most $|\xi|$ ([[lem-gr-dust-symmetric-hyperbolic-reduction]]), so the coupled block
$\left(\begin{smallmatrix}0&C(\xi)\\-C(\xi)&0\end{smallmatrix}\right)$ is
symmetric with the same bound, every other block is transport along $U$, and a
future-positive timelike conormal $\zeta$ (satisfying
$\zeta(U)>|\zeta_\perp|$) makes the total time matrix positive definite; in
particular the local well-posedness theorem for symmetric hyperbolic systems
applies to the reduced dust system.

Let $V$ be the real vector space of symmetric $3\times3$ matrices with the
positive Frobenius product $\langle B,B'\rangle=B^{ij}B'_{ij}$, and for
$\xi\in\mathbb R^3$ define
$$C(\xi):V\to V,\qquad (C(\xi)B)_{ij}=\epsilon_{kl(i}\xi^kB_{j)}{}^l ,$$
with indices raised and lowered by the Euclidean metric and $\epsilon$ the
Levi-Civita symbol on the spatial frame of
[[def-gr-dust-reduction-variables-and-gauge]]. Then:

**(a)** $C(\xi)$ is skew-adjoint: $\langle C(\xi)B,B'\rangle=-\langle B,C(\xi)B'\rangle$;

**(b)** $\|C(\xi)\|\le|\xi|$ for the operator norm induced by the Frobenius
product;

**(c)** the block operator $\left(\begin{smallmatrix}0&C(\xi)\\-C(\xi)&0\end{smallmatrix}\right)$
on $V\oplus V$ is symmetric (self-adjoint) with operator norm at most $|\xi|$;

**(d)** if $\zeta$ is a covector with $\zeta(U)=z$ and spatial part
$\zeta_\perp$, the symbol matrix
$\left(\begin{smallmatrix}zI&C(\zeta_\perp)\\-C(\zeta_\perp)&zI\end{smallmatrix}\right)$
is positive definite whenever $z>|\zeta_\perp|$, in particular for every
future-positive timelike conormal $\zeta$; hence the reduced dust system is
symmetric hyperbolic with positive time matrix on a spacelike initial surface.

Assume Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]) and Dependent Choice ([[def-dependent-choice]]), carrying the analytic uniqueness and causal-curve supplier hypotheses.

Let $\Sigma$ be a smooth spacelike initial surface with smooth induced Riemannian metric $h$, symmetric second fundamental form $K(X,Y)=g(\nabla_XN,Y)$, rest-mass density $\rho_{\rm mass}\ge0$, fixed $c>0$, and a prescribed smooth future $\gamma$-unit velocity $U_0$, where $\gamma=-g$ has signature $(+---)$. Put $\varepsilon=\rho_{\rm mass}c^2$. Assume the Hamiltonian and momentum constraints of [[thm-gr-constraint-equations-in-normal-frame]] for the initial stress tensor $T_0=\varepsilon U_0^{\flat_g}\otimes U_0^{\flat_g}$, coupling $\kappa>0$ and cosmological constant $\Lambda$. The two lowered factors give the same covariant tensor with $\gamma=-g$. Choose an orientation and oriented tetrads locally for the magnetic contractions. Then locally:

(a) Gauss/Codazzi and the spatial target Ricci equations determine a unique full algebraic curvature tensor. Its full proper Lorentz basis transformation to an oriented tetrad with $e_0=U_0$, followed by the observer electric and magnetic contractions, determines $E_0,B_0$. Boosts may mix these parts.

(b) The tangential metric connection from $(h,K)$, differentiated boost data, and $\omega(U_0)=0$ uniquely determine the entire initial tetrad connection.

(c) At the first jets supplied by the reduced system, every initial torsion, curvature, matter-conservation and Bianchi residual vanishes. In particular the required direction-slot projections are $T^i{}_{0a}=0$ and $\Delta^i{}_{j0a}=0$.

(d) For a future-positive timelike initial conormal $\zeta$, $z=\zeta(U_0)>|w|$ with $w_a=\zeta(e_a)$, the remaining Bianchi components obey $zP+\tfrac12w\times Q=0$, $zQ-\tfrac12w\times P=0$, so vanish. The initial time matrices are positive for every tilt $|v|<1$. Vacuum points remain admitted with prescribed auxiliary velocity.

Assume Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]) and Dependent Choice ([[def-dependent-choice]]), carrying the analytic uniqueness and causal-curve supplier hypotheses.

Let a smooth reduced dust solution have a nondegenerate tentative orthonormal frame for $\gamma$ of signature $(+---)$, a metric-compatible tentative connection, reconstructed algebraic Weyl tensor $C$, prescribed curvature $\overline R$, and dust Schouten tensor $S$ as in [[def-gr-dust-reduction-variables-and-gauge]] and [[def-gr-dust-electric-magnetic-weyl-variables-and-schouten]]. Allow $r\geq0$, with a smooth unit timelike $U$ prescribed also where $r=0$. Assume the parallel-comoving gauge and precisely the reduced equations
$$e_0=U,\quad\Gamma_0{}^i{}_j=0,\quad T^i{}_{0a}=0,\quad\Delta^i{}_{j0a}=0,\quad P_{ab}=Q_{ab}=0,\quad q=U(r)+r\chi=0.$$
Here $a,b=1,2,3$, the first torsion index is the output index, and $P_{ab},Q_{ab}$ are the symmetric tracefree evolution projections of [[lem-gr-dust-reduced-evolution-equations]]. No spatial torsion or spatial curvature residual is assumed zero. Define $F_{jkl}=\nabla^i(C_{ijkl}-\gamma_{i[k}S_{l]j})$, $P_a=F_{0a0}$, and $Q_a=-\epsilon_a{}^{bc}F_{0bc}/2$. Then the spatial components of $(T,\Delta)$ and the vectors $(P,Q)$ satisfy the explicit closed linear homogeneous system constructed in the proof. Its principal part is transport along $U$ for $T,\Delta$ and the curl pair
$$e_0(P_a)+\tfrac12\epsilon_a{}^{bc}e_b(Q_c),\qquad e_0(Q_a)-\tfrac12\epsilon_a{}^{bc}e_b(P_c).$$
It is symmetric hyperbolic on every spacelike initial hypersurface, including one tilted relative to $U$. If all residuals vanish initially, they vanish on its metric domain of determination. Consequently the tentative connection is Levi--Civita, its actual curvature equals $\overline R$, and the resulting metric satisfies the full Einstein-dust equation. The conclusion uses neither division by $r$ nor hypersurface orthogonality of $U$.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$
([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $s\ge5$, let $A^\mu,B$ be a periodic symmetric
hyperbolic coefficient family on the open set $O\subseteq\mathbb R^m$, let
$K\subseteq\operatorname{int}K'\subseteq O$ be compact, let $R\ge0$, and let
$T>0$ and $C$ be as in [[thm-gr-periodic-symmetric-hyperbolic-existence]] for
the class $\mathcal S(K,R)$; for every datum $u_0\in\mathcal S(K,R)$ let $u$ be
the solution produced there on $(-T,T)$ with values in $K'$. Then:

**(a) [local existence]** For every $u_0\in\mathcal S(K,R)$ and every
$x_0\in\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}$ the solution $u$ is $C^1$ on a neighborhood of
$(0,x_0)$ in $(-T,T)\times\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}$ and solves $(\star)$ pointwise
there.

**(b) [finite speed / independence of the extension]** Let $\lambda_0>0$ be
determined by the coefficient bounds on a compact set containing the values of
the solutions in the following sense: for a truncated cone
$$D:=\{(t,x):0\le t\le t_0,\ d(x,x_0)\le\lambda(t_0-t)\}$$
with $t_0<T$, $\lambda\ge\lambda_0$, lying in a single chart of $\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}$
in which the coordinate representation of $A^\mu$ satisfies
$\lambda\,A^0+\xi_iA^i\ge0$ for all unit $\xi$ (which holds for $\lambda$ large
enough by clause (a) of [[lem-gr-finite-speed-independence-of-extension]]),
let $u,v$ be solutions of two periodic symmetric hyperbolic systems whose
coefficient functions agree on a neighborhood of $D$ in the independent variables and on one common open state set containing both solution ranges, with
$u(0,\cdot)=v(0,\cdot)$ on the ball $\{d(x,x_0)\le\lambda t_0\}$. Then
$u=v$ on $D$.

**(c) [local uniqueness and stability]** If two classical solutions of the same
system on a common interval have values in $K$, $H^s$ norms at most $R$ and the
same initial value, they coincide; and the continuous-dependence estimate of
[[thm-gr-periodic-symmetric-hyperbolic-uniqueness-stability]] clause (b) holds
for the solutions of clause (a).

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$
([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $s\ge5$, let $A^\mu,B$ be a periodic symmetric
hyperbolic coefficient family on the open set $O\subseteq\mathbb R^m$
([[def-gr-periodic-symmetric-hyperbolic-system]]) and let $K\subseteq O$ be
compact, and let $K'\subseteq O$ be compact with $K$ contained in the
interior of $K'$. Then for every $R\ge0$ there are a time $T>0$ and a constant
$C$ (depending on $A^\mu,B,K,K',s$ and on $R$) such that:

for every $u_0\in H^s(\mathbb T^3_{2\pi};\mathbb R^m)$ taking values in $K$ with
$\|u_0\|_{H^s}\le R$ there is a Sobolev solution
$u:(-T,T)\to H^s(\mathbb T^3_{2\pi};\mathbb R^m)$ of $(\star)$ with
$u(0)=u_0$ which is classical and satisfies
$$u\in L^\infty((-T,T);H^s)\cap C^0((-T,T);H^{s-1}),\quad \partial_tu\in L^\infty((-T,T);H^{s-1}),$$
$$\sup_{|t|<T}\|u(t)\|_{H^s}\le C(1+R),\qquad \sup_{|t|<T}\|\partial_tu(t)\|_{H^{s-1}}\le C(1+R),$$
and whose values lie in $K'$.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$
([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $s\ge5$, let $A^\mu,B$ be a periodic symmetric
hyperbolic coefficient family on the open set $O\subseteq\mathbb R^m$, let
$K\subseteq\operatorname{int}K'\subseteq O$ be compact, let $R\ge0$, and let
$T>0$ and $C$ be as in [[thm-gr-periodic-symmetric-hyperbolic-existence]] for
the data class $\mathcal S(K,R)$. Let $u_0\in C^\infty(\mathbb T^3_{2\pi};\mathbb R^m)$
take values in $K$ and satisfy $\|u_0\|_{H^s}\le R$. Then the solution $u\in L^\infty((-T,T);H^s)\cap C^0H^{s-1}$
of that theorem with $u(0)=u_0$ satisfies $u\in L^\infty((-T,T);H^m)$ and
$\partial_tu\in L^\infty((-T,T);H^{m-1})$ for every $m\ge s$, with bounds
depending only on $m$, $T$, $R$, the coefficient family, $K'$ and the $H^j$ bounds
of $u_0$ for $j\le m$; consequently $u\in C^\infty((-T,T)\times\mathbb T^3_{2\pi})$
and solves $(\star)$ classically.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$
([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $s\ge5$, let $A^\mu,B$ be a periodic symmetric
hyperbolic coefficient family on the open set $O\subseteq\mathbb R^m$, let
$K\subseteq O$ be compact and $R\ge0$.

**(a) Uniqueness.** Let $J\ni0$ be an open interval and let
$u,v:J\to H^s(\mathbb T^3_{2\pi};\mathbb R^m)$ be classical solutions of
$(\star)$ in the sense of clause (d) of
[[def-gr-periodic-symmetric-hyperbolic-system]], both taking values in $K$ and
satisfying $\sup_{t\in J}\|u(t)\|_{H^s}\le R$, $\sup_{t\in J}\|v(t)\|_{H^s}\le R$.
If $u(0)=v(0)$, then $u=v$ on $J$.

**(b) Continuous dependence.** Let $K'\subseteq O$ be compact with
$K\subseteq\operatorname{int}K'$ and let $T>0$ be a time for which the existence
theorem [[thm-gr-periodic-symmetric-hyperbolic-existence]] produces solutions
from every datum with values in $K$ and norm at most $R$, with values in $K'$
and the bounds $C(1+R)$ of that theorem. Then for all such data $u_0,v_0$ with
solutions $u,v$
$$\|u(t)-v(t)\|_{H^{s-1}}\le C'\,e^{C'|t|}\,\|u_0-v_0\|_{H^{s-1}}\qquad(|t|<T),$$
with $C'=C'(A^\mu,B,K',R,s)$, the fixed compact coefficient time slab containing $[-T,T]$ being included in the coefficient data.

Let $T>0$, let $A^\mu:(-T,T)\times\mathbb R^3\to\operatorname{Sym}_m(\mathbb R)$
($\mu=0,1,2,3$) be smooth with $A^0(t,x)\ge aI$ for some constant $a>0$ and all
$(t,x)$, and let $\|A^i(t,x)\|\le b$ for the operator norm and all $i,t,x$. Let
$C:(-T,T)\times\mathbb R^3\to M_m(\mathbb R)$ be smooth and bounded by $K$.

**(a)** Put $\lambda:=\sqrt3\,b/a+1$; then $\lambda A^0(t,x)+\xi_iA^i(t,x)\ge0$ as a
quadratic form for every $(t,x)$ and every $\xi\in\mathbb R^3$ with
$|\xi|\le1$.

**(b)** Let $w\in C^1((-T,T)\times\mathbb R^3;\mathbb R^m)$ solve
$$A^0\partial_tw+A^i\partial_iw+Cw=0 ,$$
and let $x_0\in\mathbb R^3$, $0<t_0<T$, and suppose $w(0,x)=0$ for every
$|x-x_0|\le\lambda t_0$. Then $w(t,x)=0$ for every
$(t,x)\in\{(t,x):0\le t\le t_0,\ |x-x_0|\le\lambda(t_0-t)\}$.

**(c)** [independence of the extension] If $w_1,w_2$ are two solutions of two
such systems whose complete coefficient families, including $C$, agree on an open set containing the
truncated cone $D=\{(t,x):0\le t\le t_0,|x-x_0|\le\lambda(t_0-t)\}$, and if
$w_1(0,x)=w_2(0,x)$ for $|x-x_0|\le\lambda t_0$, then $w_1=w_2$ on $D$.

Let $X$ be a smooth vector field on $M$. For each $p\in M$, let
$\gamma_p:I_p\to M$ be the maximal integral curve through $p$, and set

$$ \mathcal D:=\{(t,p)\in\mathbb R\times M:t\in I_p\}, \qquad \Phi(t,p):=\gamma_p(t). $$

Then $\mathcal D$ is open in $\mathbb R\times M$, each fibre $\mathcal D_p$ is
an interval containing $0$, the map $\Phi:\mathcal D\to M$ is smooth, and
$\Phi$ is the unique maximal local flow generated by $X$.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $X$ be a smooth vector field on $M$ with maximal flow $\Phi$, and let
$S\hookrightarrow M$ be an embedded codimension-one submanifold. If $X_p\notin T_pS$
for every $p\in S$, then there is an open neighbourhood
$\mathcal O\subseteq \mathbb R\times S$ of $\{0\}\times S$ such that the map

$$ F:\mathcal O\to M,\qquad F(t,p)=\Phi_t(p), $$

is an embedding. Its image is a flowout of $S$ along $X$.

Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ ([[def-countable-choice]]). Every open cover of a smooth manifold has a countable cover by coordinate balls with compact closures, each closure contained in one member of the original cover.

Assume countable choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. Let $(U_n)_{n\ge 1}$ be a countable cover of a smooth manifold $M$ by coordinate balls with compact closures. Then there is an at-most-countable index set $I$ and families of open sets $(W_k)_{k\in I}$ and coordinate balls $(V_k)_{k\in I}$ such that $M=\bigcup_{k\in I} W_k$, each $\overline{W_k}\subseteq V_k\subseteq \overline{V_k}\subseteq U_{n(k)}$ for some index $n(k)$, and the family $(V_k)$ is locally finite. The index set may be finite or empty.
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. Every open cover of a smooth manifold admits a smooth partition of unity subordinate to it.

Assume Countable Choice and Dependent Choice ([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-dependent-choice]]). Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold ([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]), with the locally absolutely continuous causal curves of [[def-gr-causal-curves-and-reachability]]. Let $I\subseteq\mathbb R$ be an open interval containing $0$, and let $B_R\subseteq\mathbb R^3$ be the open ball of radius $R>0$ centered at $0$, with Euclidean norm $|\cdot|$. Suppose $(s,\sigma):U\to I\times B_R$ is a diffeomorphism of an open set $U\subseteq M$, satisfying:

**(C1)** $\partial_s$ is future timelike and every $s$-level is spacelike;

**(C2)** there is $K\ge1$ such that $|d\sigma(v)|\le Kds(v)$ for every nonzero future causal vector $v$ based in $U$.

Write $S=s^{-1}(0)$, and compute the domains of dependence intrinsically in $U$:
$$D^+_U(S)=\{p\in U:\text{every past-inextendible causal curve in }U\text{ through }p\text{ meets }S\},\qquad D^-_U(S)=\{p\in U:\text{every future-inextendible causal curve in }U\text{ through }p\text{ meets }S\}.$$
Here inextendibility means absence of an endpoint limit in the specified open submanifold, and Cauchy intersection means exactly one parameter visit ([[def-gr-spacelike-hypersurfaces-and-cauchy-sets]]). Then:

**(a)** $D^+_U(S)\subseteq\{s\ge0\}$ and $D^-_U(S)\subseteq\{s\le0\}$.

**(b)** The corrected open collar
$$Q=\{q\in U:|\sigma(q)|+K|s(q)|<R\}$$
is a neighborhood of the entire slice $S$ in $U$ and is contained in $D^+_U(S)\cup D^-_U(S)$; more precisely $Q\cap\{s>0\}\subseteq D^+_U(S)$ and $Q\cap\{s<0\}\subseteq D^-_U(S)$.

**(c)** The open set $W=\operatorname{int}_U(D^+_U(S)\cup D^-_U(S))$ contains $Q$, and $S$ is a Cauchy hypersurface of $(W,g|_W,N|_W)$. Consequently $W$ is globally hyperbolic by [[thm-gr-cauchy-surface-implies-globally-hyperbolic]].

**(d) Generic spacelike and noncompact scope.** For every smooth embedded spacelike hypersurface $\Sigma\subseteq M$ without boundary there exist an open neighborhood $U_\Sigma$ of $\Sigma$, a smooth positive function $\delta:\Sigma\to(0,\infty)$, and a diffeomorphism
$$F:\Omega\to U_\Sigma,\qquad\Omega=\{(s,x)\in\mathbb R\times\Sigma:|s|<\delta(x)\},\qquad F(0,x)=x,$$
such that $s$ is temporal and $F_*\partial_s$ is future timelike. The intrinsic set $W_\Sigma=\operatorname{int}_{U_\Sigma}(D^+_{U_\Sigma}(\Sigma)\cup D^-_{U_\Sigma}(\Sigma))$ is an open neighborhood in which $\Sigma$ is Cauchy, hence is globally hyperbolic. Neither compactness nor global acausality of $\Sigma$ in $M$ is assumed. No positive uniform lower bound for $\delta$ is asserted.

Assume the Axioms of Countable Choice and Dependent Choice
([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-dependent-choice]]). Let $(M,g,N)$ be a
time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]) and suppose there exists a Cauchy set
$S\subseteq M$ ([[def-gr-spacelike-hypersurfaces-and-cauchy-sets]] clause
(c)): every inextendible causal curve meets $S$ in exactly one parameter
value. Then:

**(a)** there is no nonconstant future causal curve with equal endpoints
(so $(M,g,N)$ is causal and chronological in the sense of
[[def-gr-causal-conditions-and-global-hyperbolicity]] clause (a));

**(b)** $(M,g,N)$ is strongly causal (clause (b) of that definition);

**(c)** for all $p,q\in M$ the causal diamond
$J^+(p)\cap J^-(q)$ is compact; consequently $(M,g,N)$ is globally
hyperbolic in the sense of clause (c) of that definition.

derivations.claim: (Local initial variables.) On a small coordinate patch choose a local oriented orthonormal frame, boost it to $U_0$ and use the explicit initialization in [L2]. It gives the tentative frame, connection, $E,B$ and $r_0=\rho_0c^2=\varepsilon_0$, with all constrained errors initially zero. At a tilted surface the conormal time matrix is positive by [L1]; on a relatively compact smaller patch continuity gives a uniform positive lower bound, and the initial frame stays in the open set of invertible frames. The magnetic orientation is local only; no global frame or orientability is imposed.

(Exact analytic prerequisite transfer.) Choose an integer $s\ge5$. Shrink the patch so its initial values lie in a small compact admissible coefficient neighborhood; a smooth cutoff to constant values then extends the data to a periodic torus without leaving the open set where the frame is invertible and the time matrix positive. Extend the symmetric coefficient matrices by smooth interpolation to constant symmetric matrices, with the positive time matrices interpolated inside their convex positive cone. These smooth periodic data have finite $H^s$ norm on the compact torus. Thus [L3], with the assumed Countable Choice for its countable Galerkin extraction, gives a smooth local reduced solution by smooth persistence. The finite-speed comparison makes its restriction independent of the extension on a smaller initial cone. No optimal finite-regularity claim is inferred: this supplies exactly the smooth data branch.

(Full system and density.) Initial errors vanish by [L2], and the corrected subsidiary theorem propagates them on the smaller local domain of determination. Consequently the tentative metric connection is Levi-Civita and its actual curvature equals the prescribed curvature; the reconstructed metric solves $G(g)+\Lambda g=\kappa r u^\flat\otimes u^\flat$. Recover $\rho=r/c^2$; since $c>0$ is constant, its continuity equation is exactly the displayed one. The parallel gauge gives $\nabla_uu=0$ independently of $r$. They are transverse to the initial slice, and $s$ is unit proper length with $u=\partial_s$. Use the same initial bundle tetrad and extend it by parallel transport in both metrics. Initial spatial frames with the same observer differ on an oriented overlap by a smooth $SO(3)$ rotation $R(p)$; extend it with $\partial_sR=0$. Its connection transforms as $\widetilde\omega=R^{-1}\omega R+R^{-1}dR$, whose time component remains zero, and its curvature transforms tensorially. Thus each locally constructed full solution can be put into the other's parallel-comoving gauge, with identical initial variables. Step 4.1 gives equality of the reconstructed geometric tensors on an actual open overlap. On an orientation-reversing overlap compare in one common local orientation; the magnetic representative changes sign together with its volume tensor, while the full curvature, metric and density remain ordinary tensors. Hence no global orientation is required, and the coordinate/frame transition cocycles give agreement on triple overlaps.

(Noncompact patching.) Apply [L5] to all admissible local existence patches, obtaining $W_i,V_i,O_i$ as stated and $K_i=\overline{W_i}$ compact. Each $K_i$ meets only finitely many $K_j$, because $K_j\subset V_j$ and $(V_j)$ is locally finite. Compactness gives a positive solution width $t_i$ over $K_i$, and step 5.1 gives a positive equality width $t_{ij}$ over every compact $K_i\cap K_j$. Countable Choice selects these widths for the countable set of pairs. Set $\delta_i=\tfrac12\min(\{t_i\}\cup\{t_{ij}:K_i\cap K_j\ne\varnothing\})>0$, a finite minimum. The solutions then agree on every overlap of the tubes $(-\delta_i,\delta_i)\times W_i$, and glue on their literal open union in $\mathbb R\times\Sigma$. For a subordinate partition $(\psi_i)$ put $\alpha(p)=\tfrac12\sum_i\delta_i\psi_i(p)>0$. At each point the finite weighted average is at most the largest active $\delta_i$, whose $W_i$ contains that point; hence $\{|s|<\alpha(p)\}$ is inside the union. This supplies a smooth positive variable-width collar, with no positive lower bound required on noncompact $\Sigma$.

(Causal neighborhood.) The conormal $ds$ is timelike initially and remains so after further positive pointwise shrinking of the collar; the same locally finite construction realizes this shrink smoothly. Hence $s$ is strictly increasing on future causal curves and the initial level is acausal. In a compact coordinate cylinder around each initial point, choose a bound $K$ on causal spatial displacement per unit $s$ by [L6]. Points with $|x-x_0|+K|s|<R$ for a ball of radius $R$ cannot escape that cylinder in the direction of the initial slice before meeting it: otherwise their causal graph would converge at a positive time to an interior point and could be extended, or would hit its spatial boundary with displacement at least $R-|x-x_0|>K|s|$, contradicting the speed bound. This supplies an open domain-of-dependence neighborhood around every point of $\Sigma$, as in the corrected local Cauchy lemma. Restricting to the interior of the domain of dependence gives its Cauchy neighborhood; [L6] supplies the Cauchy and global-hyperbolicity conclusion. All this is local in the variable-width solution and needs no uniform slab.

(Conclusion.) Steps 3.1 and 6.1 give the full smooth solution with the specified initial data and nonnegative density; step 7.1 gives the causal neighborhood and step 4.1 gives the data-fixing uniqueness for any two developments, including separately prescribed geodesic velocities on vacuum regions. These are exactly the asserted local conclusions.

Fix one scalar model with smooth potential $V$ and fixed stress normalization $K_\phi$ as in [[def-gr-scalar-field-matter-model]]. On a smooth time-oriented Lorentzian four-manifold its equations and stress are
$$\Box_g\varphi-V'(\varphi)=0,\qquad T_{ab}=K_\phi\left[\partial_a\varphi\partial_b\varphi-g_{ab}\left(\tfrac12g^{cd}\partial_c\varphi\partial_d\varphi+V(\varphi)\right)\right].$$
Fix a chart and a smooth background $\bar g$ for the reduced Einstein equation of [[def-gr-harmonic-gauge-and-reduced-equations]]. On the open state set where $g^{00}<0$ and $(g^{ij})$ is positive definite, the reduced Einstein equation coupled to this scalar equation has a smooth first-order symmetric hyperbolic reduction with variables
$$z=(g_{ab},p_{ab}=\partial_0g_{ab},q_{abi}=\partial_ig_{ab},\varphi,P=\partial_0\varphi,Q_i=\partial_i\varphi).$$
The time matrix is block diagonal with metric block $\operatorname{diag}(I,-g^{00}I,g^{ij}I)$ and scalar block $\operatorname{diag}(1,-g^{00},g^{ij})$. Matter and metric cross-coupling is zeroth order in derivatives of $z$. The partial-derivative metric variables and the background-covariant ones are related by an invertible smooth zeroth-order change of variables; either gives the reduction.

For complete initial scalar data $(\varphi_0,\pi_0)$ in an initially orthogonal chart with $\partial_0=n$, prescribe $(\varphi,P,Q_i)=(\varphi_0,\pi_0,\partial_i\varphi_0)$. The auxiliary constraints propagate, the reconstructed scalar solves its full equation on the reduced metric, and its stress is conserved there before imposing the unreduced Einstein equation. Conversely every smooth physical scalar solution extracts to the same system. No potential positivity or mass sign is required; local arguments do not require a global orientation.

Assume Countable Choice and Dependent Choice ([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-dependent-choice]]). Fix $\kappa>0$, $\Lambda\in\mathbb R$ and one covariant matter model: specified smooth fields $\Psi$, equations $\mathcal E(g,\Psi)=0$ and stress expression $\mathcal T(g,\Psi)$. Pullback by local diffeomorphisms commutes with these equations and stress expression. Let $\Sigma$ be a smooth three-manifold without boundary, with smooth Riemannian metric $h$, smooth symmetric tensor $K$ and complete smooth matter Cauchy data $d$. The sign convention is $K(V,W)=g(\nabla_Vn,W)$ for the future unit normal. Initial matter tensors involving normal directions are specified on the abstract bundle $\mathcal V=\mathbb RN\oplus T\Sigma$, with metric $g_0(aN+X,bN+Y)=-ab+h(X,Y)$, rather than on a pre-existing spacetime.

Require the following explicit reduction hypotheses on each sufficiently small relatively compact initial coordinate ball with labels $x^i$, flat comparison metric $\bar g=-(dx^0)^2+\sum_i(dx^i)^2$, and finite variables
$$z=(g_{ab},p_{ab}=\partial_0g_{ab},q_{abi}=\partial_ig_{ab},w).$$

1. There are fixed smooth extraction and reconstruction rules and fixed smooth coefficient functions $A^\mu(x,z),B(x,z)$ on an open state set $O$ giving a system
$$A^0(x,z)\partial_0z+\sum_i A^i(x,z)\partial_iz+B(x,z)=0,$$
with symmetric $A^\mu$ and positive definite $A^0$. Its metric equations are exactly the first-order reduction of the reduced Einstein equations of [[def-gr-harmonic-gauge-and-reduced-equations]], with stress $T=\mathcal T(g,\Psi)$. Every smooth physical solution of this fixed model in harmonic coordinates extracts to this same system. Any internal matter gauge is already fixed with its specified equations and complete data; otherwise state the corresponding internal gauge equivalence in the conclusion.
2. Complete data determine a smooth initial value $w=\mathcal I(h,K,d)$, including all auxiliary variables and their compatibility constraints. The initial metric jet displayed in step 1.1 and this value lie in $O$. The reduction propagates its auxiliary compatibility constraints, so the reconstructed fields solve $\mathcal E(g,\Psi)=0$ on the reduced solution, before imposing $H=0$ or the unreduced Einstein equations. The initial reconstruction induces exactly $d$ and the specified initial stress.
3. Whenever the reconstructed metric and fields satisfy those matter equations, their stress obeys $\nabla^a\mathcal T(g,\Psi)_{ab}=0$, independently of the unreduced Einstein equations. In particular this applies to the reduced solution furnished by clause 2. This is stronger than conservation asserted only after the full coupled equations have been proved.

These are concrete PDE, initialization and reconstruction hypotheses; they do not assume existence or geometric uniqueness. Require the constraints of [[thm-gr-constraint-equations-in-normal-frame]] for the stress determined by $(h,K,d)$:
$$S_h+(\operatorname{tr}_hK)^2-|K|_h^2=2\Lambda+2\kappa T_0(N,N),\qquad \operatorname{div}_hK-d\operatorname{tr}_hK=\kappa T_0(N,\cdot).$$

Then the data have a smooth time-oriented local development $(g,\Psi)$ on an open variable-width neighborhood of $\{0\}\times\Sigma$ in the literal manifold $\mathbb R\times\Sigma$, with induced data $(h,K,d)$, solving
$$G(g)+\Lambda g=\kappa\mathcal T(g,\Psi),\qquad\mathcal E(g,\Psi)=0.$$
After restriction to a smaller collar, $\Sigma$ lies in the interior of its intrinsic domain of dependence. The interior of that domain is a globally hyperbolic neighborhood with $\Sigma$ Cauchy. Any two developments of this same model and these complete data are related near the entire initial surface by a data-fixing time-orientation-preserving isometry matching all matter fields. There is no uniform noncompact time width or global-in-time conclusion.

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold, let
$\Sigma\subseteq M$ be a spacelike embedded hypersurface with induced metric
$h$, future unit normal field $n$ and second fundamental form
$K(V,W)=g(\nabla_Vn,W)$ ([[def-gr-spacelike-hypersurfaces-and-cauchy-sets]],
[[lem-gr-spacelike-hypersurface-normal-and-second-fundamental-form]]). Let
$s$ be a smooth function defined near $\Sigma$ with $s=0$ exactly on $\Sigma$
and $ds(n)=1$ (a normal time coordinate), and let $h_0$ be a smooth metric on a
product neighborhood of $\Sigma$ with $h_0|_{\Sigma}=h$ and
$\partial_sh_0=0$. Put $\bar g:=-ds^2+h_0$ as background metric. Define a smooth
metric germ $g_0$ on $\Sigma$ by the initial jet
$$g_{ij}=h_{ij},\qquad g_{00}=-1,\qquad g_{0i}=0,\qquad \partial_sg_{ij}=2K_{ij},\qquad \partial_sg_{0i}=0,\qquad \partial_sg_{00}=-2\operatorname{tr}_hK .$$
Then:

**(a)** $g_0$ is the germ of a smooth Lorentzian metric for which $\Sigma$ is
spacelike with induced metric $h$, future unit normal $n=\partial_s$ and second
fundamental form $K$;

**(b)** the harmonic-gauge vector of $(g_0,\bar g)$ vanishes on $\Sigma$:
$H^a|_\Sigma=0$.

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold, and let $\Sigma\subseteq M$ be a smooth spacelike embedded hypersurface with future unit normal $n$, induced Riemannian metric $h$ and second fundamental form $K(X,Y)=g(\nabla_Xn,Y)$ ([[def-gr-spacelike-hypersurfaces-and-cauchy-sets]], [[lem-gr-spacelike-hypersurface-normal-and-second-fundamental-form]]). Write $D$ for the Levi-Civita connection of $h$, $R^h$ for its curvature operator in the same operator convention as the ambient curvature, and $S_h$ for its scalar curvature. Explicitly distinguish the lowered tensor from the operator pairing by setting
$$\mathcal R^g(A,B,C,D):=g(R^g(C,D)B,A),\qquad \mathcal R^h(A,B,C,D):=h(R^h(C,D)B,A).$$
Thus $\mathcal R^g_{abcd}=R_{abcd}$ in [[def-gr-curvature-tensor-and-derived-tensors]]; in particular $g(R^g(X,Y)Z,W)=\mathcal R^g(W,Z,X,Y)$. Let $G$ be the Einstein tensor defined there. At every $p\in\Sigma$ and for all $X,Y,Z,W\in T_p\Sigma$:

**(a) Gauss equation.**
$$\mathcal R^g(X,Y,Z,W)=\mathcal R^h(X,Y,Z,W)+K(X,Z)K(Y,W)-K(X,W)K(Y,Z).$$
Equivalently, in operator order,
$$g(R^g(X,Y)Z,W)=h(R^h(X,Y)Z,W)+K(Y,Z)K(X,W)-K(X,Z)K(Y,W).$$

**(b) Codazzi equation.**
$$g(R^g(X,Y)Z,n)=(D_YK)(X,Z)-(D_XK)(Y,Z).$$

**(c) Normal projections.** Define $(\operatorname{div}_hK)(Y)=h^{ij}(D_{e_i}K)(e_j,Y)$, $\tau=\operatorname{tr}_hK=h^{ij}K_{ij}$ and $|K|_h^2=h^{ik}h^{jl}K_{ij}K_{kl}$. Then
$$G(n,n)=\tfrac12(S_h+\tau^2-|K|_h^2),\qquad G(n,Y)=(\operatorname{div}_hK)(Y)-D_Y\tau.$$

**(d) Constraint equations.** If the tensor equation $G+\Lambda g=\kappa T$ holds at $p$, for a smooth symmetric covariant $2$-tensor $T$ and real constants $\kappa,\Lambda$, then
$$S_h+\tau^2-|K|_h^2=2\Lambda+2\kappa T(n,n),\qquad (\operatorname{div}_hK)(Y)-D_Y\tau=\kappa T(n,Y).$$
With $\rho=T(n,n)$ and $j(Y)=-T(n,Y)$, the second equation is $(\operatorname{div}_hK)(Y)-D_Y\tau=-\kappa j(Y)$.

Let $(M,g,N)$ be an oriented time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]],
[[def-oriented-smooth-manifold-and-oriented-chart]]), let $c>0$ be a fixed
real constant, and let $\nabla$ be the metric-selected connection of $g$
([[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]],
[[thm-gr-nondegenerate-levi-civita-and-tensor-derivative]]).

**(a) Data.** A **scalar-field matter model** on $M$ is a triple
$(\varphi,V,K)$ consisting of

- a smooth function $\varphi:M\to\mathbb R$
  ([[def-c-r-and-smooth-maps-between-smooth-manifolds]], with target the
  standard one-dimensional smooth manifold $\mathbb R$);
- a smooth function $V:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$, the **potential**; and
- a real constant $K>0$, the **coupling**.

The physical reading of $K$ and of the units of $\varphi$ and $V$ is fixed by
the framework's matter postulate, not by this definition.

**(b) Scalar-action density and action differences.** For every smooth
function $\varphi'$ and every smooth Lorentzian metric $g'$ of signature
$(-,+,+,+)$ on $M$ define the **scalar-action density**

$$\ell(\varphi',g'):=-\frac{K}{c}\Bigl[\tfrac12\,g'^{ab}\,\partial_a\varphi'\, \partial_b\varphi'+V(\varphi')\Bigr]\mathrm{vol}_{g'}\in\Omega^4(M),$$

where $g'^{ab}$ are the inverse-metric components
([[def-gr-inverse-metric-and-musical-isomorphisms]]) and
$\mathrm{vol}_{g'}$ the metric volume form
([[def-gr-metric-volume-form-and-current-flux]]). For two pairs $(\varphi,g)$
and $(\varphi',g')$ with $\varphi'-\varphi$ and all components of $g'-g$
supported in a compact set, the difference $\ell(\varphi',g')-\ell(\varphi,g)$
is a compactly supported smooth $4$-form and the **action difference**

$$\Delta S:=\int_M\bigl[\ell(\varphi',g')-\ell(\varphi,g)\bigr]$$

is a real number ([[lem-finite-chart-localization-defines-choice-free-integration-and-compact-stokes]]),
the integral being independent of how the pair $(\varphi,g)$ is extended outside
the support. Only such differences are used; no integrality of the total
action on a noncompact $M$ is asserted.

**(c) Scalar equation and candidate stress-energy tensor.** The model's
**scalar equation of motion** is

$$\Box_g\varphi-V'(\varphi)=0,\qquad \Box_g\varphi:=\nabla^a\partial_a\varphi,$$

and the model's **candidate stress-energy tensor** is the smooth symmetric
covariant $2$-tensor field

$$T_{ab}:=K\Bigl[\partial_a\varphi\,\partial_b\varphi -g_{ab}\Bigl(\tfrac12\,\partial^c\varphi\,\partial_c\varphi+V(\varphi)\Bigr)\Bigr],$$

with $\partial^c\varphi\,\partial_c\varphi=g^{cd}\partial_c\varphi\,
\partial_d\varphi$ ([[def-gr-inverse-metric-and-musical-isomorphisms]],
[[def-gr-smooth-covariant-two-tensor-field]]). That this candidate is indeed
the Hilbert stress-energy tensor of the model, and that the scalar equation implies its conservation, are proved in
[[prop-gr-scalar-field-stress-energy-conservation]]; the definition itself
asserts neither proved property, and this item does not assert that any solution of
the scalar equation exists.

Let $M$ be a smooth four-manifold carrying a chart $(x^0=t,x^1,x^2,x^3)$ whose
domain $U$ contains the slice $\Sigma:=\{t=0\}$, let $\bar g$ be a smooth
background metric on $U$ with its Levi--Civita connection $\bar\nabla$, and let
$T$ be a smooth symmetric covariant $2$-tensor on $U$ together with the
background-covariant derivatives needed below (the matter field data). Suppose
smooth functions $g^0_{ab},g^1_{ab}$ on $\Sigma\cap U$ are given such that:

1. $g^0_{ab}$ are the components of a smooth Lorentzian metric on
   $\Sigma\cap U$ with $g^{00}_0<0$ and positive definite spatial block
   $(g_0^{ij})$;
2. $g^1_{ab}$ is symmetric and agrees on $\Sigma$ with the components of
   $\bar\nabla_0g_{ab}$ for some smooth extension $g$ of $g^0$ to $U$;
3. the harmonic-gauge condition $H^a=0$ holds on $\Sigma\cap U$ for the pair
   $(g,\bar g)$ ([[def-gr-harmonic-gauge-and-reduced-equations]]).

Then there is an open neighborhood $V\subseteq U$ of $\Sigma\cap U$ and a smooth
metric $g$ on $V$ with $g|_{\Sigma\cap U}=g^0$ and
$\bar\nabla_0g_{ab}|_{\Sigma\cap U}=g^1_{ab}$, solving the **reduced Einstein
equation** with the given background $\bar g$ and matter tensor $T$
([[def-gr-harmonic-gauge-and-reduced-equations]]) on $V$.

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a smooth time-oriented Lorentzian four-manifold, let
$\Sigma\subseteq M$ be a smooth spacelike hypersurface
([[def-gr-spacelike-hypersurfaces-and-cauchy-sets]]) with future unit normal
field $\mathfrak n$ and tangential frame $(e_i)$
([[lem-gr-spacelike-hypersurface-normal-and-second-fundamental-form]]), and let
$U$ be an open neighborhood of $\Sigma$ carrying a smooth background metric
$\bar g$ and a smooth symmetric tensor $T$ with $\nabla^aT_{ab}=0$ on $U$. Let
$H$ and $E$ be the gauge vector and Einstein residual of
[[def-gr-harmonic-gauge-and-reduced-equations]]. Suppose:

1. $(g,T)$ solves the reduced Einstein equation on $U$;
2. $H=0$ on $\Sigma$;
3. the constraint residuals vanish on $\Sigma$: $E(\mathfrak n,\mathfrak n)=0$
   and $E(\mathfrak n,e_i)=0$ for all $i$.

Then there is an open neighborhood $W\subseteq U$ of $\Sigma$ on which $H=0$ and
$E=0$; consequently $G_{ab}+\Lambda g_{ab}=\kappa T_{ab}$ on $W$, so $g$ solves
the Einstein equation with the prescribed matter tensor there.

Assume Countable Choice and Dependent Choice ([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-dependent-choice]]). Fix $\kappa>0$, $\Lambda\in\mathbb R$ and one covariant matter model: specified smooth fields $\Psi$, equations $\mathcal E(g,\Psi)=0$ and stress expression $\mathcal T(g,\Psi)$. Pullback by local diffeomorphisms commutes with these equations and stress expression. Let $\Sigma$ be a smooth three-manifold without boundary, with smooth Riemannian metric $h$, smooth symmetric tensor $K$ and complete smooth matter Cauchy data $d$. The sign convention is $K(V,W)=g(\nabla_Vn,W)$ for the future unit normal. Initial matter tensors involving normal directions are specified on the abstract bundle $\mathcal V=\mathbb RN\oplus T\Sigma$, with metric $g_0(aN+X,bN+Y)=-ab+h(X,Y)$, rather than on a pre-existing spacetime.

Require the following explicit reduction hypotheses on each sufficiently small relatively compact initial coordinate ball with labels $x^i$, flat comparison metric $\bar g=-(dx^0)^2+\sum_i(dx^i)^2$, and finite variables
$$z=(g_{ab},p_{ab}=\partial_0g_{ab},q_{abi}=\partial_ig_{ab},w).$$

1. There are fixed smooth extraction and reconstruction rules and fixed smooth coefficient functions $A^\mu(x,z),B(x,z)$ on an open state set $O$ giving a system
$$A^0(x,z)\partial_0z+\sum_i A^i(x,z)\partial_iz+B(x,z)=0,$$
with symmetric $A^\mu$ and positive definite $A^0$. Its metric equations are exactly the first-order reduction of the reduced Einstein equations of [[def-gr-harmonic-gauge-and-reduced-equations]], with stress $T=\mathcal T(g,\Psi)$. Every smooth physical solution of this fixed model in harmonic coordinates extracts to this same system. Any internal matter gauge is already fixed with its specified equations and complete data; otherwise state the corresponding internal gauge equivalence in the conclusion.
2. Complete data determine a smooth initial value $w=\mathcal I(h,K,d)$, including all auxiliary variables and their compatibility constraints. The initial metric jet displayed in step 1.1 and this value lie in $O$. The reduction propagates its auxiliary compatibility constraints, so the reconstructed fields solve $\mathcal E(g,\Psi)=0$ on the reduced solution, before imposing $H=0$ or the unreduced Einstein equations. The initial reconstruction induces exactly $d$ and the specified initial stress.
3. Whenever the reconstructed metric and fields satisfy those matter equations, their stress obeys $\nabla^a\mathcal T(g,\Psi)_{ab}=0$, independently of the unreduced Einstein equations. In particular this applies to the reduced solution furnished by clause 2. This is stronger than conservation asserted only after the full coupled equations have been proved.

These are concrete PDE, initialization and reconstruction hypotheses; they do not assume existence or geometric uniqueness. Require the constraints of [[thm-gr-constraint-equations-in-normal-frame]] for the stress determined by $(h,K,d)$:
$$S_h+(\operatorname{tr}_hK)^2-|K|_h^2=2\Lambda+2\kappa T_0(N,N),\qquad \operatorname{div}_hK-d\operatorname{tr}_hK=\kappa T_0(N,\cdot).$$

Then the data have a smooth time-oriented local development $(g,\Psi)$ on an open variable-width neighborhood of $\{0\}\times\Sigma$ in the literal manifold $\mathbb R\times\Sigma$, with induced data $(h,K,d)$, solving
$$G(g)+\Lambda g=\kappa\mathcal T(g,\Psi),\qquad\mathcal E(g,\Psi)=0.$$
After restriction to a smaller collar, $\Sigma$ lies in the interior of its intrinsic domain of dependence. The interior of that domain is a globally hyperbolic neighborhood with $\Sigma$ Cauchy. Any two developments of this same model and these complete data are related near the entire initial surface by a data-fixing time-orientation-preserving isometry matching all matter fields. There is no uniform noncompact time width or global-in-time conclusion.

Assume Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ ([[def-countable-choice]]). Fix $\kappa>0$, $\Lambda\in\mathbb R$ and one covariant matter model: specified smooth tensor fields $\Psi$, specified equations $\mathcal E(g,\Psi)=0$, and a specified stress expression $T=\mathcal T(g,\Psi)$. Covariance means pullback by a local diffeomorphism commutes with these equations and stress expression. Fix complete smooth matter Cauchy data $d$ for this model, a smooth Riemannian metric $h$ and smooth symmetric tensor $K$ on a smooth three-manifold $\Sigma$, with $K(V,W)=g(\nabla_Vn,W)$ for the future unit normal.

The following explicit harmonic-reduction hypothesis is required. On each relatively compact initial coordinate ball, with flat comparison metric $\bar g=-(dx^0)^2+\sum_i(dx^i)^2$, specify finite first-order variables
$$z=(g_{ab},p_{ab}=\partial_0g_{ab},q_{abi}=\partial_ig_{ab},w),$$
fixed smooth extraction and reconstruction rules for $w,\Psi$, and fixed smooth coefficient functions $A^\mu(x,z),B(x,z)$ on an open state set $O$, shared by both solutions, such that:

**(R1)** Every smooth solution of this same model written in harmonic coordinates has extracted variables satisfying
$$A^0(x,z)\partial_0z+\sum_iA^i(x,z)\partial_iz+B(x,z)=0,$$
where all $A^\mu$ are symmetric and $A^0$ is positive definite. Reconstruction recovers all matter fields and $T$ from $z$. Any internal matter gauge has already been fixed with its specified data and equations; otherwise the conclusion must include the appropriate internal gauge equivalence.
**(R2)** The initial value of $w$ is a specified smooth expression $\mathcal I(h,K,d)$ in the full data in this coordinate gauge. Thus $d$ determines every initial first-order variable, not merely initial stress tensor jets.
**(R3)** After shrinking a closed cylinder, both state ranges lie in one compact convex subset of $O$, coefficient first derivatives are bounded and $A^0\ge aI$ for some $a>0$.

These are PDE and extraction hypotheses, not an assumption of geometric uniqueness. Let $(M,g,\Psi,j)$ and $(M',g',\Psi',j')$ be two smooth time-oriented developments of this same model, solving the same Einstein equation $G+\Lambda g=\kappa\mathcal T(g,\Psi)$ and the same matter equations, whose spacelike embeddings induce $(h,K,d)$. Then near each initial point there is a smooth time-orientation-preserving isometry $\Phi$ with $\Phi\circ j=j'$ on the initial patch, $\Phi^*\Psi'=\Psi$ and consequently $\Phi^*T'=T$. Its germ along the initial patch is unique. These germs glue to one such isometry between open neighborhoods of the entire embedded initial surfaces. No uniform collar width or global-in-time assertion is made.

Assume Countable Choice and Dependent Choice ([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-dependent-choice]]). Fix $\Lambda\in\mathbb R$, $\kappa>0$ and one scalar model $(\varphi,V,K_\phi)$ of [[def-gr-scalar-field-matter-model]], with its fixed smooth potential and normalization. Let $\Sigma$ be a smooth three-manifold with smooth Riemannian metric $h$, symmetric tensor $K_2$ and complete scalar data $(\varphi_0,\pi_0)$. Suppose the constraints of [[thm-gr-constraint-equations-in-normal-frame]] hold for the scalar stress computed from these data, with $\pi_0$ the prescribed future-normal derivative. Then there is a smooth local Einstein-scalar development
$$G_{ab}+\Lambda g_{ab}=\kappa T_{ab},\qquad \Box_g\varphi-V'(\varphi)=0,$$
with induced geometric data $(h,K_2)$, $\varphi|_\Sigma=\varphi_0$ and $n(\varphi)|_\Sigma=\pi_0$. The neighborhood may have position-dependent time width. The initial surface is interior to its intrinsic domain of dependence; restricting to the interior Cauchy neighborhood gives a globally hyperbolic development. Every two developments of this same fixed model and complete data are related near the entire initial surface by a data-fixing time-orientation-preserving isometry matching $\varphi$. No potential positivity, mass sign, global existence or uniform noncompact slab is asserted ([[thm-gr-local-geometric-development]]).

Assume Countable Choice and Dependent Choice ([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-dependent-choice]]). Fix $\Lambda\in\mathbb R$, $\kappa>0$ and one smooth EOS $p=p(\epsilon)$ on an open interval $J$ with $\epsilon+p>0$ and $0<p'(\epsilon)<1$ ([[def-gr-perfect-fluid-matter-model]]). Let $\Sigma$ be a smooth three-manifold with smooth metric $h$, symmetric tensor $K_2$, density $\epsilon_0:\Sigma\to J$ and tangent field $v_0$ with $h(v_0,v_0)<1$. These specify the future unit initial velocity
$$U_0=W_0(N+v_0),\qquad W_0=(1-h(v_0,v_0))^{-1/2}$$
in $\mathcal V=\mathbb RN\oplus T\Sigma$, with metric $g_0(aN+X,bN+Y)=-ab+h(X,Y)$. Require the constraints of [[thm-gr-constraint-equations-in-normal-frame]] for
$$T_0=(\epsilon_0+p(\epsilon_0))U_0^{\flat_{g_0}}\otimes U_0^{\flat_{g_0}}+p(\epsilon_0)g_0.$$
Then a smooth time-oriented local development has metric $g$, density $\epsilon$ and future unit fluid velocity $u$ satisfying
$$G_{ab}+\Lambda g_{ab}=\kappa\left[(\epsilon+p)u_au_b+pg_{ab}\right],\qquad D\epsilon+(\epsilon+p)\vartheta=0,\qquad (\epsilon+p)a^b+\Pi^{ba}\partial_ap=0.$$
Here $D=\nabla_u$, $\vartheta=\nabla_a u^a$, $a=\nabla_u u$ and $\Pi^{ab}=g^{ab}+u^au^b$. Initial geometric data are $(h,K_2)$ and initial matter data are $(\epsilon_0,U_0)$ under $N\mapsto n$, $X\mapsto i_*X$. Arbitrary smooth subluminal tilt is allowed. The initial surface lies in the interior of its intrinsic domain of dependence; its interior Cauchy neighborhood is globally hyperbolic. Any two developments of this same EOS and complete data agree near the entire initial surface by a data-fixing future isometry matching density and velocity. The neighborhood may have position-dependent time width; shocks, vacuum boundaries and vanishing sound speed are outside this strict interior-fluid statement ([[thm-gr-local-geometric-development]]).

Assume Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ ([[def-countable-choice]]) and Dependent Choice ([[def-dependent-choice]]). Fix constants $c>0$, $\kappa>0$ and $\Lambda\in\mathbb R$. Let $\Sigma$ be a smooth three-manifold with smooth Riemannian metric $h$, smooth symmetric tensor $K$ and a smooth mass-normalized density $\rho_0\ge0$. Specify initial velocity as a smooth section $U_0$ of $\mathcal V=\mathbb RN\oplus T\Sigma$, with the bundle metric $g_0(aN+X,bN+Y)=-ab+h(X,Y)$, satisfying $g_0(U_0,U_0)=-1$ and positive $N$ coefficient. Thus the velocity need not be normal and does not presuppose a spacetime development. Put $\varepsilon_0=\rho_0c^2$ and require the constraints of [[thm-gr-constraint-equations-in-normal-frame]] for $T_0=\varepsilon_0U_0^{\flat_{g_0}}\otimes U_0^{\flat_{g_0}}$. On $\{\rho_0>0\}$ this is exactly the dust supplier with density parameter $\varepsilon_0$, rather than $\rho_0$ ([[def-gr-dust-matter-model]]); zero regions have independently prescribed velocity.

Then there is a smooth local development: a smooth time-oriented Lorentzian metric $g$, density $\rho\ge0$ and future unit timelike field $u$ near an embedded copy of $\Sigma$, solving
$$G_{ab}+\Lambda g_{ab}=\kappa\rho c^2u_au_b,\qquad \nabla_uu=0,\qquad u(\rho)+\rho\nabla\!\cdot u=0.$$
The induced geometric and matter data are $(h,K,\rho_0,U_0)$, with $\mathcal V$ identified by $aN+X\mapsto an+i_*X$ using the future unit normal $n$. The initial surface lies in the interior of its domain of dependence; restriction to its Cauchy neighborhood gives a local Cauchy development. Every two such developments agree near $\Sigma$ by a data-fixing time-orientation-preserving isometry matching $\rho,u$. No division by density is used, so smooth empty regions are admitted. The neighborhood may have position-dependent time width; no uniform noncompact slab or continuation past flow crossings is asserted.

derivations.claim: (Vacuum branch.) There are no matter variables and $T=0$, so matter reconstruction and conservation on the reduced solution are automatic. The metric wave block and complete harmonic jet of [L2] give its reduction and initialization contract; the displayed vacuum constraints give zero initial normal residuals. Applying the vacuum instance of [L2] yields the full solution, intrinsic Cauchy neighborhood and fixed-data future isometry uniqueness, with [L1] giving the reduced-to-full recovery.

(Scalar and strict-fluid branches.) Their branch theorems in [L3] verify the complete fixed-model contract, including all initial first-order variables, auxiliary recovery and conservation before Einstein recovery. Apply these concrete theorems to obtain exactly the stated developments and complete-data uniqueness. Local initial values lie in compact admissible state neighborhoods; smooth cutoff extensions have finite $H^s$ norm for each finite integer $s\ge5$, and smooth persistence supplies exactly the smooth branch. No optimal finite-regularity threshold is asserted.

(Geodesic dust branch.) Put $\rho_0:=\varepsilon_0/c^2$ and apply [[thm-gr-dust-local-evolution]] to this mass-normalized density and the prescribed $U_0$. Its initial tensor is $\rho_0c^2U_0^\flat\otimes U_0^\flat=\varepsilon_0U_0^\flat\otimes U_0^\flat$, so its constraints are exactly the present constraints. It gives an independent smooth frame-reduction development with its common-flow uniqueness and variable-width patching, without invoking the abstract harmonic matter hypothesis for dust. Recover $\varepsilon=c^2\rho$; constant scaling preserves continuity, geodesic velocity, nonnegativity, the empty-region branch and the stress tensor. Its causal and isometry conclusions are therefore precisely the stated ones.

boundaries.evidence: Vacuum in Statement has no matter variables and T=0; step 1.1 discharges reconstruction and conservation automatically while still supplying the full metric data.
Step 2.1 converts epsilon0=0 to rho0=0 by c²>0 and retains prescribed dust velocity; scalar zero fields retain their fixed potential equations.
Statement selects one of four named sectors, not a sum or arbitrary family of sectors; step 1.2 treats the single scalar and strict fluid branches through their own suppliers.
The sector conditions in Statement exclude fluid epsilon+p=0 or pprime=0, while admitting nonnegative dust density through step 2.1 without a density division.
Step 1.2 provides smooth high-regularity developments locally and claims no optimal finite-regularity threshold; step 2.1 retains the dust variable-width causal conclusion.
Statement explicitly carries CC/DC through the sector theorems; step 2.1 calls the independent dust route rather than selecting a nonexistent harmonic dust reduction.

citations.quote:
Adopt as the field law of the direct-equation presentation of the classical
gravitational framework, for models satisfying
[[post-gr-spacetime-and-classical-domain]] and
[[post-gr-field-and-matter-assumptions]], the following statement.

**(i) The equation.** Let $(M,g,N)$ be the model's smooth time-oriented
Lorentzian four-manifold with metric-selected connection $\nabla$
([[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]],
[[thm-gr-nondegenerate-levi-civita-and-tensor-derivative]]) and let
$G_{ab}=\operatorname{Ric}_{ab}-\tfrac12Sg_{ab}$ be the Einstein tensor of that
connection ([[def-gr-curvature-tensor-and-derived-tensors]]). Let
$T$ be the model's stress-energy tensor field on its matter domain
$U\subseteq M$ ([[def-gr-stress-energy-tensor-field]]) and let
$\Lambda\in\mathbb R$ be a constant parameter with dimension
$\mathrm m^{-2}$ and $G_N>0$, $c>0$ the constants of
[[def-gr-si-unit-and-coordinate-conventions]]. Adopt

$$G_{ab}+\Lambda g_{ab}=\frac{8\pi G_N}{c^4}\,T_{ab}\qquad\text{on }U$$

as the field law of the model. Writing
$\kappa:=8\pi G_N/c^4$ and $T_{ab}=g_{ac}g_{bd}T^{cd}$ for the lowered tensor,
the equation reads $G_{ab}+\Lambda g_{ab}=\kappa T_{ab}$

**(ii) Matter content.** The equation constrains the metric and the matter of
the model jointly. A model specifies its matter sector as in
[[post-gr-field-and-matter-assumptions]]: a scalar-field model with its action
and stress-energy tensor ([[def-gr-scalar-field-matter-model]]), or a dust or perfect-fluid model with prescribed
stress-energy tensor and matter equations. The consistency condition that
every solution must satisfy, $\nabla^aT_{ab}=0$, is not adopted separately; it
is a consequence of the equation and of the contracted second Bianchi identity
and is derived in [[pthm-gr-einstein-consistency-and-energy-conditions]].

**(iii) Alternative presentation.** The action formulation of the same field
law is adopted separately in [[post-gr-classical-gravitational-action]]. A
model adopts exactly one of the two presentations. They are alternative
presentations of one classical field law: the action-to-equation theorem of
this page identifies the equation obtained from stationarity of the total
action with the equation displayed in clause (i), and the direct presentation
is not an additional premise of an action-formulated model.

**(iv) Status and scope.** The equation is an adopted law of the model. It is
not derived from mathematical symmetry, from the equivalence principle, or
from observation; covariance and correspondence arguments motivate but do not
prove it. No numerical value of $c$, $G_N$ or $\Lambda$ is asserted, and no
claim is made that any particular metric or matter configuration solves the
equation or describes nature. The smooth-branch exclusions of
[[post-gr-spacetime-and-classical-domain]] and
[[post-gr-field-and-matter-assumptions]] apply: distributional or
lower-dimensional sources, boundaries with junction conditions, and non-smooth
fields are outside this formulation. Comparisons of a model's predictions with
data test the combined model — geometry, matter content and this law — and
agreement is evidence about that combination, not a proof of the postulate.

Adopt as physical assumptions of the classical gravitational framework the
following statements.

**(i) Spacetime model.** The spacetime of a model of the framework is a
time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold $(M,g,N)$ as in
[[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]: a smooth four-manifold $M$ without
boundary, a Lorentzian metric $g$ of signature $(-,+,+,+)$ on $M$
([[def-smooth-manifold]]), and a time orientation $N$. Its points represent
idealized physical events; the vector $N$ fixes which causal directions are
future-directed; and the causal classification of tangent vectors along any
worldline is the classification of the Lorentz vector spaces $(T_pM,g_p)$
together with the future/past convention of the time orientation. The metric
$g$ is the gravitational field of the model: it is the object that the field
law of the framework constrains, and its curvature is the model's
representation of gravity. The rules by which ideal clocks, test bodies and
light rays couple to $g$ are adopted separately as physical assumptions of the
framework.

**(ii) Classical domain.** Geometry and matter are treated as classical
continuum fields: the model describes macroscopic configurations of matter and
a classical metric, with no quantum description of either. The framework makes
no claim that a real spacetime is exactly such a manifold, that matter is
exactly a classical continuum, or that the smooth description applies to
arbitrarily small scales or arbitrarily strong fields; those are domain
limitations of the model family, not consequences of it.

**(iii) Unity of the model.** A model of the framework is specified by its
geometry $(M,g,N)$ together with its matter content and the field law adopted
for it; the geometry alone selects no matter configuration and no dynamics
(the matter assumptions are
adopted separately, in the companion postulate on matter content). Physical
parameters enter through
the unit conventions of [[def-gr-si-unit-and-coordinate-conventions]]; no
numerical value of a constant is asserted here.

**(iv) Smooth-branch restriction.** The fields of a model are defined on an
open domain of $M$; the metric is $C^\infty$ on all of $M$ and $M$ has no
boundary. Configurations in which a field fails to be smooth on a nonempty open
set, in which matter is concentrated on a lower-dimensional set in a way that
produces a distributional stress-energy tensor, or in which $M$ carries a
boundary, are outside the stated smooth domain of the framework and require
mathematics not supplied by these postulates.

**(v) Status.** These are adopted assumptions. They are not derived from the
mathematics of manifolds, from any symmetry principle, or from experiment; the
equivalence principle and covariance arguments motivate but do not prove them.
Testing the framework means comparing predictions computed from a fully
specified model — geometry, matter content and field law — with observations,
and agreement is evidence about the model, not a proof of these postulates.

Adopt as physical assumptions of the classical gravitational framework, in
addition to [[post-gr-spacetime-and-classical-domain]], the following statements
about the matter content of a model.

**(i) Matter content is model input.** A model of the framework specifies its
nongravitational fields or matter and their explicit equations of motion and
couplings. The geometric data $(M,g,N)$ of
[[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]] and covariance of the model's equations
under relabelling of events do not select those fields, equations or couplings:
different matter specifications over the same geometry are different models of
the framework, and no dynamical selection principle is asserted.

**(ii) Smooth matter and its stress-energy tensor.** The matter of a model on
its matter domain is represented by smooth fields on an open domain
$U\subseteq M$, and the model's stress-energy tensor is the smooth symmetric
covariant $2$-tensor field $T$ on $U$ of
[[def-gr-stress-energy-tensor-field]], with the unit reading recorded there.
The relation of $T$ to the matter fields is part of the model: a model derived
from an action defines $T$ as the Hilbert stress-energy tensor of that action,
while a model that prescribes $T$ directly is a separate source model.

**(iii) Consistency with the field law.** Where a model prescribes $T$
independently of matter fields, the prescription is admissible only if it meets
the consistency conditions imposed by the gravitational field law adopted for
the model, stated where that law is stated; in the action formulation the
matter equations, their coupling to the metric, and the on-shell conservation
of $T$ are derived within the model rather than assumed. Conservation is an
on-shell statement about a specified model and is not automatic for an
arbitrary smooth symmetric $T$.

**(iv) Energy conditions are optional additional assumptions.** A model may
adopt any of the pointwise inequalities of [[def-gr-energy-conditions]] as
further assumptions on its stress-energy tensor. None of them is a consequence
of the preceding clauses, of the field law, or of the symmetry of $T$; each
model records which conditions, if any, it adopts, and a model that adopts none
is not thereby excluded.

**(v) Scope and exclusions.** Idealizations such as unmodeled self-force,
finite-size and tidal corrections, dispersion, dissipation, and quantum effects
are outside the framework unless the model's explicit equations include them;
matter concentrated in a distributional or lower-dimensional source, and
matter configurations whose fields fail to be smooth on the model domain, are
outside the stated smooth branch and require additional mathematics. The
adoption of a matter model is not a claim that it describes nature.

Let $(M,g,N)$ be an oriented time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]],
[[def-oriented-smooth-manifold-and-oriented-chart]]), let $c>0$ be a fixed
real constant, and let $\nabla$ be the metric-selected connection of $g$
([[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]],
[[thm-gr-nondegenerate-levi-civita-and-tensor-derivative]]).

**(a) Data.** A **scalar-field matter model** on $M$ is a triple
$(\varphi,V,K)$ consisting of

- a smooth function $\varphi:M\to\mathbb R$
  ([[def-c-r-and-smooth-maps-between-smooth-manifolds]], with target the
  standard one-dimensional smooth manifold $\mathbb R$);
- a smooth function $V:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$, the **potential**; and
- a real constant $K>0$, the **coupling**.

The physical reading of $K$ and of the units of $\varphi$ and $V$ is fixed by
the framework's matter postulate, not by this definition.

**(b) Scalar-action density and action differences.** For every smooth
function $\varphi'$ and every smooth Lorentzian metric $g'$ of signature
$(-,+,+,+)$ on $M$ define the **scalar-action density**

$$\ell(\varphi',g'):=-\frac{K}{c}\Bigl[\tfrac12\,g'^{ab}\,\partial_a\varphi'\, \partial_b\varphi'+V(\varphi')\Bigr]\mathrm{vol}_{g'}\in\Omega^4(M),$$

where $g'^{ab}$ are the inverse-metric components
([[def-gr-inverse-metric-and-musical-isomorphisms]]) and
$\mathrm{vol}_{g'}$ the metric volume form
([[def-gr-metric-volume-form-and-current-flux]]). For two pairs $(\varphi,g)$
and $(\varphi',g')$ with $\varphi'-\varphi$ and all components of $g'-g$
supported in a compact set, the difference $\ell(\varphi',g')-\ell(\varphi,g)$
is a compactly supported smooth $4$-form and the **action difference**

$$\Delta S:=\int_M\bigl[\ell(\varphi',g')-\ell(\varphi,g)\bigr]$$

is a real number ([[lem-finite-chart-localization-defines-choice-free-integration-and-compact-stokes]]),
the integral being independent of how the pair $(\varphi,g)$ is extended outside
the support. Only such differences are used; no integrality of the total
action on a noncompact $M$ is asserted.

**(c) Scalar equation and candidate stress-energy tensor.** The model's
**scalar equation of motion** is

$$\Box_g\varphi-V'(\varphi)=0,\qquad \Box_g\varphi:=\nabla^a\partial_a\varphi,$$

and the model's **candidate stress-energy tensor** is the smooth symmetric
covariant $2$-tensor field

$$T_{ab}:=K\Bigl[\partial_a\varphi\,\partial_b\varphi -g_{ab}\Bigl(\tfrac12\,\partial^c\varphi\,\partial_c\varphi+V(\varphi)\Bigr)\Bigr],$$

with $\partial^c\varphi\,\partial_c\varphi=g^{cd}\partial_c\varphi\,
\partial_d\varphi$ ([[def-gr-inverse-metric-and-musical-isomorphisms]],
[[def-gr-smooth-covariant-two-tensor-field]]). That this candidate is indeed
the Hilbert stress-energy tensor of the model, and that the scalar equation implies its conservation, are proved in
[[prop-gr-scalar-field-stress-energy-conservation]]; the definition itself
asserts neither proved property, and this item does not assert that any solution of
the scalar equation exists.

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold with
metric-selected connection $\nabla$ ([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]],
[[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]],
[[thm-gr-nondegenerate-levi-civita-and-tensor-derivative]]) and let
$U\subseteq M$ be a nonempty open matter domain
([[prop-an-open-subset-of-a-smooth-manifold-has-a-canonical-restricted-smooth-structure]]).

**(a) Data.** A **perfect-fluid model** on $U$ is a triple $(\varepsilon,p,n)$
consisting of two smooth functions $\varepsilon,p:U\to\mathbb R$, the **rest
energy density** and the **pressure**, and a smooth future-directed unit
timelike vector field $n$ on $U$ with $g_p(n_p,n_p)=-1$ and
$g_p(n_p,N_p)<0$ at every $p$ ([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]],
[[def-c-r-and-smooth-maps-between-smooth-manifolds]]). No positivity of
$\varepsilon$ or of $p$ is required or implied. A model may carry the
additional data of an **equation of state**: a function
$P:D_P\to\mathbb R$ on a subset $D_P\subseteq\mathbb R$ with
$\varepsilon(U)\subseteq D_P$, together with the relation $p=P(\varepsilon)$;
the relation is a further assumption and is not part of the basic triple.

**(b) Stress-energy tensor and derived fields.** The model's
**stress-energy tensor** is

$$T^{ab}:=(\varepsilon+p)n^an^b+p\,g^{ab},$$

a smooth symmetric contravariant $2$-tensor field ([[def-gr-smooth-covariant-two-tensor-field]],
[[def-gr-inverse-metric-and-musical-isomorphisms]]). The **comoving
derivative**, **expansion** and **acceleration** of $n$ are

$$D f:=n^a\partial_af\quad(f\in C^\infty(U)),\qquad \vartheta:=\nabla_an^a,\qquad a^b:=n^a\nabla_an^b ,$$

and the **rest-space projection** is the smooth tensor field

$$h^{ab}:=g^{ab}+n^an^b .$$

The physical reading of $\varepsilon$ and $p$ as a rest-frame energy density
and pressure, and their units, are fixed by the framework's matter postulate,
not by this definition.

**(c) Fluid equations.** The **perfect-fluid equations** on $U$ are

$$D\varepsilon+(\varepsilon+p)\vartheta=0,\qquad (\varepsilon+p)a^b+h^{ba}\partial_ap=0 .$$

That the stress-energy tensor is divergence-free if and only if these two
equations hold is proved in
[[prop-gr-dust-and-perfect-fluid-conservation-equations]]; the definition
asserts neither divergence-freedom nor the equations.

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold with
metric-selected connection $\nabla$ ([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]],
[[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]],
[[thm-gr-nondegenerate-levi-civita-and-tensor-derivative]]) and let
$U\subseteq M$ be a nonempty open subset, the **matter domain**, carrying its
restricted smooth structure
([[prop-an-open-subset-of-a-smooth-manifold-has-a-canonical-restricted-smooth-structure]]).

**(a) Data.** A **dust model** on $U$ is a pair $(\rho,u)$ consisting of

- a smooth function $\rho:U\to\mathbb R$ with $\rho(p)>0$ for every $p\in U$,
  the **rest density**; and
- a smooth future-directed unit timelike vector field $u$ on $U$
  ([[def-c-r-and-smooth-maps-between-smooth-manifolds]] with target $TM$
  described through the tangent bundle; concretely, $u$ is a smooth vector
  field on $U$ with $g_p(u_p,u_p)=-1$ and $g_p(u_p,N_p)<0$ at every $p$,
  [[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]).

The physical reading of $\rho$ as a rest-mass density in a unit system, and of
$u$ as the four-velocity congruence of the matter, is fixed by the framework's
matter postulate, not by this definition.

**(b) Stress-energy tensor.** The model's **stress-energy tensor** is the
smooth symmetric covariant $2$-tensor field

$$T^{ab}:=\rho\,u^au^b\qquad\text{equivalently}\qquad T_{ab}=\rho\,u_au_b,$$

with $u_a=g_{ac}u^c$ ([[def-gr-inverse-metric-and-musical-isomorphisms]],
[[def-gr-smooth-covariant-two-tensor-field]]); the two expressions correspond
under raising both indices, by $g^{ac}g^{bd}T_{cd}=T^{ab}$.

**(c) Dust system.** The **dust system** on $U$ is the pair of equations

$$\nabla_a(\rho\,u^a)=0,\qquad u^a\nabla_au^b=0 .$$

The first is a continuity equation for the density current $\rho u$; the
second says that the integral curves of $u$ are geodesics in the parameter that
makes $u$ their unit tangent, i.e. that the dust particles are in free fall
([[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]],
[[thm-gr-nondegenerate-levi-civita-and-tensor-derivative]]).

Let $\Lambda\in\mathbb R$, $\kappa>0$ and $c>0$ be constants, let $\Sigma$ be a smooth
three-manifold with smooth Riemannian metric $h$ and symmetric $2$-tensor $K$,
and suppose smooth matter initial data and a matter sector are given in one of
the following four branches, with the constraint equations of
[[thm-gr-constraint-equations-in-normal-frame]] satisfied:

1. **vacuum with cosmological constant:** no matter fields; the constraints
   read $S_h+(\operatorname{tr}_hK)^2-|K|^2_h=2\Lambda$ and
   $\operatorname{div}_hK-d\operatorname{tr}_hK=0$;
2. **scalar field:** a model $(\varphi,V,K_\phi)$ as in

4. **geodesic dust:** an energy-coefficient density $\varepsilon_0\ge0$
   with prescribed smooth future unit velocity $U_0$, as a section of
   $\mathbb RN\oplus T\Sigma$ with metric $-ab+h(X,Y)$.
   On positive-density regions this is the model $(\varepsilon,u)$ of
   [[def-gr-dust-matter-model]]; through zero-density regions its smooth
   unit velocity is separately prescribed and required to remain geodesic.
